FIRST REVIEW!.....and maybe the only one?
First most I want to say this game has ALOT of potenial to be something great, especially for people who like RTS games and for peolple who like me like to design there own machines to use in battle however I have to wonder wiether this game is a quick cashgrab or If the devloper doesn't have any experience with making games in this genre? I will give my honest opionon and I want people to understand am not going to praise or bash it for not reason.
Onto the review, on the surface this game looks really interesting with it's concept of armored vechicle designing and indeed it is a good concept but it poorly done but I will get to that in a bit. The game uses a Risk like map however do not be fooled, this game is NOT RISK in any real way besides moving units to an area or city and capturing it. The board to me is more like Civilization without any of the diplomacy. The purpose of this game is to design the best vehicle for the job along with putting that unit in a battalion that will have it work well with. Battalions are easy to create and in a way are similar to Hearts of Iron III but is far worse :/. you Automatically ALWAYS have one unit of Tanks and Infantry in a battalion so you can't have an all infantry or tank battalion which is a bit akyward. You can choose what tanks you want in the battalion BUT you can only have one TYPE of Tank in the battalion so you can't have medium tanks you designed in a battalion with Heavy tanks you designed which is surprising. For infantry you can put in a infantry unit with a present you can make so you can make an entire Infantry unit comprised of riflemen, machinegunmen, anti-armor(RPG's) etc and can do what you want which is nice but is useless, I will explain shortly.
The most fun part of this game is the designing part and it is FUN!....well to a certain extent until you realize that it's pointless unforuntely. When designing a tank, you pick the engine, suspension, the main gun and it's armor in the front, side and behind essentially. One gripe I have is that you can't actually choose how it looks and is randomly generated on the parts you picked which estically goes from Pre-WWI looking wheeled armored behicles to whacky WWI Tank models something you see in Warhammer 40,000K but is far less cook and kinda corny looking. There isn't any interperiod or WWII looking designs in the game, want to make a Tiger II with a 100mm cannon? your ♥♥♥♥ out of luck my friend lol
To unlock better equipment, you need to research these components which take time usually from 2 months to 6 months ingame. This is probably the only part of the game that is perfectly fine for the most part beacuse Research in general in this game is almost completely pointless. Besides researching equipment for Tanks, you also can research Infantry weapons as well but since Infantry are literally powerless agianst Tanks and the AI only uses Tanks, there's no point at all. Besides that you can also research how fast research is done with upgrading equipment or waiting for your new sweet protoype tank to be done, You can also research how fast infantry are trained but is pointless since the AI only uses Tanks, you can also research the flexiability of Production which means how fast your factories can change it's line from making thing to another which is quite handy if your getting beaten to haw well your design is made on the line and production in general. Now the last two are pointless as well beacuse no matter how much you invest in increasing the efficiency of production, you always produce the same amount of vehicles no matter what every month and improving how well your tanks or armored cars are made in your factories are so minor that it doesn't mattter.
Now for the most crappy part of the game.....urrgghh! Warefare is just broken in this game, you start out on the board automatically at war with other nations and there's dipomacy whatsover so no peace treaties, no trading of tech or alliances, hell you can't start the game as a team deathmatch, It's YOU agianst the world and let me tell you, all the AI's will team up on your and steam roll...why you ask? Well Tank warefare is broken all to hell in everyway possible, no matter what design you make and IF you are able to deploy them in decent numbers, you will 9 times out of 10 get steam rollled by the enemy AI. At the beginning of the game, they automatically have better armored vehicles then you and usually even if you research enough to make a true sequal from the T-1 Rabbit, the AI will either have a far better vechicle then you already or if you managed to hold your own somehow, the AI will constantly send Tank at your front until you can't replace the tanks and infantry you lost since you NEVER make enough tanks for mass production per month and the more cities you lose, your production capabilities will diminish greatly to the point you won't be able to produce anything really at all, hell even the starter unit can't be produced in great number and if you wan't, it's worthless, sure you can throw on a slightly better gun but it won't help. No matter what you make and deploy, it will get destroyed, I had an ENTIRE battalion(100) of Maus tanks essentially in my last game solely for defense and somehow the Ai was able to use one battalion with only tanks to take it out so either they have the same quality tanks or something far better since there is no Air power or support power. There's also no rea recon so you never know what the AI has deployed so you can't prepare.
Am sure Am forgetting something on here but in this state, I can't recommend this game at all honestly until it's improved. There's a great foundation for a fun ♥♥♥ game but that's all it is and it's too shallow and cheap, hell there's not even a torturial to teach how to play :/

Apocalypse Now under the guise of a generic, brown cover shooter. A really great story, but mediocre gameplay overall.
7/10

Now this is a game that has impact on you. Throughout the chapters you come to feel what means to be human, to make mistakes and to learn about the weight of your actions. Three main characters (though only one is playable, but you get to like all of them), each one with their own personality and showing different reactions to the situations they come across and the things they have to do and choose to do. Yes, this game is a master at making you think if you ever had a choice, if you could have made the outcome different. You'll most likely get yourself wondering what you would have done or how you would have felt in their places.
Storywise this game could hardly get any better. It's epic, it's moving, it's personal.
Gameplay could see some improvements, movement sometimes is your worst foe, but it's not bad, many guns, squad commands, smooth aim, some strategy, some possibilities and the most useful grenades i've ever thrown (the enemies fully agree with this, believe me).
It has a decent amount of replay value, if you want to see the different paths you can take, make different choices and see all the possible outcomes. You can also increase the game difficulty and replay it, things can get very challenging.
So, in a nutshell, this game is a gem, completely worth playing, an amazing experience that still doesn't receive all the attention it deserves. I highly recommend this one.

Update: 11/30/2017
I really like this game, it's not a bad survival type of game and it functions pretty well.
But this game probably has the most toxic player base I've ever encountered. Now of course, in PvP, you're going to die here and there, that is a given. But between hate mongering and people who act to almost cruel degrees, it makes this game extremely difficult to enjoy.
Example: Get shot by player, I'm annoyed and ask if he can at least not kill me. He picks me up, gives me back the resources he looted off me and says he's "sorry." No more than a couple seconds later, he puts an arrow through my head and laughs. Another game where people calling themselves "pirates" somehow changed all my door locks in less than one minute, which only increases my loathing for PvP gameplay. Along with this, one thing I've noticed, a high amount of people in this game act rather immature and do everything ranging from idle threats, acting profane and being plain rude. Most of all, though I do understand it, almost all players are kill on sight, no questions asked; even when your fresh off the beach, nude and armed only with a torch and a rock while they're sporting an assault rifle.
But of course, there are plenty of people who can be very friendly. Though most are located within the PvE servers and seem rare to find in the PvP, aside from people who run hotels. But most friendly people will express a healthy cautiousness of other players they don't know, KoS doesn't apply to that group.
As for the game itself. The graphics look pretty good. Nothing mind blowing, but things like lighting and shadows are fairly well don and textures remain consistant thoughout. Plenty of graphics options to get things tuned to your likeing, which is always a plus. Though some textures or actions look a little weird here and there, the game is still receiving updates, so this is a plus as well.
Gameplay feels pretty solid. Though a bit grindy depending on what your doing or what server your in. But there's a great range of servers to choose from. Everything from battle royals, high resource count servers which create a battle that spans the island, roleplay and PvE servers and a few others with their own additions in the modded servers.
All in all, I really like this game, but a majority of the player base are incredibly immature and it appears that majority are in their teens. The only other game I have to compare the player base too is GTA Online. People just being rude and thinking ruining others experiences are fun, when their just out trolling. So honestly, my recommendation is a soft yes, but a yes no less. But this game isn't for people who are tempermental.

I write this as a huge fan of all things RPG. Below is a bullet point of good vs bad.
Good:
•	Atmosphere
•	Ambient sounds
•	Music
•	Voice acting
•	Graphic
Bad:
•	Almost everything else.
I have played a ton of RPGs in my 40 years, I love the immersion the development of characters and story above all else. This game just drops the ball in being fun and making you care. Most others say it is a visual interactive novel and that is pretty spot on. Game play is a lot of reading of text and if you get into combat, you poor soul, you are in for defeat. The combat is overly tough as it seems like a punishment for not playing the game the way the writers wanted it.
Took me 6 tries to win the first encounter, I finally won by not getting into the fight. As with all the fights, you can avoid them, IF you made a combat useless face character. If you wanted to make a hulk smash guy, as the game lets you, you will uninstall this game quickly.
Overall I was highly disappointed when they started changing things quickly after the Kickstarter ended. From what was pitched to what we got is not even remotely the same. I have tried to like this game, I have played a bit and watched videos and game play, I just do not care to sit through a visual controlled novel. RPGs are so many things; this is very much not a RPG. Sure, you play a role and it is a game but beyond that you are not in control. You set forth on a very limited path and you are forced to experience the story as the writers wrote it, it is not for you to pick and choose.

Mad Max is a fun, open world, post apolocyptic game that I personally enjoy picking up and playing for a hour or two at a time.  Though it does have a few glaring issues that cannot be over looked.
Long and skinny of it, I'll give it a 8 out of 10.
Pros:
-Graphics, sound and music are well done.  All wrapped together, they compliment each other while adding a nice immersive feel to the game.  Getting caught in the middle of a storm is nerve wracking at times if you don't get to a safe spot to hide from the storm, and when you do, the sound of the wind howling around you, along with the explosive thunder; will make you're heartbeat pick up.  If you are wearing headphones, you may want to take them off or quickly lower the volume, as it gets really loud as one would expect being stuck in a storm of this nature.
-Combat system is fun, and will make you feel like a bad♥♥♥♥♥after clearing out a mob with your bare hands.  Though, it is very similar (if not identical) to Batman Arkham Knights combat system.
-Visually the game is appealing, and really sets the apocalyptic scene.  Though it differently wont be setting any standards, it's on par with most other games.
Cons:
-The UI and menu system....oh God.  This game is NOT friendly to keyboard and mouse users.  The menu and controls are awkward at best, and trying to get to the basic main menu to be able to quit or change settings, forces you to hit escape to open the menu, then select the main menu button to access the basic main functions.  Also, keybinding is damn near non-existent.  I have a personal keyboard layout that I like for game playing, and there is no way to adjust the keybindings to do so.  Heck, one cannot even change the keybinding of opening the map.  It's set to Tab, and you cannot change it.  Granted, this is not a absolute game breaker, but come on, how can you put a AAA game out for PC and not recognize that the individual player would want customize their own keybindings?
-While there are many things to go do in the game world, after a while, it tends to get repetitive.  Quite a few times I've found myself not even wanting to take on a mission, and just driving around hunting for roaming caravans, thirsty wanderers, and any random cars.   This doesn't mean that I don't play the quests, for I do; it's just kinda dull after a while of doing the same/similar style mission that you've already done a hour ago, over and over again.
All in all, would I recommend this game to a gamer?  Yes, when it's on sale.  Granted, I still pick this game up here and there and play it for a hour or two, especially when I'm having a rough day and I just want to run down bandits with my mighty car of post-apocalyptic bad-assery, and lay waste to a bandit camp.  I had grabbed this game when it was on sale for $15, and I'll have to say, ~20hrs of fun w/ it, I've gotten my money's worth out of it.  Just, if you do pick it up, make sure you've got a 360 controller, or get ready for a hour or two of cursing the game while you keep hitting the wrong buttons.

is a hilarious text adventure that puts you into Hamlet's shoes, makes him a video game protagonist... and then Hamlet applies REASON. It's not very effective...
The game goes all out, satirizing and heckling every step Hamlet made, revelling in just how easy it would have been to avoid most of the play's tragedies. The result is often comedy gold—it made me laugh aloud several times (which is a lot in our informationally-overloaded-yet-desensitized-to-everything times). Hamlet's emo teen logic in the game is just too amusing, and somehow the whole thing also manages to have a touching moment or two.
You can also play as Ophelia and Hamlet Sr., but I'd say that their stories, as well as the bits from Hamlet's that stray from the original completely, are less compelling than the parody bits—although still fun and good interactive prose.
The whole thing is broken into easily digestible bits that allow for reasonably simple backtracking and exploring alternative branches. And if you have a favourite comic artist of international renown, chances are that an artwork of theirs is featured in the game—although I have to point out that the artworks, unlocked by reaching various endings, are not present in the game itself, but rather serve as non-useful rewards, so if you were hoping to see a ton of cool art, you're kinda out of luck. (Except for Kate Beaton's art that's present in the game and obviously instantly makes it cooler.)
Some people criticize
for the fact that the choices in the game aren't equal. True: the game blatantly ridicules you for making some. However, I don't think it's a reasonable critique.
is not a real CYOA  game; it's based on a work that already has a "canon" storyline, so different options have different weight by default, some of them being "real" (i.e. Shakespeare's), while others being alternative. The goal of
is not to provide you with an array of balanced options, each of them having its own merit, it's actually quite the opposite: the game sets to make fun of the "canon" choices.
So, if you're looking to truly, honestly roleplay Hamlet,
won't suit you (you should maybe consider a career as an actor instead, people say the notion of playing Hamlet is kinda popular in theatre). However, if you're up to having some fun and are not averse to text adventures, this game is definitely one I would suggest trying.

Speaking of the shake, get ready to feel whole realm's worth of disappointment in the between chapter cinematics - which are pre-rendered in stunning 720P! This game isn't Planescape: Torment. It's not even all that much like it, despite the fact that it wanted to be, and that it certainly intends to open itself up to comparison. That's not a terrible thing; it's just a little misguided on the part of the developers. It probably helped their angle on their Kickstarter, I suppose.
HOWEVER, this game is, in and of itself, a delight to play. The writing is solid, polished, layered, and interesting. There are a ton of details to explore, many of which are easy to miss (though few of those are crucial). The mechanics and systems are generally fun. And, of course, there's the replay value, of which there is plenty, depending on which actions you take.
Generally, I recommend this, unless you dislike reading (because there's an awful lot of it), or want something with a quick pace to it.

The story is OK, but the much better writing is in the fringes. They hint of many amazing sights which unfortunately, you'll never get to experience in game.
The game is too short and the locations are disjointed, feeling like a series of separate and unconnected pieces. This may be partially the fault of the setting.
The system behind it is bland and feels very flat. You rarely feel like you are increasing in power, and I never once felt like I was short on stat points to spend on whatever I felt like. You never feel like blowing points to succeed on a skill check is going to leave you short later.
Crises are trivial, and while it's great that there are non-combat options for almost all of them, swimming in stat points means you can breeze through every one.
InXile seem to have put a lot of effort into the writing, but it's let down by the actual game.

You'll have to excuse this pissy little rant, but I'm beyond waiting for Inexile to make this right.
It's been three months of waiting. Scratch that, I Kickstarted this game so it's been YEARS of waiting to play and finish this game. I wanted any review I wrote in reaction to it to be nothing but praise. And it would have been. Sadly, I can't do that and it's no fault with the game design itself. Sorry to Gavin and the other people who poured their creative heart and soul into this - the tech guys have failed you and soured a fan's opinion of your work.
There I was, at the end of a fantastically written and conceptualised game only to find that QA had failed spectacularly and left a game breaking bug in the closing moments. Battles were fought, companion conclusions found and the finishing line was in sight. I'd loved every second up until that moment. The writing had been fantastic, thoughtful and pushed me into viewing familiar moral quandry with fresh eyes. The gameplay was a nice mix of tactics and decision making, with unusual options for non-aggressive actions and conclusions that surprised.
And then it happened.
A load screen that I've since found out connects to a location called Oasis, right at the end of the game. The load screen popped up and never left. I waited. I reloaded. I validated the game cache in steam. I did everything I could and nothing was getting me past that load screen. I contacted Inexile over on Twitter and was told they were aware of the issue, that they were working on a solution and that I perhaps could revert to an old save file and un-equip a particular piece of equipment - a pair of rings that allow characters to share stat buffs. My last save before this moment? Five hours prior. I wasn't all that excited at having to slog through familiar territory, repeating actions so I could see the conclusion as I'd intended to. That wasn't my job, releasing a working product was their job. So I waited.
And I waited.
And I waited.
A patch arrived and didn't fix my problem. I asked Inexile about the issue again on Twitter. This time there was silence in response. Embittered by the farce so far but wanting to praise this game in the face of a lot of people complaining about the writing and gameplay I'd enjoyed, I thought I'd give them the benefit of the doubt, wait and see one more time.
So here we are. A major content patch and even a hint that my specific issue had been fixed in the patch notes. Has the issue been fixed? No. I'm still stuck on 49% on that same loading screen, still faced with the increasingly high likelihood that I'll have to spend hours replaying things I've seen before after months of holding plot points in mind. If QA had done their job and tested properly then I'd never have had this game ruined. It's as simple as that. And I get it, I might come off as overly upset about a game and life could be worse, but after a long wait, money gambled on crowd funding and a lot of positive talk in the aftermath of the game's release from Inexile, I can't be anything other than irritated by my experience with their product.
Is it a smart, thought provoking piece of media? Yes. Absolutely.
Could I confidently tell you that you'll be able to play as you like and finish the game without issue? No, I can't. At this point, I expect I'll never finish the game unless there's a fix in the next few days, I'll uninstall the game and put Inexile in a mental pile marked "Wait for a deep discount, buying their games on release is a pointless gamble".

The only RPG in recent years that has truly drawn me in and had me wanting to always play just a bit more. The world is engrossing and I found myself always wanting to know more about the backstory and characters. It's also unique in being one of the few RPGs you can go almost the entire campaign without using violence to solve a quest. Even the "crisis" rounds, which are effectively the combat sequences, can usually be resolved in a variety of ways, many of which don't involve direct combat. For some people, that might be a drawback, but if you enjoy actually roleplaying, it's amazing because it gives you the freedom to play out however you want in any situation.
The criticisms I'm reading in these reviews are weird, because it's like they didn't actually enjoy what is good about both Torment games: the story and the ideas. There are really interesting philosophical ideas and questions at play both in the main quest and in the side characters you meet throughout. I will grant one criticism is a bit valid, in that ending hits a little odd and you don't quite feel it as you would hope, but many of the characters really draw you in nonetheless. I didn't want the story to end.
As of the current date, there are a few things to be aware of that will hopefully improve with future patches. One, there are some game-breaking bugs that can happen, especially if you have a particularly large number of NPCs in a crisis round. This has improved already, but be forewarned that you might want to give them a few more months to work out bugs. Two, there were a number of features that didn't quite get rounded out, such as plot developments you expect them to follow-up on, but don't come back. They have announced they will be adding back in that content in future patches, they just didn't have enough time to finish some of the extras.
I'm already looking forward to playing it through again, role-playing different personalities for the last castoff, and enjoying the extra content that will come.

Most of the complaints I've seen for T:ToN seem to be the very drawing features of the game. It is wordy. It is heavily reliant on narrative/text to push the story forward and world build. Some of the text has been called "pointless" because it merely describes unnecessary things, but it succeeds in creating a sense of immersion.
The combat isn't the best, but it's nowhere near the worst either. You can spend almost the entire game without dealing with combat if you choose, but, even when you do get into combat, once you get the hang of it, it flows pretty smoothly. It's definitely a step up from Planescape, which had some of the worst combat in isometric rpg history.
I definitely enjoyed this game. My favorite game is most likely Planescape: Torment, and this, while being refreshingly different in some ways, is a worthy spiritual successor. Could it have been better? Of course! Having expectations of it being as intricate, deep, or having the same level of engagement as the former will hinder your enjoyment because the former was a masterpiece. This game however definitely holds its own with the best of the isometric narrative rpgs of old.

Luna Sky seems to have a solid idea in it's hands, but utterly fails in it's execution.
Let's start with the core gameplay:
You are Luna and you must jump around a level collecting crystal saturators, or things of light whichever suits you.
There is a certain amount needed to pass through each level's checkpoints and collecting these is very tedious and boring.
Part of that lies in how Luna controls and how she moves in the enviroment.
The dev's seem to be inspired by Sonic styled gameplay, as in go fast and collect things. No robots to beat though.
You do get at times a great sense of speed but that speed is halted at every turn as you don't generate almost any momentum and just stop dead at even very small angled inclines.
The animation on Luna is just hilariously bad, in the cutscenes she is basically a stick figure.
The level design and the environments are equally bad.
It reminds of NES era games where there were platforms only for the reason that you can jump on top of them, this makes them feel out of place.
I mean why are there floating rocks in this cavern? Are they magic? Is something holding them up?
No they are just there, floating,  without logic or reason.
The only good thing I can say about the game is the music.
It is actually quite pleasant.
The game needs a lot of polish, in almost every regard.

I always liked Hitman, until Absolution. Thankfully, this newest game skips right past that linear b-movie abortion of a game that was Absolution and returns to the roots of Hitman gameplay. This feels a lot like Blood Money, which is a good thing because that was the best Hitman game until now.
The best thing about this Hitman is that it's more of a sandbox, the maps are huge and they offer a wealth of opportunities to take down your targets in a plethora of ways. The UI is excellent, the graphics are beautiful and in my 14 hours of gameplay i haven't encountered any major bugs (the game does ctd from time to time though, especially on DX12). Despite that, its original and most of all entertaining. Kudos to whoever came up with the idea of the Elusive targets, really original and fun game mode.
This game is far from perfect though due to two MAJOR design flaws.
1. Always online DRM: Seriously, Io-Interactive have you guys been living under a rock, the world hates this DRM system because it may somewhat protect your game from pirates but it damages in a big way the experience of people who actually pay for your game. If your game is solid (and your game comes close to that) people will buy it, just look at the witcher 3 sales, there's seriously no need for always online DRM.
2. The episodic release: Some people don't hate it but nobody likes it, is a way to sum up how people feel about it. Personally, i don't like it at all and i would have prefered a complete game instead of little episodes.
People who bought this game by single episodes are getting the middle finger by IOI by not letting them know beforehand what they'd be missing if they didn't buy the full experience or the upgrade.

I have to admit that I was extremely sceptical about this game when it was announced. The episodical and always online stuff just sounded ehhhh like hell and I only ended up buying it after seeing some videos of it (Robbaz and Giant Bomb if anyone is curious) which made the game look amazing.
And it is! It's absolutely astonishing how many ways you can go through missions and the maps are enormous. Yes, there are some issues with the DRM (don't buy the game if you don't have a stable internet connection) but it hasn't affected my enjoyment of the game at all. I really enjoy that it's episodic as well since it encourages me to explore the maps as they are released, it's a model that I enjoy personally.
It's the best hitman game I've played and I've played blood money so there is really no bigger praise I can give to it.
They originally said buying the episodes individually would not hinder your gameplay, but tomorrow they are releasing content I will not have access to because I bought it episodically.

I just wanted to give this a recommendation but honestly I cant
I started playing this game this year in april and has quickly become my favourite game
But It only has become my favourite game because of the little rare good things that can happen to you in this game
I almost always play this game solo so I have been through it all, from 1v10ing zergs to 1v2s and much more
Although i admit, the game makes it fun the way the maps are generated differently and all of that it just wastes tooo much of your time
If you want a game that you can play all day non stop, then this is it
But if you are going to play any amount less than that then it is definitely not going to be fun
Now are the PROS and CONS
PROS::
The wipe days of this game.
Now I will admit, the most fun I have had on this game is when everyone is equal with bows and other low tier gear and everyone is fighting and getting bases down. The wipe days are the most fun and rewarding, but also the most likely to make you rage quit or just delete the game.
The hapis map
Now this is just my opinion, but I will say that the hapis map,(or atleast the old one) is where some of the non toxic and the most enjoyable people are. I will say that about half my hours are hours on the hapis map, because when I just started out the game I knew it was the easiest map to get started. In all my map wipes I have met at least  1 nice person that I have become friends with(and this was when I had about 50 hours). It has some of the noobiest players with the worst aim, just like all of us when we started out.
Constant development and updates
EVERY single thursday there is an update. Now I know that the updates arnt always big or exiting, but that means that the devs care about this game and want it to keep running. They also listen to the community and even have MASSIVLY helped new players over the months. When I started rust I kept on trying to eat the seed because they said they were edible and now the new players even know what to get, what to hit and not to hit and the descriptions are a MASSIVE help
CONS::
The massive waste of your time
Now if you want to spend all of your time on a new and entertaining game, then this is the game for you. But if you want to casually want to spend about an hour a day on this game then please DO NOT get this game. Sometimes you will be spending hours just to die with all of your stuff that you need to make a base and will have to restart,( has happened to me multiple times).
The community
Now with an exeption of a few servers, almost all the servers I have been on I have had a toxic encounter with at least on person. I am not saying all people are bad, in fact I have met a few people who have become good friends with me. But I have had WAYYY more bad encounters than good in this game
Zergs
What is a zerg? A massive group of people with low skill count who target lesser groups for raiding or harrassment. Joining a zerg is like joining a ctf map on tf2, very very easy. Zergs are like texas, where everything is bigger
The fps and lag
Now I have a $1000 laptop that can run csgo in 120 fps, overwatch in 90 fps, tf2 in 150 fps and other games that have meduim graphic needs I can run fairly well. And even though I have a decent pc. I can only run this game at about 60 fps. Sometimes on 2x or 4x servers my fps can go down to 45-50. Also in game whenever yu render a base on two, the screen stops and rubberbands you a couple seconds back, and in some cases that could mean death for you. Now I get it that the devs are working on garbage collection right now, but tell me, shouldnt they have a game that most people can run before they add anything else?
END:::

For me, this was a great experience; worthy a successor of Planescape Toment.
+ Battle system is a new approach, maybe too easy and too heavily scripted but overall, it does its job well
+ Story is intruiging and relevant
+ Skill system works fine, although "edge" might be a little bit too strong overall
+ Characters are memorable, at least the ones I played with; their stories evolve over the course of the entire game...
- ...which is why you would have to play through the game again to experience the other's stories (maybe it did it wrong, possible)
- replayability is probably not too high, as of course the quests are the same, as are the battles
+ length is good, ending was coming when I got tired of the game; can't understand how to get through the game in 20 hours; 30 hours I would deem a "normal" playthrough, I did spend some extra time, I have to admit
+/- short gametime of others might be expliccable though by the fact that some quests must be actively searched; for me, this is positive, but others might not like it
But I am pretty sure I can get back to the game in some year-periods, just as I did with Planescape Torment.
If you enjoy reading, exploration, and decision making more than combat then Tides of Numenera is a great title.  There is almost no combat in the 8 hours I've played so far.

The game is interesting (though in no way really succeeding to live up to Planescape: Torment), but the Mac version is essentially broken for me: since two months now, the game freezes on launch and is thus unplayable. InXile fails to provide any kind of support to the reported problem. This is ridiculous.

Much like Planescape: Torment, you're likely to either fall squarely into this game's audience or not like it at all. While it doesn't pack *quite* the storytelling punch of its predecessor, Torment: Tides of Numenera is well worth playing if you're a fan of the story-rich atmospheric RPG.

Don't write many reviews, but having sunk 140 hours into this badboy, can definitely say if youre into fun management/strategy hybrids, that are detailed enough to capture your attention, but casual enough that you can drop in/out as you feel like it, then you will thoroughly enjoy this!
After 100+ hours you will (at least I did) start to feel like maybe you could do with that tiny extra bit of complexity, mainly in the transfer window, but it really is a minor gripe, and only if youre nerdy enough to sink that amount of time into it like me! haha

I will write some things that I don't like in the game, but I don't want to be misunderstood... I definitely recommend it and absolutely love it! It is a unique idea, that all football gamers will like...
I read on other reviews, comparisons with other Football Manager games, like FM... Just don't fool yourselves. It has nothing to do with the depth of FM, or the management aspect of it. This is the game's greatest strength, but also its greatest weakness...
What do I mean by that?
The strength is that the in-game management during the game is managed by you! For example, the decision to place a certain left CB in your defence to deal with a superb right CF of the opponent is going to hit back at you, whether you were right or wrong... This means that the stats each player have, will surely play a big part in the game, if the tackling will be successfull or not, if the long ball will make it to the midfielder, if if if.... You will feel very excited and perhaps proud, if you make right choices, but also frustration when you click the button and miss the tackle! A superb experience!
All aspects of the game point at your in-game management. With that in mind you will be looking for the right players in the transfer market, renew the contracts, or swap your players positions. That is the greatest difference with FM. The in-game management, the turn-based RPG system.
The weaknesses on the other hand of this game (in my opinion ofcourse) is the lack of one element: Realism.
I don't like the superpower of some players, the skills they can develop, with which the opponent can't react, if they don't have the opposite "super skill". For example scoring in corners, magically dribble the opponent, scoring at a great distance, make the super tackle etc. It ruins all the realism in football! I would prefer a more realistic approach...
I also don't like the lack of movement of players. For example during a turn you can only move the player with the ball. Why? In football all players are moving at the same time. I would prefer a game where during a turn you could move all of your players at the same time, with propably a bigger pitch and not moving in squares. I know that this suggestion ruins much of the mechanism, that the game is currently built, but for me it would made more sense this way.
I would also like to see the dev team to make use and explore more elements of football, such as headers, free kicks or crosses...
I know it's a game still on early access, but I am writing all these things as a constructive discussion and opinion. I know its a great idea, there is a great dev team behind and I am thrilled to see a game which will have the realism of FM and the mechanism of a turn based RPG game...!

I find myself having the most success letting the AI do the matches, so actually watching the matches is really...boring after the third time.
The 'x-com' element is really just boils down to how can i make a shot in 3 moves.  If you have an ai opponent that is just smashing you on one saide there aint♥♥♥♥♥♥you can do about it until the half.  Any moves you want to make for a defender means you aren't movign the ball up and the same AI will just steal and shoot in the same move.  Boiler player 3 moves per side doesn't cut it.  Maybe 1 move each.  I think the dev's have watched a few matches but don't realize every action on the pitch has a reaction on both ends.  Offsides really isn't a thing.  fouls are just RNG, no slider to effect your chances on how aggressive you want your players.
the way you level up your 'coaches' with fame is the same way you're leveling players...which is drip fed at a slow pace.  you can get 'maybe' 2-10 fame per match and every upgrade is n+2.  Meaning whatever upgrade, from whatever coach, is going to need 2 more than the last.  By an hour in, each upgrade was 50 fame and I was getting maybe 4 fame?  To upgrade a player its either 2 seasons of play or...200 fame.  At this point I was over my head and nothing I could do but lose.  I ended up leveling up my players, but then when they were retiring the players i could buy were woefully crap.  So I made it to the first league (3->2->1), then had to drop down to the second cause i had to rebuild.  But because I wasn't getting good replacements well I was still losing.  I find myself either woefully underpowered or smashing everything.
It doesnt make sense that you use fame instead of money to pretty much level up everything.  EPL is known for throwing money at any problem but this is pretty much a no-op.  The jumps in spending are insane.  10k -> 100k -> 370k.  The most I got from a match is maybe 22k.  Most players cost 200-500k.
gameplay loop seems to be simulate all the matches, and inbetween make minor adjustements on injury or training.  End of season buy your new team then hope it was enough carry over.  if not, well you'll relegated to a league you smash so you build up your $$ (not fame) again.
to the devs, who gives a ♥♥♥♥ about face engine when you don't even see your players on the pitch.  I didn't even realize that one of my star players had a mowhawk until I had to renew the contract.  You're exponential costs for upgrades is absured.  Make coaches like players where you hire/fire them.  Remove the fame system and make everything money.  If you want to keep fame, then do it in building your arena more.  Use it to attract fans.  Why can't I build buildings?  Where is the training camp.  Where is the locker room.  Where is the coaches meeting room.  There is absolutely no reason for me to keep a player at age 34 when he retires in a year when I can ax him for a 6 figure payout most times.  When a player retires with the team, that's fame.  When Thierry Henry retired he got a statue.  When Ian Wright retired there were documentaries.  When a player retires here, he's just deleted.  Fame in real life is built by the player sticking with the club and it's ignored.
I really want to like this game.  I will come back to this but for now it's not enough.  Even the demo isn't enough. It gets you from league 3 to 2 which is just a cakewalk.  I won the league by simulating every match and made 2 changes to player positions at the start.

Finally, we get a new Hitman game, and it hasn't disappointed (yet) and remains fun.
One of the peeves of this game is no doubt the episodic release which is a huge, huge disappointment and what I would normally consider a significant blemish on an otherwise amazing game.
However, I think iO made the right move here. Let me explain.
Each level is an individual sandbox assassination utopia. Multiple ways to take down your main story targets, and your approach can easily shift geras without your plans blowing out of the water. The levels present themselves with obvious ways of accomplishing your task, but this doesn't mean it's nessecarily easy. It's more throwing your options in your face so you don't have to waste time hunting how to trigger objectives; it's now very obvious compared to previous games.
The real genius here is the inclusion and return of the Contracts mode from Absolution, arguably the best thing to come out of the game. Escalation is also a lot of fun while swiching up the pace and end up doing some really creative and ridiculous bonus missions. These may seem like filler and padding but they really do bring out the most bang for your buck for the game and are genuinely entertaining.
The only major criticisms I have are very minor, but I find them to be deeply flawed.
Assassinations are as simple as pressing the Q button near your target now for a neck snap or fiber wire strangulation. It really takes the fun out of pulling out your wire and hoping nobody sees you when you can just knock your target to the ground quickly and flee the scene and get away with it.
You can essentially cheese the unlocks by taking advantage of game saves and reloading every time you do something different, making it possible to unlock what would normally take 5 or 6 playthroughs in one. I consider this a con because it encourages laziness. However I am willing to bet some people would embrace this feature.
There are performance issues. I would expect better performance on my FX-8320 and GTX 970 both overclocked. Framerates are across the board, dipping into the low 30s and high 20s at times in crowded areas. Hopefully more tweaks to the engine improve this in the future.
With that said, this IS the next Blood Money for sure, with some tweaks to make the game more accessible to newer players. Older players and fans of the series may not appreciate the new changes, but this is truly a worthy successor to the original franchise as we knew it before Absolution.

Five Nights at Freddy's is a bizarre franchise. It came from a man who was at his worst, and in sprouted into something of internet sensation. People were playing it left and right, and it was extremely beloved by many. Sequels were made that was more or less the same, introducing new mechanics and building on it's story. By the fourth game, however, it had been there done that. FNaF World was a huge disaster on launch, to the point it was made free on GameJolt. However, people still continued to like the games. Now there was a new FNaF game in development called "Sister Location", and obviously people were hyped. Scott learned from his mistakes and actually took his time on the game. After almost half a year, the game releases. The question is, does it stand up along with the other games in the franchise?
Five Nights at Freddy's: Sister Location is almost COMPLETELY different from the previous installments. You no longer need to survive from 12 to 6 am, you need to complete a variety of tasks before you can complete the night. It's not as linear as before, there is always something new each night. It's extremely innovative for the franchise, and there's so much more to it. There is actual fear, panic, dread, and terror, and doesn't just rely on jumpscares and atmosphere anymore. It has a charm to it that the other 4 games (not including FNaF World) didn't ever attempt. This is defiantly one of the best games of the franchise thus far.
That being said, this game has some issues as of now (v1.0). The most prominent being the sudden difficulty spikes in the nights. The game can and will get extremely difficult. You will die. ALOT. Most infamously being Night 4. Took me about 2-3 hours to finally pass, and even then it was just barely. If your looking for extreme difficulty, give it a shot.
The story is extremely interesting, especially the ending. I wouldn't spoil it here, but I will say it is most definitely up for interpretation.
It's a fantastic game. Horror fans should give this game a go, even if they have never tried FNaF before. You wouldn't regret it (until Night 4 :P)

This might just be the best game I've played to date, if not one of the best. This game sort of came and went during 2012, and nobody noticed it too much. IGN gave it a 7/10, and GameSpot gave it a 6/10, and the world moved on. But not me. I was fixated on my favorite game reviewer, Yahtzee Croshaw, who proclaimed this was the best games of 2012 and one of his personal favorites. And I thought to myself while looking up the info on Spec Ops, "What's so special about this? It looks like a samey third-person cover-shooter." And I have never been so wrong in my life.
To lay things down simply, don't go into Spec Ops: The Line to feel like a badass or a hero. Just don't. While 99% of games make you feel like you can take on the whole world, Spec Ops is part of the 1%, making you feel like a horrible piece of crap- and manages to tell the story of you, as a piece of crap, in the immerse and beautiful, yet ugly, Dubai. As you navigate this storm of sand and insanity with your crew, you start to realize how things aren't just getting more complicated with the situation in Dubai... but also in your own head.
The game handles controversial issues like fighting Americans (Seriously! No Russians or Muslims, but your own men!), the usage of White Phosphorous, and PTSD, all of which the game sheds in it's horrifying light. The game even goes beyond the actual gameplay mechanics to ask you things like, "Do you remember why you came here?", and "This isn't real, so why should you care?". And people chastise the game on this front saying, "Well, I did it because the game made me do it!", which is completely missing the point of Spec Ops. You are actively taking away peoples lives in this games, if you want to believe it or not. And Spec Ops goes out of its way to make sure you know the weight of death and how these people are living and breathing- not just programs.
A great example was a mundane moment, where my squad and I were about to enter this tower, and I raised my gun to these two guards- unaware of my presence. I held my finger, because the first guard said, "Would you like some gum?", which led to a horrible conversation involving the two opening up to each other, and feeling depressed of how the whole world has gone to hell. And I shot them.
The funniest thing is, people glanced over this game, not giving it the time of day, then the very next year showered praise all over The Last of Us. I love The Last of Us, don't get me wrong, but Spec Ops: The Line is far superior to it's message than I think The Last of Us was to theirs. I view The Last of Us, like The Godfather- the one everyone loves and talks about and I love just as much. But Spec Ops: The Line is like Barton Fink. If you bring it up, people will react with, "What is that? I've never heard of it." but I think it's superior to the former.
Don't play Spec Ops expecting to play another Call of Duty game or Battlefield- go into Spec Ops like a normal human being, and realize just how horrible of a human being you are.

-> MINOR SPOILERS AHEAD <-
Batman Arkham Origins when it was initially released had too many bugs to count, that frankly not only ruined the overall
experience but in some cases made the game literally unplayable. Having played the previous Arkham games and seeing the Trailer for the game I got really hyped, it looked promising. So how does the game fare?
-Intro:
To start off - the setting is great, playing the role of an unrefined Batman struggling to survive on Christmas Eve being targeted by 8 hired killers of Black Mask and the one and only - Joker whilst getting to know himself, what he wants, his ambitions and goals in life and who he is or will become, how to world views him. Meeting familiar faces and forging the friendships and rivalries we know and love from DC characters.
-Story
The Story is mediocre and it throws its trump-card, the big reveal WAY TO EARLY!
I don't want to spoil anything so I won't continue with this section.
-The World
The game starts at the Blackgate Prison Facility, being overrun by criminals, and the beloved "super-criminals". Batman has to investigate who is behind the prison break and put an end to their deeds. While the prison segment is great, the intro fantastic, and later being introduced to all the assassin that you will face later on, with amazing backstories and cinematics, through that little segment the goals are set and you have a purpose as a player and as Batman!
<->And it pretty much goes downhill from here except one or two points in the game.<->
Getting to explore all of Gotham sounded great! (on paper) The game features the same places as Arkham City, adding in the rest of Gotham (an island south of the Arkham part) Two equally large places for you to travel and explore! The game introduces a fast travel option which makes the whole exploration thing a lot faster getting from place to place. One of the biggest drawbacks of this game is that freeroaming Gotham isn't as fulfilling or satisfying as the previous game.
The world is really bland (going as far as to say the city feels dead at some parts). The snow that is covering ALL of Gotham is there so they can hide the fact that they are unable to create a lust and immersive city for the player to explore and interact.
You will feel like you are making circles around the place or just seeing the same places over and over again, because you can't tell where you are going or making progress, forcing you to open and close the map every 5 seconds to get your bearings. Both upper and southern Gotham, are 99% most of the part boring, they don't offer any interesting places to explore and the places that are rehashed are more interesting that the new places (solely for the fact that you want to find how much bland the Arkham City part is).
In contrast-> Arkham City felt alive, every detail there made the gameworld so much more vivid and much more interesting to explore, it gave the motivation to learn more about this place and its habitats/prisoners/criminals. Listening to prisoners talking to each other, badmouthing their bosses, witnessing prisoners bullying other prisoners, other random events, from the carefully placed billboards featuring known places to people who read the comics or seen the movies. Everything was placed with care and Rocksteady with respect to the Batman/DC lore. Getting to know the villains from their interesting and long side-missions, sympathize with them and pity them at the same time.
[That brilliant writing from Rocksteady isn't here to no-ones surprise]
-The Side-mission Characters
While great in the comics, here they are pushed aside for no reason, the missions are rushed and the payoff isn't at all great or fulfilling and you will end up wanting more of these characters, without recordings, no other interactions, all but one or two missions are very anti-climactic and feel half-arsed. The other new addition is the "extensive" (in quotations) detective mode, which would have made you feel more like Batman, while the concept seems promising it isn't executed well. The game will hold your hand throughout all of the investigation scenes, telling you exactly where the interaction points are, while looking cool and impressive your involvement in this as a player is minimal at best.
-The Gameplay
Its pretty much the same as City, but slightly changed so that is more forgiving with the addition of some charged fists weapon. The combat might seem the same to a lot of people but from my experience with it, it is more cheap that City, when a enemy swings his fist, sometimes it connects when it shouldn't and feels more clunky and unnatural,
(Like the Batman vs Bane fight in the Dark Knight Rises, HEYO!)
I came to that conclusion because having finished every Riddle combat challenge with every character in Arkham City, (which is a lot) I have a near perfect understanding of the combat system and can safely say that they ruined the combat formula by changing little things here and there.
The last things that needs to be addressed are the
-Boss Fights
and
-Voice Acting
Batman is not voiced by Mr. Conroy anymore and Joker not by Mark Hamill. Which turned many people off, it was little discouraging I'll be honest, the fact that THE definite voices for these two characters are getting replaced is off-putting. Batman's new voice is surprisingly very fitting and suits the character and timeline VERY well, the actor portrays him faithfully and is a welcome addition and worthy (If you may) to play the Batman role.
On the other hand we have Troy Baker taking the role of the Joker. Honestly I was in shock when I heard his voice in the game, the laugh was SPOT ON and portrayed the character to a T. I'll go on a whim and say that he is ON PAR with Mark Hamill, In my humble and honest opinion no-one could have voice this Young Joker more *perfectly* that Baker. I was honestly scared when he made a threat (Like the Nolan Joker) always laughing even when beaten to a pulp.
They can't replace them but where a welcome and great addition to the franchise.
The thing that is bar none, no questions asked, no argument here: are the boss fights (most of them a least)
The payoff is fulfilling and deserving to call itself an Arkham game based on how it handled the boss fights.
For the most part they are diverse and unique. The most hyped battle in the game with Deathstroke, delivers ALL it promises:
(Black-Bar Short Description about the fight )
---Very Minor Spoilers---
FINAL PART (PROS)
1)Fantastic Voice Acting
2)Great looking visuals/textures
3)Great Boss Fights
FINAL PART (CONS)
1)Uninteresting Game World
2)Mediocre Plot
3)Bugs/Glitches (Gamebreaking ones, official patches/support ended)
4)Unbalanced Gadgets
5)Not fleshed out side-characters
6)Multiplayer still unbalanced and may never be fixed
7)Rehashed assets not put to good use.
I wouldn't recommend this game despite its pros. They are way, way outnumbered, I would recommend buying Arkham Asylum and Arkham City, they are VASTLY superior to this title, its just not up to par. I could recommend it only to the hardcore die-hard fans of the Bat and the series and only after a huge price drop.

Overall the game is very very good the combat has depth and is not too complex, maling it really feeling like one of the only games that feels like it can stand on combat alone if needed but with the platfroming/ puzzle solving mechanics that give it a balance of fun that I feel that only this and the orgional price of persia series has accomplished in the 3d relm. The story is engaging and gritty while keeping the plot simple and is meant to give of a feeling of determination to stop what is going on rather than putting 50 plot twists in or going down so deep in Batman lore that you have to read years worth of Batman comics or stop the game to search in wikipedia to understand (thats is not saying there will be no charcters that people will not know before getting into the game but rather the game does a very good job explaining who they are through both the cut scenes and gameplay styles and areas that you interact with them in). Thank being said I think there is two things holding the game back. The main one is that the city in the single player just feels so....... empty you end feeling like your saving a city with nobody in it. Now, the games excuse is that everyone is staying in their homes due to a huge storm, but in reality there are still some people out and about even in snow storms (now saying that is smart or not, that is a different subject) so could had a least a couple of people out and about in the streets, something like saving a woman when those sudden crime reports come up? Even a few npcs would make it feel that your in a living city and not an apocalytic one. (and for any of those that will say that the world is more for collecting, the orgional Crackdown was a collect-a-thon in almost the same exact way and still managed to create a livelier city than this AND was released in 2007) the other promlem is that the multiplayer is boring, which I know is a very common complaint and is really not the reason people buy this game but it still dosen't change the fact that it could be done better than a generic thrid person shooter with batman combat, what makes it frustrating is that all it need to be good was a endless oneline mode with friends similar to the single player challenges or some online co-op.  Don't let the negatives deter you though this game is good just could have been better if Wb interactive wasn't trying to release a new game every year  like it is the combat version of call of duty which I am very afraid that it is becoming like that with the new game announced for this year.

It pains me to give this game a bad review. I am an old-school CRPG gamer from back in the days of Interplay and Black Isle Studios. I backed Wasteland 2 and was very happy with the results, so it was a no-brainer that I would back Torment: Tides of Numenera. After a long four-year wait, I am sad to express my disappointment. I was looking forward to a strange, story-rich RPG in the vein of Planescape: Torment, but I was wasn't expecting this. The weirdness has been piled on like paint with a palette knife on a Van Gogh. Dialogue options added no real depth to my character, because each response was just as cryptic as the others, giving me no real insight into the way other characters felt about my decisions. After a mere 5 hours of playing time, I was dreading loading the game back up for fear of conversing with another NPC; and I hadn't even gotten into a combat situation beyond the first introductory encounter. Like an acid trip that's gone on too long, I just wanted the game to be over so I could get back to relaxing in the soothing world of reality. Other people seem to like this approach based on the reviews, and I can see why some might find it a refreshing change of pace, but I need a little more grounding to keep from getting lost in the mire of obscurity.

3 things before we get started: 1.) I played more than 10 hours, 2.) the review is based on my personal thoughts and experiences with T:ToN and its predecessor and thus there will be some bias. TL:DR included at the bottom.
I'v probably dumped around 100 hours into Planscape Torment, it's probably one of my favourite roleplaying games of all time. As such I've had incredibly high hopes for the spiritual sucessor. With that in mind, I've got to admit that this game was a complete and utter disappointment for myself. Here's why:
- Both Planscape Torment and ToN had a (somewhat) predetermined character to begin with, although PT allowed for a much wider approach to character development. The amount of different methods in approaching and solving quests/altercations far surpasses the newer game. Which in turn allowed for me to really connect with my character, something very important for immersion reasons. I felt that ToN went much less diversive in regards to that, and often times I felt that I couldn't carry myself (or the character for a lack of a better term)  in the way I wanted to, and instead had a number of ways this particular predefined character would behave.
This would be fine, IF the character would be as charasmatic, interesting, or strong as, say, a Gerald of Rivia, JC Denton, or Shepard. It's no good, however, if I can't relate to the main protagonist in an RPG, while not being able to much alter his demeanor. ToN's main protagonist I found extremely forgettable and the options at my disposable did not help me mold them into something interesting.
- Party side-characters are as uninteresting as they come and to me, it feels like as if the developers didn't even mean for them to be relevant. They mostly keep quiet, don't have much to say if you initiate conversation, nor do I find what they say particularly interesting.
Game mechanics wise:
- There's some sort of karma system at play, but it seems very intangible and I can't really speak on its effects. A notification will pop up every now and then, mentioning that the character has drifted towards a certain tide, but I'll be honest in saying that I found it much too abstract for it to peak my interest. Personal preference, I suppose.
- Combat seems slow, sluggish and extremely simple. I get that combat is a very minor part about the game, which isn't something I'm happy about as long as it's not optional, but even with it being such a sidenote it's incredibly dull and I found myself trying to avoid it at all costs.
- Which brings me to my next point; each action that is based on your attributes/stats has a certain pool. The pool will be drained depending on how much effort is spent on an action/attempt. More effort = higher % of success. So get this, let's say I make a really strong, intimidating character, because I want to be able to do strong-man things and intimidate. All the time. That's what my character's about, otherwise I'd probably use trinkets or other stat-boosting items whenever necessary.
I get into a couple of scenarios in which I can do the above...after about 3 encounters in which luck-based failure wasn't an option (to me) and a subsequent high effort, I have drained the respective pool for actions involving str and/or fortitude. My character's no longer there to handle the dirty work, but he's not smart either, nor well versed at things related to magic...pretty useless, he is right now.
I'm a wuss though, so I save plenty of times and always make sure to be well equipped for what's ahead of me. So what am I going to do? Quickload whenever I run out of pool-points, with the intention of prioritizing or return to a location at which I can rest (for an arguably hefty amount of currency). I mean to say that this mechanic adds nothing to the gameplay, at least nothing positive. As soon as you drain a character's respective pools they're virtually useless, both in conversation and combat... much fun to be had indeed.
On the technical side of things, there's really little worth mentioning. I found the overall look very plain and uninteresting, there's some utterly weird locations here & there, but weird doesn't automatically equate to good or memorable in my books.  Same goes for the music.
To summarize;
- if you like to read a LOT and aren't necessarily interested in making major plotaltering decisions left & right, then this game may be for you. If, however, you don't enjoy somewhat predefined protagonists in RPGs, unless they're very strong characters to begin with or give you all the tools to make them believable in their own rights, I'd say you'll probably not enjoy this game very much.
- if you enjoy regular and well-executed combat, this game is not for you.
- if you enjoy an intriguing storyline, this is PROBABLY not for you. this is highly debatable, I guess. For me, neither the story, plots nor any of the characters managed to suck me in.
- if you expect this game to expand on Planscape Torment's strengths, you will more than likely not enjoy this game. i'd argue that it's much closer to being several leaps behind than on par, never mind ahead.
tl:dr
less than stellar, not much like Planscape Torment. there are and have been much better RPGs on the market that share /some/ similarities. (The Shadowrun series,  Tyranny, Pillars of Eternity, Wasteland, Fallout 1 & 2 and the list goes on if you're willing to play 1st person, 3rd person and/or more action oriented RPGs). as harsh as it sounds I wouldn't play this game if it were for free.

Like a lot of people here, I loved Planescape. The cRPGs - and especially the isometric RPGs new and old - are my favorite genre. I was so excited for this game, and I never would have expected that 6 hours in I would be so bored that I just couldn't go on.
Others have written more detailed criticisms, but one I'd like to add: While critics applaud this game "for its lack of combat" because its "refreshing" and "different" what you get is a total lack of action.  I'm all for world building, character building, and exploration. But at some point, all you're doing is talking to one NPCs after another, each of whom have their own weird gimmick. So I went back to Pillars of Eternity and started a new playthrough. Torment made me yearn for games that similar, but much better.

Played a little over 30hrs (Offline with patch 1.0.2) as a Jack.
RECOMMEND? - Yes!, if you love RPG’s where decisions matter long-term and have a variety of fascinating stories.
PROS:
1. Story – It’s like reading 20 great, chose-your-own-adventure books. The game also gives an epilogue of your actions when the game ends.
2. Dialogue – Characters have opinions that change based on your decisions with many branching paths.
3. Combat – The combat was a major step-up from Planescape Torment’s (the non-remastered version) combat.  I had a good sense of what was happening and felt less pressure with it being turn based combat.
CONS:
1. Character Actions – During combat, npc’s actions would sometimes suffer from severe lag. I sometimes wondered if a npc was ever going to perform an action. Characters could also go into a loop of not knowing where to go if their path was blocked. They also got momentary stuck on objects quite frequently outside of combat, but this didn’t bother me.
2. Alerting the Player – Most generally the game does a good job of informing the player. However, it wasn’t always apparent that I was about to enter a new area that I couldn’t return from. I also feel the game should have done a better job of pointing out which quests were time sensitive.
3. Ending – Seemed like the ending happened a little too quickly based on the pacing of the rest of the game.
FINAL THOUGHTS:
I was a Kickstarter backer and was displeased when I found out some promised features were cut.  As of writing this, I had read that InXile is going to hopefully add some cut features.
I hope you love reading because this game has a lot of reading.  After finishing it, I wanted more of this game and stories of the Ninth World. That might be why it seemed like it was ending a little too quickly. Here’s hoping that there will be a sequel.

I think the best way to realise the seperation between the quality of this game and the quality of its technical execution is to observe the radically different review ratio on the main game compared to each of the individual episodes.
The levels are absolutely what a Hitman game needs, they're sprawling, multistaged, abound with opportunities and full of a strange personality. Each location feels new and different, Sapienza particularly, which I think (having played all the Hitman games) is my favourite level ever made. Contracts are quite weak but elusive targets are fantastic, I love the added tension and forced immersion into the role of a Hitman. Adding to some of the later complaints, however, it does really suck once you're half way through the mission and the server boots you out because it lost connection. The main issues in that regard would be the voice acting, having to hear the same three voices over and over again, and some costume repetition, espesically the waiters seem to kinda look all the same over three completely different countries. Four if you include the tutorial mission.
Where this games becomes a real piece of toilet potato is its A) DRM and B) server stability issues. I'm sure anybody reading this will have read much into these complaints in most of the other reviews so I'll avoid the details. I actually quite like the episodic format, I simply return to it once a new episode comes out and enjoy it all over again. It also gives IO an opportunity to develop on some of the weaker gameplay elements, which they seem to have actually done in response to player criticism. But you cannot underestimate the DRM enough, and it is a real dealbreaker for many people, espescially if the episodic format doesn't work for you. Living in a country that doesn't have the best internet (E.G. Australia) makes it even worse, as sometimes your normal internet connection just wont do for their terrible servers.
I'm recommending this game because its gameplay elements felt enough like a true Hitman game that they overcame the absolutely pisspoor execution of its technical qualities. Prison Architect is a game made by Introversion Software and is a game that actually did early access right. While being technically  "a fully released game" the development team is still working out a few bugs. The game is currently in version 1.0 at the time of this review and boy is it good. With 1.0 the guys up there at Introversion Studios decided to add a new mode called Escape Mode. Escape Mode allows you to jump on the other side of things and go from building prisons to flat out destroying them. The game places you into the sickening minds of one of the many possible prisoners and you must escape. You can escape through many possible ways; you can fight your way out, dig, sneak out right under patrolling guards noses, or become top dog of the prison and gain respect to plan your escapes. What prison will you be escaping from? Well, that is up to you. From the many prisons on the Steam Workshop to the prisons you've designed the possibilities are endless. Speaking of designing prisons creating a prison is harder than it seems. Although, you will catch on to the mode after playing through the games campaign which is more like a storied tutorial than anything else. Although there are problems with the game I do expect the developers to improve the game as time goes by. (9/10)

This might just be the best game I've played to date, if not one of the best. This game sort of came and went during 2012, and nobody noticed it too much. IGN gave it a 7/10, and GameSpot gave it a 6/10, and the world moved on. But not me. I was fixated on my favorite game reviewer, Yahtzee Croshaw, who proclaimed this was the best games of 2012 and one of his personal favorites. And I thought to myself while looking up the info on Spec Ops, "What's so special about this? It looks like a samey third-person cover-shooter." And I have never been so wrong in my life.
To lay things down simply, don't go into Spec Ops: The Line to feel like a badass or a hero. Just don't. While 99% of games make you feel like you can take on the whole world, Spec Ops is part of the 1%, making you feel like a horrible piece of crap- and manages to tell the story of you, as a piece of crap, in the immerse and beautiful, yet ugly, Dubai. As you navigate this storm of sand and insanity with your crew, you start to realize how things aren't just getting more complicated with the situation in Dubai... but also in your own head.
The game handles controversial issues like fighting Americans (Seriously! No Russians or Muslims, but your own men!), the usage of White Phosphorous, and PTSD, all of which the game sheds in it's horrifying light. The game even goes beyond the actual gameplay mechanics to ask you things like, "Do you remember why you came here?", and "This isn't real, so why should you care?". And people chastise the game on this front saying, "Well, I did it because the game made me do it!", which is completely missing the point of Spec Ops. You are actively taking away peoples lives in this games, if you want to believe it or not. And Spec Ops goes out of its way to make sure you know the weight of death and how these people are living and breathing- not just programs.
A great example was a mundane moment, where my squad and I were about to enter this tower, and I raised my gun to these two guards- unaware of my presence. I held my finger, because the first guard said, "Would you like some gum?", which led to a horrible conversation involving the two opening up to each other, and feeling depressed of how the whole world has gone to hell. And I shot them.
The funniest thing is, people glanced over this game, not giving it the time of day, then the very next year showered praise all over The Last of Us. I love The Last of Us, don't get me wrong, but Spec Ops: The Line is far superior to it's message than I think The Last of Us was to theirs. I view The Last of Us, like The Godfather- the one everyone loves and talks about and I love just as much. But Spec Ops: The Line is like Barton Fink. If you bring it up, people will react with, "What is that? I've never heard of it." but I think it's superior to the former.
Don't play Spec Ops expecting to play another Call of Duty game or Battlefield- go into Spec Ops like a normal human being, and realize just how horrible of a human being you are.

[[TL;DR REVIEW COMING UP]]
So, I bought this game "for the lulz" because one of my hobbies is playing and making fun of dating sims for my own amusement.
Turns out this game trolled me into laughing my♥♥♥♥♥off not AT the game, but WITH the game. The mix of clever and outlandish is amazing. The only thing that MIGHT be unintentionally funny is some of the voice acting (particularly the character of Robert), but I feel that might be a subtle jab at the "sexy" voice acting in bad, stereotypical dating sims.
It also has a lot of heart. The artwork is great and while the look of your avatar may spoil the mood a bit (even if you try and make them look normal---which I actually suggest you do the first time you play), it's still a really touching story that definitely squeezed several good tears out of me on multiple moments during my first playthrough. Despite being a dating sim, it's mostly about a relationship between a father and his daughter. I won't spoil it for you, but as someone who is closer to my father than anyone else in the world, this got me pretty emotional.
The music is pretty cool too. Even though I've tried like 10 times to beat one of the minigames, the music is so catchy that I still don't turn the sound off.
My only real critique that I can think of right now is that I wish the voice acting was a tiny bit less repetitive. That's something they really can't change, so I'm not going to comment on the the very tiny bugs because the developers can patch that up.
[[TL;DR REVIEW DONE]]

Star Wars: Jedi Academy is the latest and (sadly) last installment to the Jedi Knight series. For the first time ever, you get to choose your own character by name of Jaden Korr, a force user given the oppurtunity to be under tutelage of Jedi Master Luke Sykwalker and Kyle Katarn in Luke's prestigious jedi acdemy in Yavin 4.
So let's talk about gameplay. It was just as good as previous title. Lightsaber battles were so much more satisfying now as you have plenty of battle with cultist that you ecounter throughtout the game. However, one thing that I have noticed was that the force power were slightly unsatisfying than the previous game. It wasn't as effective (not sure if this is the right word) and it had shorter range. Other than that, level design was impressive and puzzles was not as hard and it was fun trying to nagivate my jaden through corridors. Enemy types were slighly varied except for lightsaber cultist. I felt you would only encounter 4 types of cultist only and they were kinda of oversaturated at certain point. So lightsaber battles felt a little bit tedious at certain point but the sheer fun of battling made up for it.
Story wise, it's quite simple. One thing that stuck out the most was that you now have a choice to choose light or dark something you could not do in previous entries and i was glad this option was there because it means you are able to choose dark force power without forcing you to automatically be a dark user. So you can spice things up with your playstyle. Such a welcome change!
Overall I enjoyed this game alot. A little bit tedious and very simple story but if you're looking for lightsaber battles, this is it. Get this game and the previous one (Jedi Outcast)

Nutshell: 11/10 - Awesome, pure awesome. It's got character customization, combat, and you even get to make your own lightsaber... Need I say more? Plus it's not an expensive game!
Setup: 10/10 - Really simple, just set to the highest resolution your monitor supports, set it to 32-bit texture mode, and done. Careful not to set the resolution higher than what your monitor supports, it seems stupid to do so, but it lets you, and if you do, it'll be a pain to fix, but there are no real problems on setup that is truly worth mentioning.
Will it Run: 10/10 - Absolutely! Even on my cheap laptop from 2013 can play it on highest settings, one thing to enjoy about old games is how easy they are to run.
Graphics (Compared to back then): 10/10 - This game had REALLY good graphics back then, just compare it to other games of it's era and you'll know what I mean.
Graphics (Test of Time): 6/10 - Well, this game has not withstood the test of time all too well, but, don't let that stop you from buying this game.
Gameplay: 11/10 - Ever wanted to create your own Jedi? Well here's the game to do so!
Bugs and Glitches: 10/10 - If there is any bugs, I didn't notice them, and they certainly aren't game-breaking
Overall this game is incredible, I'm glad I took the opportunity to buy it on the Christmas sale, it's a great game and you absolutely should try it if you like Star Wars.
