I got this game in a steam sale for a fiver, and I've only played it for a couple of hours so far, but I've got to say I'm already very impressed! I can see myself playing this game for many, many hours, and it looks like it'll have some replayability value as well. It's not without it's issues (which I will outline later), but no game is perfect; and the game is certainly good enough to overcome any issues or bugs it has.
The graphics are strikingly beautiful from wonderful natural landscapes right down to the sand on the ground (try drifting a car in the dirt/sand and then going to capture mode and looking at the dust particles, they are a work of beauty by themselves) and the ripples and veins on Max's arms. The combat mechanics are responsive, engaging, and exciting, the driving feels realistic enough (i.e it's not arcade style, but it's not exactly Forza or AC either), the world seems varied and large, the capture mode is wonderfully brilliant and partnered with the amazing graphics can lead to some brilliant results. I can't really comment on the story too much as I'm not too far in but it seems interesting enough, and the charachters are voiced by some good voice actors which is nice. There are also some nice little features I like such as the survival elements of the game, like fuel consumption, water, etc.
The game does have faults though - despite my PC being perfectly capable the game can be a bit choppy unless you tweak the settings a bit, fuel cans can be a little buggy when storing or carrying them, and Workshop support would be nice. I'll probably find more bugs or things to fault but this is it thus far.
Overall, it's a good game buy it for £15, buy it for £5 - it doesn't matter, it's worth it either way.

No apologies button masher (it even directly tells you at times to “mash button”).  Gameplay is long if you want to complete all the given tasks.  You can skip by a lot of things but you end up at more of a disadvantage as you go along.  Lots of grind to make the game seem long.
You’ve got only a couple buttons to worry about in the button masher and that is incredibly frustrating at times.  Want to open a gate that the game tells you to kick open? Hold “E”.  Want to open a gate that the game tells you to use a pry bar on?  Hold “E” until it tell your to “mash button” then keep hammering “E”.  Want to pick up loot?  Guess what: hold “E”.  Want to pick up a weapon, hold “E”.  Want to drop the weapon?  You’d think it’s another button but… just… hold “E”!  Want to climb a ladder?  Hold “E”.  You can probably guess you’ll be dropping things sometimes when you want to climb while holding it.  It happens way more than you’d think to the point of annoyance.  Just really uninspired gameplay controls, shameful even.  Oh yeah, want to get in a vehicle?  Hold “F”.  (You thought I was going to say hold “E” right?)
Fights go the way you think.  Just keep hitting that attack button (mouse1) till it tells you to either hold “E” for a special move or repeatedly hit “E” when it doesn’t explicitly say to hold.
When you want to block it’s the other mouse button, but be careful that button also starts the targeting cycle for the shotgun so if you hold it too long you’ll start the targeting cycle for the shotgun leaving yourself exposed for some other enemy to make a swing on and you’ll never block that once the target cycle starts.  Sometimes in fights you'll get into a fight animation with one enemy and another one will start an attack and you can't block because that action doesn't follow the animation you already triggered so you'll get hit.  Happens very frequently if you're on higher difficulty to the point that you'll get killed often by enemies with no way to stop it from happening.
You get the point I hope.  Lots of repeated button mashing and holding like you’re some kind of lowly console user that can't handle more than 4 buttons...
I'd have no problem with it if it allowed more buttons to be used for different tasks.  If "drop weapon/item" wasn't the same as "climb" and if he'd pick up the enemy-dropped items without a 3 second animation that'd be a great start.
I know it's a console port, but dang.  Just so much time wasted in fluff that wouldn't need to be there in a "great game", so it's a "meh" game.

For example, in sub upgrade menus, it will kick you back to the main upgrade menu if you buy something. This is not a problem when changing upgrades already bought. Also a dialog box will appear, telling you, you bought the item you bought, but to make matters worse, it has a short 2 second time preventing you from clicking the close button. These don't sound like a big deal but i'm guessing there are over 100 upgrades, some being purely cosmetic and i doubt you'll be wanting to grabbing these 1 at a time for the most part. There is just stuff like this, which on it's own in another game, you wouldn't dare call padding, but given statements from developer in the past, and how this game plays, you could be that cynical and think you're justified.
Game pauses when you alt-tab, even in loading screen (You might care). With a GTX 970, and I7 4700k i was playing on high preset with i believe bloom and motion blur turned off. I was getting at least 100 FPS most of the time, but there was one area which i saw a constant 50FPS. It wasn't a dip! this was the area itself or possibly some other bottle neck in the system. When you launch the game, When on linux OS, if you aren't using Ubunutu or SteamOS, it will give you a warning that the game isn't optimized for your system (Message can be disabled). I was getting this with latest version of mint, which is based on Ubunutu but as said i was getting 100FPS on high.
Basically, i don't recommend it, but if you've had your eye on it, maybe pick it up as one of your semi-risky but cheep buys. In terms of DLC, they didn't nickle and dime like shadow of mordor which has near universal bad rating for DLC (I hear the expansion DLC is good). It's a solid game, but it's covered in padding, that the developer thinks gamers want.

So I invested over 70+ hours into this game and I bought this game during.....what alpha 15? I remember it was VERY early playable Alpha. If I could give this game over 9000 (teehee) thumbs up, I would. The game is spatacular!!!
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Pros:
-Very well designed Topdown Isometric layout makes creating prisons a ton of fun, enjoyable, and easy!
-Designing prisons is very realistic with daily needs for food, privacy, exercise, and so much more!
-The Steam Workshop at such an early stage of development (I believe Alpha 18!? Don't quote me on that!) makes it that there are a BUNCH of mods you can use to enhance your Prison Architect experience!
-The pacing in game is almost if not perfect, making progression in the game at a pace where you can create your own path; say for example you want to make a new cell block but you also want to increase your security. The game gives you that option that you can go ahead and invest into a new cell block first or increase your force, or you can just create a workshop or two, whichever YOU CHOOSE!

-Prisioners details and stories are absolutely hiliarious; some of which are created by the community.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Cons:

Nothing graphical but the game either crashes and closes out on me, pathfinding is crap, and sometimes you'll put certain items into a room yet it doesn't fulfill the requirements (Example: Cell requires enclosed room, bed, and toilet. They literally wake up on the wrong side of the bed! And this is probably the most frustrating issue I have about this game.
-I may either be just not reading directions right or something, but I can never get execution to work right ever. Maybe I'm doing something wrong when reading the forums or guides but its kind of sad.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Final Verdict: The BEST Prision Simulation out there! 9.5/10

I enjoyed my time with the game.  It wasn't perfect but there were good ideas and it kept me engaged for the first half or so, especially.
So what did I like?  The crisis system was really nice (i.e. combat).  Many of these you can interact with the environment and talk to enemies.  Some are even mostly / all conversation.  Was it perfect, nope.  There were balance issues, skills were a bit lacking and because there aren't very many of these they can be overwhelming, especially early in the game.  The idea was awesome though and I hope to see aspects of this in other games in the future.  I wish they would have added more of these, made them a bigger part of the game and spent more time polishing / balancing them.
The other great thing about this game was the use of skills in conversation.  They come into play in almost every conversation with you actively trying to use them for different / better options.  Also other skills just give more information or possibly new conversation options (i.e. perception).  A good system held back a bit by some other negatives.  It made the conversation much more engaging though.
The other major positive was the setting.  The magic / tech setting isn't my favorite but it was well done and kept me interested inspite of that.
That was the best stuff, the negatives do take away from the above though.  For me, there was just too much reading.  I knew there would be a lot going into it as it was a spirtual successor to Planescape Torment.  I played that way back when and for me that was also a bit too much so I am not exactly the target audience for this.  For the first half, the amount of text was fine.  I was learning about the world and all the extra fluff was sort of needed.  By the end I had kind of had enough.  Some of the text at that point just seemed so out of place.  Why am I reading about some random memories from a not real guy underwater near the climax of the game?
As for the story and overall flow: It was somewhat interesting but became less so as the game progressed, partly due to the out of place text and partly because it just wasn't resolving in a very interesting way for me.  I really felt no sense of climax or excitement as the game reached the later stages.  Just kind of wanted it to hurry up and end.  The ending itself was also a let down.  I didn't find any of the ending to be very rewarding.  Kind of sad for a game that is so story focused.
The other problems didn't bother me much.  Skills were perhaps unbalanced but if you roleplay and don't min/max you may not notice it as much.  The whole skill system has issues as they are a resource.  If you have enough of that resource you can get optimal outcomes, if you don't you get bad results or perhaps can't even continue.  Not the best system but it didn't bother me as much as it seems to have bothered others.  One way they tried to balance this was really nice though, when you rest to recover your pools, time advances and things happen.  Quests may change, people may die, or whatever.  We need more of this in RPG's as well.
Characters were a bit bland, polish was a bit lacking, etc but that didn't detract from the game much for me. I don't care about the broken promises.  Well I do a bit but I am not factoring that into my review at all.  Some seemed justifiable, some not so much.  Read other reviews if you care about those.
Even with the sizeable negatives, I still found it a worthwhile game though.  It won't go down as a classic, but if you are out of RPG's to play and you don't mind a game focused on reading it may be worth a buy.  7/10

If you want an oldschool PC rpg  rather go for the excellent Pillars or Eterniy or even the remastered Icewind Dales or Baldur Gate's, or the true Planescape: Torment.

I'm a big fan of Planescape: Torment and really waited for this game to come out since it was announced four years ago. I spent two months trying to wade through the walls of text that usually bored me to tears. 30+ hours within 2+ months -- that should give you some idea about how boring and disappointing this game is. There are more detailed reviews to be found here and I usually agree with the negative ones. Long story short: the plot is at most okayish and unsuccessfully attempts to copy/mimick the original Torment, combat is absolutely horrible, Tides do next to nothing, the overall difficulty level is ridiculously low, companions are hard to care about (Rhin being an exception), descriptions are boring and excessive, and inXile just pooped on their backers by going back on their crowdfunding promises. If you want to play something that can actually be called a Planescape: Torment successor, play Neverwinter Nights 2: Mask of the Betrayer. I definitely won't buy anything from inXile Entertainment anymore, and I would request a refund if I could. This is not the Torment I've been waiting for for years. You had the money, you had as much time as you needed, and you still failed to deliver the game you promised to RPG fans all over the world. Shame on you inXile.

The character design selections are limited, and the art style of your Dadsona doesn't match the art in the rest of the game, but these are things you stop noticing because the stories just draw you in. Even the dads you think you won't like (Brian) will wind up surprising you in the end. They're all so wonderful, and the journeys they take you on are full of heartbreak, laughter, and twue love.
It's not a particularly challenging game, but it's fun, and there are several minigames throughout for those who like skill challenges. I highly recommend it.

The thing about this game is that it's an adaption of a choose-your-own-story adventure book. As such, there's not much "gameplay" - it's literally just clicking the mouse to advance text boxes and select options. And after you've played through the whole thing as each character once or twice, a lot of the game becomes pretty repetitive. But if you're a Shakespeare fanatic or someone who's read Hamlet before and likes playing games, To Be or Not To Be is definitely for you. I liked Hamlet because it was utterly absurd, and TBoNTB allows you to both rationaly resolve the situation and take the ridiculousness of the original play to a whole other level.
TL;DR: If you've read Hamlet at least once before, love choose-your-own-adventure novels, and have a silly sense of humor, this is the game for you!

is the video game version of Ryan North's chose-your-own-adventure novel,
as a parody version of William Shakespeare's
. Aside utilizing the names and events of the original storyline for a setting - and paraphrasing the book now and then - this is nothing even slightly close to the original work. If you have never read or watched the play, I strongly recommend doing so before venturing into this cheesy spoof.
I've always been a bit of a fan for chose-your-own-adventure format, exploring various courses of actions and their consequences presented for a singular story. I basically grew up reading them, playing on the notion of a choice action. Also becoming a fan of Shakespeare's all works as my age and experience in English language progressed enough for me to appreciate them; this game felt like a natural choice for me. Well... this wasn't what I expected.
As the narration starts, you are given the opportunity to play the game as Hamlet, Ophelia or Hamlet Sr. a.k.a. King of Denmark, exploring 110 various parody paths and their endings harboring cringe and insult comedy, narrated in modern slang mostly. It's a cute and imaginative game to spare some mindless time with, sure but nothing exceptionally rich I must say. You start playing the game with a silent smirk on your face, scoffing now and then, deepening that smirk into a smile. It has its almost hilarious moments too, mostly presented in situational comedy through written narrative.  It works for 2-3 playthroughs. Yet, as you keep playing and keep witnessing the same kind of shallow remarks for the 30th time, the game quickly loses its charm.
I must confess that the humor presented here was not my cup of tea. It is mostly rough parody and elementary satire, downright underrating the brilliance of the original author by taking crude logic and blatant exaggeration as its weapons. It's not a traditional or psychological reading of the concept. It's an absurd and cheesy parody of the norms of the era, story path choices, gender representations, free-will itself and character interrelations. The relationship between the player and the narrator is somewhat of a semblance to
with the narrator constantly criticizing you, intervening with your choices and rearranging actions to fit into prearranged storyline format, and doing so while belittling your sentience mostly. Some of the scenes presented - like the naval war between Hamlet's fleet and pirates - are imaginative and entertaining; but most scenes end up being direct hits on the original play with American sitcom humor.
I am aware that I've mostly presented downsides, but would I recommend the game as a final verdict? Meh, why not if it's in a heavy sale and you'd feel like watching Ophelia going on a killing spree, Hamlet time travelling or King of Denmark exploring the bottom of the sea. It is cute, but that effect doesn't last. There is nothing to actually dislike in the game. Narrative dynamic functions fine and the author obviously knows his Shakespeare enough to criticize
in to this extent. This whole thing is a matter of taste. I'll refuse to downvote it for the sake of creative spark it contains. It should be some labor to write 110 different endings to begin with.

which begins  your Shakespearean adventure to attempt to kill your evil Uncle Claudius while fighting pirates, time travelling, becoming a ninja, playing death chess, having a singalong with a gravedigger, oh and turning yourself into a trout. (And you can have some stew in the mean time, and lots of making out, if you want)
I'm a huge fan of "Choose Your Own Adventure" stories, I've studied and read Shakespeare's
and I'm a big fan of Ryan North's witty and snarky sense of humor. Put all that together and you have "To Be or Not To Be".  In this game, you play as either Hamlet, Ophelia (BEST CHARACTER BY THE WAY), or Hamlet Sr (Yes, a ghost).  The premise is simple, read along and make choices and create your own version of Hamlet. With so many choices, and some  cringingly awesome puns, you control the fate of your character and his/her kin.  The gameplay is fun, although, I wouldn't recommend it to someone who doesn't enjoy reading or appreciate Ryan North's brand of humor (snarky, sarcastic, and nerdy).  Also, it can get a bit pedantic, so I also wouldn't recommend trying another story immediately after beating it the first time. While the gameplay doesn't have much artwork, like in a visual novel, certain plot elements allows you to unlock pieces of artwork create by a variety of webcomic artists.  Music is charming but a bit repetitive and there is great narration (which you can turn on or off).
It's a great game, but not necessarily for everyone; if you like to make your adventures with a nice dosage of nerdy humor, definitely pick up this game in  a sale.

Everyone who is wondering if they should buy this game. everything will be in this Review.
WHAT IS THIS GAME
This is a game where you play as an Agent known as 47 who has been tasked to eliminate targets in the most efficent
and discreet way as possible.
STYLE OF GAME
Starting it off is if its worth the money. we can find this out by looking at some of the key features of the game and how they play. firstly this is a Stealth game with Assasination mechanics that allow you to use a vast variety of objects to murder your target. i believe the general stealth and kill mechanic is great and i can only see improving it by adding more ways to murder or move hostile NPC's such as if your higher rank then them make it so you can tell them to leave the nearby location. this would allow for more core gameplay Mechanics. secondly this game is also set in a semi-freeroam environment for you to explore and find secrets and other ways to murder your target.  Sadly this game cannot be a dream for stealth loving viewers as it comes with a few catches. firstly it is an Online DRM game that you can only play online. this means you cannot play the game if your on a journey. secondly thisg ame is Episodic which is arguebly good and bad reasons but i agree on the bad as it shows the developers got tired of this game being in development and released it before it is supposed to be. this has annoyed many fans which is one of the main reasons of the mixed Reviews. I would just like to add that the AI is dreadfully daft on this game if you go gun nuts. such as if you shoot into a crowd they will just duck and scream or do nothing. i managed to shoot the target in a room with a dozen people and walk straight out. completing the mission. i thought the AI would play a huge toll on the game but the AI is smart enough to feel immersed in this universe.
GAMEMODES
There are 2 main gamemodes. Contracts and Target. Target is the classic hitman style go in and come out with your contracts killed.  The Contract mode grants you to decide who will be the hit and challenge online players and friends to try and take on your level. this is one of the reasons for ONLINE DRM.
LEVELING SYSTEM
The leveling system grants you to bring weapons onto the field with you. the better you do on the Missions EG Minimum casualties and Maximum challenges completed. Your gain Levels to allow you to bring fun toys into the map. Suprisingly these weapons can be helpful but usually they are not as any gun or weapon that causes harm to enemies will probably make it harder to level up.
FINAL VERDICT
I would give this game a 7/10. this game is an extremely fun game with great stealth mechanics and constant feedback on their game, aswell as following the old routes of the game and allowing a more open terrain rather then the linear game before this. however things like Dumb AI and Online DRM drags this game away from a 9/10. I would reccomend this game for anyone who is a Hitman fan or likes the stealth genre

Apart from the community aspect, the mod builds on the already present lightsaber combat adding a block and different styles to fight with.
The customization is very fun to play around with as I was just an hour ago, running around as Count Dooku with dual pink lightsabers yelling "YOU WERE THE CHOSESN ONE" at the top of my lungs.
This all being said, if you're wanting a fun story, play the original game on single player.
If you're wanting a multiplayer experience, get MBII and be ready to tinker around with the game when it decides to break!
In all I will reccomend this game although it can be a pain at times!

The game was amazing in the first couple of hours, but then it got repetitive fast. Although you may see positive feedback that says "it doesn't matter" you should still think twice before buying Mad Max. I didn't finnish the game because of repetitiveness and cons below. Simply put I got bored clearing all the areas.
Pros:
+ Combat is really neat and has variety
+ Game sounds, especially when you get the V12 (although there can be minor glitches in sound world)
+ Car customization
+ Excitement at the beginning (speed pursuits, fights generally)
Cons:
- Repetitive especially when clearing all the zones (and there are lots to clear)
- Even though your car is customized to the max the lower enemy cars can keep up with you which is annoying
- Minefield clearing is absolutely boring and you can't fight the enemy cars the way like with your main car (because you need to clear them with special car)
- Unlockable cars don't have anything special on them
It may seem like cons are minor things in Mad Max, but they are constant when playing the game and were major to me. The gameplay is designed the way that you should first do the main quests and then clear everything. If you do latter first, you can get the best car parts but some quests still require worse car parts which were also annoying. If you dont mind repetitiveness and can cope with the cons I suggest you get the game when it is in discount.

This game allows you to build a prison in any form or shape you want and then house the criminal elements of the state for the duration of their sentence. You can be strict and keep your inmates on a short leash. Constantly watching their every move and disturbing their nightly sleep with shakedowns and routine searches. Alternatively you can create a prison where it isn't actually all that bad to spend the next eight years. A place where inmates may work or go to school. A prison where your prisoners get good meals and loads of free time. The choice is yours.
Your goal in the game of course is to earn money through your intake of new prisoners to make room for even more prisoners. You need to avoid the 'avoidable' deaths and preferably avoid anyone escaping your prison before their time has been served. Eventually though you probably feel that you have a pretty lean prison with no easy way out and this is when you test out your prison in the escape mode.
Once you get into the shoes of an inmate, having to navigate the prison halls that you built, you suddenly get a feeling of how secure your prison actually is.
I found that my first prison, one that I was extremely proud of until this point, was far from secure and I could basically trick myself out through the front door and then just make a run for it. I made some tweaks but in the end I decided to start over. My second prison was created with my own escape attempt in mind and I tried to prevent all the things that I had managed to do when I escaped from the last one. I still haven't managed to get out... Don't let the Five Nights at Freddy's branding scare you - this is a FNAF game in title only. It's not the same reskinned formula with a couple new gimicks (@FNAF 1-3) nor is it a confusing and all around boring mess where the mechanics make no sense (@FNAF 4). This game is altogether a new experience. Even with just ten minutes dedicated to the game, that's easy to tell. You crawl through vents, you have complete control over where your character looks, and the game sees an all around boost in quality. There's at least a couple of voice actors, some charming humor, and the series all around re-establishes itself as the gold standard for horror. The only suggestion I can really give here is this: Scott, please stop while you're ahead. I want to see you remembered as an influential horror developer who helped to reinvent the genre. That's what we saw in FNAF 1 and 2, and it was shining through the cracks in 3. When we got FNAF 4, there was a slight groan, and it frankly didn't feel like a new game. When we got FNAF World, a top down RPG special only for its controversy, it didn't release to the acclaim of the other series entries, because people were slowly but surely getting sick of the franchise. When the FNAF book launched, it wasn't difficult to see that you were jumping the shark. Now, with the FNAF movie on its way out, I just wish you would... move on. This series was great. It made its mark on the world of video gaming and I just want it to leave that mark there, not cover it in scratches. You have something good. Please keep it that way and move onto new projects. I eagerly await the next Scott Cawthon game, but I can only hope that it's not Five Nights at Freddy's.
EDIT: Here I am, a couple hours into the game. It definitely gets better as you go. This one's worth checking out.

Ok... APB Reloaded is a peculiar game. It's fun and completely awful all at the same time. The most controversial aspect of this game is it's usage of the Free-to-play model, a significant change from it's original incarnation as a subscription based game. However, this model always begs the question: Do you actually have to pay money to play this game against other paying players? In this case, the answer is unfortunately a resounding "Yes!!!" Using in-game money received from beating missions (which I have significant issues, as you'll read momentarily) only unlocks weapons for 10 days. Additionally, not all weapon types are available for purchase using the in-game money. Some of the most powerful weapons in the game (the OCA "Whisper," for example) are only available for purchase using G1 credits -- otherwise known as real money. This type of F2P model is horribly unattractive to me. If you offer a game for free, don't restrict the fun to the people that play.

I just wanted to give this a recommendation but honestly I cant
I started playing this game this year in april and has quickly become my favourite game
But It only has become my favourite game because of the little rare good things that can happen to you in this game
I almost always play this game solo so I have been through it all, from 1v10ing zergs to 1v2s and much more
Although i admit, the game makes it fun the way the maps are generated differently and all of that it just wastes tooo much of your time
If you want a game that you can play all day non stop, then this is it
But if you are going to play any amount less than that then it is definitely not going to be fun
Now are the PROS and CONS
PROS::
The wipe days of this game.
Now I will admit, the most fun I have had on this game is when everyone is equal with bows and other low tier gear and everyone is fighting and getting bases down. The wipe days are the most fun and rewarding, but also the most likely to make you rage quit or just delete the game.
The hapis map
Now this is just my opinion, but I will say that the hapis map,(or atleast the old one) is where some of the non toxic and the most enjoyable people are. I will say that about half my hours are hours on the hapis map, because when I just started out the game I knew it was the easiest map to get started. In all my map wipes I have met at least  1 nice person that I have become friends with(and this was when I had about 50 hours). It has some of the noobiest players with the worst aim, just like all of us when we started out.
Constant development and updates
EVERY single thursday there is an update. Now I know that the updates arnt always big or exiting, but that means that the devs care about this game and want it to keep running. They also listen to the community and even have MASSIVLY helped new players over the months. When I started rust I kept on trying to eat the seed because they said they were edible and now the new players even know what to get, what to hit and not to hit and the descriptions are a MASSIVE help
CONS::
The massive waste of your time
Now if you want to spend all of your time on a new and entertaining game, then this is the game for you. But if you want to casually want to spend about an hour a day on this game then please DO NOT get this game. Sometimes you will be spending hours just to die with all of your stuff that you need to make a base and will have to restart,( has happened to me multiple times).
The community
Now with an exeption of a few servers, almost all the servers I have been on I have had a toxic encounter with at least on person. I am not saying all people are bad, in fact I have met a few people who have become good friends with me. But I have had WAYYY more bad encounters than good in this game
Zergs
What is a zerg? A massive group of people with low skill count who target lesser groups for raiding or harrassment. Joining a zerg is like joining a ctf map on tf2, very very easy. Zergs are like texas, where everything is bigger
The fps and lag
Now I have a $1000 laptop that can run csgo in 120 fps, overwatch in 90 fps, tf2 in 150 fps and other games that have meduim graphic needs I can run fairly well. And even though I have a decent pc. I can only run this game at about 60 fps. Sometimes on 2x or 4x servers my fps can go down to 45-50. Also in game whenever yu render a base on two, the screen stops and rubberbands you a couple seconds back, and in some cases that could mean death for you. Now I get it that the devs are working on garbage collection right now, but tell me, shouldnt they have a game that most people can run before they add anything else?
END:::

Put about 20 hours into Football Tactics so far, I'm about ~40% done achievement wise and played through 5 seasons so far.
The game is very promising, there is a glimmer of what could be a very good tactics game, unfortunately, it's a pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥ football game. The AI is very binary, and with the RNG dice rolls and the way the AI gets players makes the game inherently unfair. For example;
My last game the opposing team had a Goalkeeper with ~90 defence and one Striker with ~65 Accuracy. The rest of their team was awful and did not impact on the team at all. As my Strikers are ~40-50 Accuracy and my Goalkeeper is ~50 defence, no matter how I attacked it was impossible to score, no matter how their team attacked it was impossible for them not to score. Result, 6-0 loss.
This is further exasperated by the AI. The AI knows that the Striker will score every shot. This means every turn for the AI consists of 2 passes to that striker, and a shot from max range that will always score. That's right, their League 3 Striker scored
Add to this a lack of crossing or headers, defenders moving one square only (no wing backs in this game...) there are no actual football tactics in this football game. Nearly every match relies on using your best passer to play down the middle to your best striker, score. Reset, do the same again.
I've seen matches where both myself and the AI can score in 3 moves from kick off, lots of 6-6 or 7-7 draws etc. in this game.
The way the RNG works can also lead to massive swings. Whatever the stat is for your player is the max they can roll. So if you have a defender with 25 defence they will roll a D25 for every action, if the Striker has 50 Accuracy they will roll a D50. The Striker is almost guaranteed to win every dice roll.
The skill system is obtuse and doesn't always seem to trigger, a lack of defensive options (Pressing and ending the turn seemingly has zero affect on the AI), AI bonuses leading to whichever 3 teams were relegated nearly always winning the league by huge margins and a lack of management simulation, I really can't recommend the game. The training and sim systems are particularly bad, with players being sold/bought on a whim without needing to go to a team, you can't choose what to train your players in (skills are randomly allocated) and a lack of any real management beyond buying some one shot upgrades for bonus exp.
To finish up fully, I could see myself needing to grind for 20-25 seasons slowly leveling up players.
Every draw and loss has a chance to lose you fans and reduce your income on a weekly basis.
Avoid unless they make significant changes.

I must say that I enjoy playing this, but I'm a fan of the franchise, so by that account I can only recommend it to fans that are willing to put up with all the flaws, and if you were a fan, odds are you have already picked it up. Thereby lies the problem. I simply can't recommend this to everyone else. Maybe once all episodes have come out and a physical copy is released, but still then maybe wait for it to go on sale.
Everyone else has already pointed out the big flaws like online requirements to progress and fully enjoy and many other.
This summer they have chosen to release some bonus content for some of the already released episodes (Sapienza and Marrakesh) giving you a whole new experience in playing those, when I first heard about this I thought that everyone that had purchased the individual episodes would get that episodes individual bonus for free, but alas. They have chosen to make a bundle of the bonus content with a coming third bonus for a future map. When that comes you will have to buy the bonus bundle to gain access, thus missing out on this content until that day comes, unless you are amongst those that have bought the Full Exp. or the Intro + Upgrade (which is the Full Exp. basically). This means that this is basically DLC and not part of the main game (main story), which the devs said they weren't going to do.
I was and still am, liking the episodic release as I think it actually suits Hitman, as he travels from place to place. But this is a first for developer IO Interactive, and they are having a lot of 'infant' problems adjusting and so is every consumer, as in the beginning there isn't really any content at all, and even by now, after the release of the 3rd of 6 levels (episodes), it still feels like there's missing content. Maybe eventually when it's completed (Season 1) and released physically in January 2017, there'll be content for consideration. Although they have said that if they see it as a success, then there'll come a Season 2 (probable released over the course of 2017). Mind you this has only 6 levels (plus 2 tutorials) which is literally half or less than previous Hitman titles, but again I think that they have tried to do a good job of making it so that you would want to play the same levels again and again. But as everything else you can encounter levels which just doesn't do it for you which then turns them into boring and tedious, trying to unlock all content from them.
Contracts Mode also seems bareboned. I didn't really like Absolution, but of what I've read, the Contracts mode in that game (where it was introduced) has a lot more features. Which again makes this Hitmans Contract mode odd since this is a upgraded version of the Absolution engine, so they shouldn't really that big of a problem transfering it over, or maybe they have, but that's not how it seems from the outside. But if dev studios were a little more transparent and better at communicating then things could've been a lot better.
I also feel that although it looks great and plays great most of the time, it just still feels of compared to earlier Hitman titles. I've never really understood when you're making the 3rd, 4th or 5th game in a franchise, how a sequel can take a step back regarding certain aspects which makes up some of the core gameplay. Shouldn't you try to up yourself each time or atleast keep what already work, instead of scrapping and trying to reimagine/rebuild a system for a new "audience", thus♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off the fanbase.
Overall this is and should have been a AAA title, but feels like a big Indie title.
EDIT: Positive Score as it's now complete and bonus for IOI to go independent.

Years ago, I worked in a prison... Northern nevada Correction Center and Warm Springs Correctional Center located in Carson City Nevada. That being said, a few games have come out over the years trying to emulate running a prison. Prison Tycoon 1 & 2 were the first that I tried. Both failed miserably. This game has a long way to go, but it is trying... improving... and actually comes close. Riots, gang wars, contraband, escapes and even a death row. Real rehabilitation, if there is such a thing. Not all inmates go back to prison whatever the reason.
This game is evolving, getting better and feels real on some levels.
A critical review should be just that, critical. So while I give this game a thumbs up, it is not perfect. It has bugs, Some new, some old, but many are recognized and others have been fixed. The developers are working to improve it both in game play and fixing that which is broken. I have not seen a game breaking bug.
An active community of posted prisons and mods, the spread of ideas and again active developers have made this game more real than it's predicessors and a bit fun.
My 1 suggestion is to add race tension. Race wars are alive and well in the US prisons. Segregation could be implemented as it is in many prisons. However, Gangs do add an interesting aspect that mimic this, but recruitment is rampant in prisons and should be added as well. Gun towers, a better way to implement sally ports (1 door can not open until the other closes, linking doors together in some way of added user defined rules) and so forth. How about a bit of staff corruption? All of this would make the game more real, challenging and fun.

I keep learning from other's prisons, and thinking of more ideas on how to make my prison better...
Although, I have gotton a riot because my power station exploded because the water pump broke,

It could be my own personal biases, but this game really resonates with me. It's a choose your own adventure book, revamped and updated with a shiny digital interface, achievements, and cards. It takes an esoteric subject matter banished to the wasteland of high school English courses, Hamlet, and asks the player to simply reconsider what they remembered.
"Perhaps Hamlet had been hit with Gamma Radiation and turned into a green killing machine anytime he got angry?"
"Didn't Ophelia have a thing for science? No no, I'm sure left to her own devices, she'd have created a death ray, right?"
"How big a thing was dripping poison in someone's ear really? I mean, that's actually a thing right? like ghosts?"
I love this game; it's a bold attempt to pay homage to one of the pillars of English literature, while not taking itself seriously at all. It's the game equivalent of bringing your nerdy friend with a Masters Degree in English Literature to a party, and after some drinking, asking them “so, what did you –really- think of Shakespeare?” The resultant pandemonium as they work out ever semi-coherent grievance is an ambrosia.
Pure gold.

Torment: Tides of Numenara is the spiritual successor of Planescape: Torment, which is probably my favourite cRPG of all time. Tides of Numenara did not give me the "wow" feeling I had at the end of Planescape: Torment, but I cannot hold that against it too much as it is a high standard to compare to. The game did leave me amused, bemused, and with a vague dissatisfied curiousity that makes me want to play it again to see how my choices exactly impacted results.
I liked the story. The introduction did a decent job of outlining the edges of the plot and left me with enough curiousity to want to figure out more. Initially I was a bit surprised at the limited options in character generation but as the story quickly explains what you are, that design choice fit in its proper place. At the start he game places you in a sizable city to explore, filled with interesting NPCs (including all possible companions) but perhaps more importantly, objects: the Numenara. Numenara is a catch-all term for artifacts from previous worlds, the Ninth World you play through is a civilization built on the remnants of older civilizations and as a result the world is filled with barely understood objects that are useless, entertaining, and/or outright dangerous.
The build-up and culmination of the story had its interesting moments, and it is clear the designers went for a final encounter similar to Planescape: Torment, where what you had learned and discovered during your gameplay mattered more than having a good combat character capable of doing a grand bossfight. As a consequence the game leans far more on Intellect skills and challenges than it does on Speed or Might, which is also reminiscent of PS:T, where having high Intellect and Wisdom stats brought out far more story, choices, and non-combat resolutions. However, it seemed a little lacklustre overall, especially regards to the Tides, which are an important plot point and also a "stat" type that you earn points in. I ended up with dominant Gold and Blue tides (the altruistic and knowledge tides respectively) but it seldomly seemed to do anything. Similarly the unique Tidal Affinity skill for the main character was barely ever used and left me wondering what the point of the Tides was. It seemed to function mostly as an alignment meter which a game like this really does not need, being constantly engaged in the story I can do my own morality tracking perfectly well.
Story, after all, is the main point of this game, it's definitely not the combat. This point is driven home by the game's term "crisis" instead of "combat", and while you can definitely fight, a crisis typically can be resolved without much or any fighting as well. Adding to that that combat is *really really easy*, if you are looking for an RPG with good fights, don't pick this one. I barely ever used any cyphers (one-shot "magic items"), even the exceedingly powerful ones, as there was just no reason to. Focusing characters for a task quickly left them so completely overpowered with nearly constant 100% success rates on anything they attempted, without using much or any Might/Speed/Intellect points, that each crisis was a breeze (except the one the Sorrow was involved in), each skilltest succesful, consumables saved, and sleep never needed.
Companions were... frankly a little disappointing. While it is clear that attention has been paid to make each character unique and have a background story, the stories never really came to life. You can ask them about their backgrounds and you get some information, if you say/do things they like you can get more information, and they have a sidequest of some sort related to their stories for you to resolve, but nothing seems to happen in the game because of it, just the "end-game slides" likely tell a different epilogue depending on what you do. In PS:T your companions became more powerful and developed new abilities if you helped them which was a clearly felt impact, I can't help but feel that in T:ToN they dropped the ball on this. PS:T's companions also had some sort of relation to the protagonist that made you feel connected to them, in T:ToN, this is mostly absent as well. Of the companions I chose (Aligern, Tybir and Erritis) only Aligern had some history with "me", Tybir was just some random guy I got a quest from and Erritis is a hero (Really. Just ask him) so he came along to adventure.
Last bit to mention is the Merecasters. Merecasters result in stories within the story that you play through, and they were the only times in the game I was genuinely bored. They are like little interactive books, depending on your choice made (or the succes/failure of a skill) you get told what happens on the next page. Some of these were interesting and important to the plot but most seemed to have minor impact or felt entirely pointless, so rather than improve immersion they left me feeling rather detached while resolving their mini-arcs. Especially given that halfway through the game some minutes of playtime are reserved purely for understanding the impact of your choices using the Merecasters, including rather heavy-handedly inserting the main question of the game "What is a life worth?" in this process, the Merecasters might as well have been called Meh-casters.
Conclusion: Despite its flaws which we can hope will be improved on in future patches, I greatly enjoyed Tides of Numenara. The world is beautifully crafted, there are lots of small things that make it feel alive (like interesting non-critical NPCs and objects), gameplay mechanics are adequate. While it falls short of the amazement that was Planescape: Torment, if you are looking for a decent story-driven game, definitely give it a try.

TL DR: I Tides of Numenera isn't terrible but not good either, and only worth on a VERY deep discount. Awful combat and UI and a really bland story don't really make this worth buying at more than 5€.
Torment: Tides of Numenera is the spiritual successor to Planescape: Torment, a classic mixing RPG and adventure game, and the finest game I've ever read (That's not a mistake.) In Tides you explore a weird world through exploration and text through the eyes of a protagonist trying to remember countless past lives, just like its predecessor. But Tides is much, much inferior, and even if didn't have any association with Torment I'd probably still be giving it a negative review.
Let's start with the basics, since the bloody game can't even seem to get that right. Tides is a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥to interact with. When you order your party to walk they take some time to turn around and start walking because they just had to have some sort of """realistic""" animation. Interacting with characters and items takes a bit for the text window to slide up, and every time you choose a text response there's also a sliding animation. Overall the game feels sluggish to interact with for really no reason. The UI is also pretty bad, with terrible use of space. Also, no inventory sorting option. This is especially bad since this game uses Pillars of Eternity tech, and that game didnt' have such basic issues.
On to less basic things. Tides doesn't have a combat system, as the equivalent of combat ingame is called a Crisis, and may or may not include two action point combat. This is an interesting concept with terrible execution. The few Crises I participated in (not many since I avoided combat as much as I could, but certain events do force you into Crises) usually consist of large numbers of enemies (sometimes even spawning more every turn!) and you have to either kill them all, run, or do "something else". You can usually interact with items and even talk to some people in the middle of these events, but the thing here is the same sluggishness seen in overall interacting with anything is seen here. If you want to be efficient with your turns and run the max distances possible you often need to wait several times for the game to display the distance you can walk (using only 1 movement point) by hovering the mouse pointer on the floor. Why they couldn't just make it always show the path is beyond me. Apart from that you have large numbers of enemies which means waiting for their excruciatingly slow animations to complete. There's magic, weapons and cyphers (very powerful items that you can only use once) but this is so♥♥♥♥♥♥easy I never used any cyphers and barely did anything in combat except run around passing skill checks.
Which leads us to yet another issue, skill checks. Tides has several skills and three attributes, Might, Speed and Intellect. Your actions always have a probability to occur based on your skill in that action (think of this as every action having a "miss chance"), and spending points in the corresponding attribute allows you to increase the "hit chance". By levelling you can also get Edges on the different attributes, which are like a free point of that attribute in every check you make. The thing here is that in most dialogue interactions you can use your companions' skills/edges to pass them. And almost all interactions where you can't are Intellect ones, which means that as long as you have high INT and edges on your main character and the other stats in your companions you almost can't fail at any check, which defeats the purpose of having skill checks in the first place! Apart from that, like Planescape and KOTOR2, this also means that being a high-INT character is the sole way of playing this game without locking yourself out of content. The nano ("mage class"), apart from benefitting from high INT the most, also has a Scan Thoughts ability which is actually fairly interesting in some cases, and what I'm saying here is: Play a nano if you're playing this game. Of course, if you have played PS:T before you were already going to, I assume.
But why I am I whining about combat and skill checks on a Torment game? I mean, what about exploration, story, companions, writing? Well... This isn't too good either. The game starts off and in about 30 minutes you already know the main antagonist and who you are. "What is mystery?" -Tides writers. Too much of the dialogue is questions on lore so you can get your dose of expostion, or overly elaborated descriptions. The writers seemed to make extensive use of a thesaurus to discover words that no one uses to use in descriptions, but they failed to look up the definition of "brevity" in a dictionary. There are two interesting companions, but otherwise they're fairly bland. PS:T has a floating skull, a guy who is permanently on fire and wants to burn the Multiverse, a succubus who swore a vow of chastity, etc. Tides has 6 humans. ...yeah. They don't feel unique even in their way of talking as Dak'kon or Morte did, and neither do the normal people in the Ninth World. This game is set on an Earth a thousand million years into the future where humanity has returned and everyone is mixed race because of countless years of different races reproducing, but people speak pretty much modern English with a few different words. Overall this feels like writers padding out text to accomplish a 1.2 million wordcount, which is dumb as ♥♥♥♥.
Exploring the world is already kind of annoying due to how sluggish it is, but due to the amount of exposition dumps there are it sometimes feels as if you're in a museum reading the plaques next to an exhibition instead of talking to people in a world. There are a few interesting bits throughout (the last area does get a bit more interesting) but there's barely any non-Crisis gameplay other than talking to people and fetching stuff. You could say PS:T suffers from this as well but the thing is PS:T has adventure game-like puzzles. Tides either doesn't have them or they're so brainlessly easy it doesn't really matter. All you get here is a Museum of Weird Futuristic♥♥♥♥♥♥without much content. The best part of the game is preobably meres, which are short text adventures where you can live part of the life on another person. Some of them are pretty fun little adventures, but they're a fairly small part of the game. The sound doesn't really contribute to exploration as even though the music is fairly nice, the ambient soundscape is mostly barren, where the original had sounds of crowds chatting in cities to liven up the atmosphere.
I barely talked about the main story, but it's nothing to write home, or Steam, about. They have a "big question" like in the original ("What does one life matter?" instead of "What can change the nature of a man?") but the moment it is asked it just feels really underwhelming, since the game doesn't really touch the theme much. There's an alignment system (the titular Tides) but for all the devs talked about it, it's really underdeveloped. With certain conversations you get an increase in one or two of the Tides and... yeah. They affect some things like part of the ending but that's it. This is the "magical reason why people follow you around" (like you being the incarnation of torment who attracts other tormented beings in PS:T) but it's barely touched upon. The game is also fairly short and this seems to have been a very badly mismanaged project as the sheer amount of cut content from Kickstarter promises seem to indicate. From what I've heard this isn't like you can only experience only part of the content each playthrough, so it's just short.
Watching the Early Glimpse on inXile's Youtube channel left me with one question: "How could you ♥♥♥♥ up this much?!" But hell I can massage an alien's sphincter to open it up and crawl inside. 10/10 GOTY right here, guys.

Disclaimer: I was one of the original backers for this game.
In my opinion Torment: Tides of Numenera is a great narrative focused CRPG on its own. Instead of trying to figure out the best character creation combination for my char (as I would do in a game like Pillars of Eternity), I could just pick what I liked and do not get punished for it later on. Playing a conversation focused character does not put you at a disadvantage here.
Writing in the game is more world-building focused as it is character focused, so expect a lot of lore and some references to Planescape: Torment. If you read carefully you often can figure out quite a lot about a place's past, a future game section to come up soon or multiple viewpoints on the solution of a quest. In hindsight I must say the connection to the original PST could have been both bane and blessing of this game, while it ensured the game's funding it also is the most reoccuring point of criticism in reviews here. I think some of that criticism is justified while the majority is not. What it revealed most for me is that most people did not really know what they wanted from this game in the first place OR wanted something much closer to PST than just a spiritual successor. Although I have to acknowledge that neither gameplay nor writing in the game are without its flaws. The main plot or the lack in race diversity among the companions are examples where there indeed could have been better solutions in my opinion.
I recommend this game despite its flaws, but I also see why a game like Pillars of Eternity can please a much broader audience, while this here is a very niche product. I don't consider this game too short, I spend about 20 hours just questing and reading in the first hub. If you like worldbuilding and lots of lore, this game is for you. The Numenera world is no PST but I think it's still interesting to explore. However, if you primarily enjoy combat in CRPGs, don't buy this game as the combat is quite basic and optional in most of the game.

THIS is the football manager game for people who don't understand football manager games, or for people who really don't know (or care) a lot about football even!  It's a manager game for people who have little patience for poring over the big spreadsheet-management games that the pros play and who don't want to be swamped by stats and the minutiae of skill points typically found in the bigger games in this genre.  This is manager-LITE!
Very easy - you can literally jump right in and play from the start with the very simple tutorial.  The game is mostly point-and-click.  Stats screens are few and simple.  The management functions are very basic but effective.  Best of all, you don't need to know the first thing about football (soccer to our American friends).  You can do pretty much everything that you can do in a full-blown management sim, except it's all very simplified and lightweight here.  Fans of full management games will probably not enjoy this one at all, but for those of us who could never master the bigger games, this one is perfect!
You start out by either selecting a pre-existing team (it seems quite a few countries are supported) or you can create your own team.  I picked my local town's team and found myself starting out in the lowest amateur league.  If you choose to create your own team, there is a superb player editor where you can (hope to) emulate your favourite players' faces in the creator screen if you have that kind of patience.  Once you have your team, there are no numbers to play with at this stage, so it is a case of starting your first match.  You can watch, simulate or actually play the match yourself.  Playing is easy and turn-based: click on a player, choose one of his available moves, then click to execute the move.  You get three moves per turn, and then it's your opponent's turn.  Everything is demonstrated in a simple, hands-on tutorial.   If you don't want to play and prefer to stick with team progression only, you can simply watch the game instead.  However, I found playing the match to be a lot of fun.
If you win, you'll accrue both fame points and cash with which you can upgrade your team, your club and your stadium.  You can manage contracts and recruit new players, and there is a basic screen to play with tactics.  Again, it's all very simple.
Simplicity!  Everything is so clean and nicely presented.  No fussy user interface, everything displaying context descriptions when hovered over with the pointer, and every part of the game very simple to play, requiring no knowledge of football as a sport, or of manager games generally.  The graphics use a fun art style that I found to be quirky and amusing, and the few tables of stats were simple and self-explanatory.  A real joy to people who have no patience (like me...)!
My only disappointment is that, in creating a team, I cannot opt for a female team instead.  That's a bit nit-picky, but the excellent graphics style would easily have accommodated female players too - something I would have loved.  Other than that, everything is great for this level of casual game.
I've lost count of how many football-manager games I've bought and then not played over the years.  This one is basic enough for people who don't have patience for the bigger management games.  While it's definitely at the 'casual' end of the gaming spectrum, it's one of those lightweight games that hits a perfect balance between simplicity and the fun (and addictiveness) of a management-genre game.  If you're like me and have found the big-name footie management games a bit too much of a chore or trial to understand, then this game is for you.
Recommended!

Skills are taught via the "coaches notes" which pretty much show you a screenshot of the skill as well as a little bit of text.
Videos, demonstrations, etc would have been much more helpful. It wasn't until I started to watch simulated games and saw how the AI used the skills of my players did I finally understand them.
And then I realized just how OP the skills are. Cannon shot, olympic kick, and rainbow feint are absolutely ridiculous. One of my guys, a low level forward, was able to use rainbow feint to not only get past 2 defenders but also through the goalkeeper for an incredibly easy, and unsatisfying goal.
Olympic kick allows the corner kick guy to shoot directly into the goal. It works 99% of the time.
The only way to protect yourself from these skills is to have defensive skills but these are extremely rare and can still fail. This works for the computer as well and it was how I was able to quickly dominate and reach 1st place of the Ukrainian Premier League fairly quickly despite only having a team with a 3-star rating and most of my opponents having 4.5 stars.
Currently, the game lacks depth and strategy. Every match is almost the same. After kick off, I pass to my forward, he gets into position and attempts to score. The shot is either deflected, caught, or goes in. Then the opponent does the same thing, then I do the same thing. However, on my next turn, I'm able to use skills (you can't use them immediately at kickoff) and then I can just spam cannon shot or rainbow feint for free goals.
It gets easier later on since the AI is terrible. They never take into account your formation and will gladly have an awful defensive one which will allow you to spam cannon shots.
I've had a match where the opponent had 0 forwards. It was 6 defenders and 5 midfielders. This team had a 4.5-star rating but it didn't matter as they could never score. Other times I've had teams that were using terrible midfielders who got into position to attempt to score but never did instead of passing to their forwards.
As players start retiring, the AI starts using low-level players on the field (instead of training them earlier after they came from the youth academy) and it is so easy to exploit that especially if the guy is a goalkeeper or defender.
At this point, I doubt I'll be playing this again until a new update arrives. Currently, every season is the same, I win everything, my players get even stronger, and the enemy teams are even weaker as their stars retire and are replaced with low-level trash.
However, I do think it is worth it. $15 is chump change and I got around 30 hours of enjoyment out of it. The devs are responsive and are continually updating the game.  I do recommend watching the video I linked above as it is far more positive than this criticism. This is just a collection of my thoughts after putting in about 7 after I made the video and saw that I pretty much did everything the game has to offer.
There are a lot of things that I feel this game is missing. It needs more strategy, more depth, skills reworked and more variety. I know that specified positions are in the works (defensive midfielders, offensive ones, CBs, etc) and I'm looking forward to it.
I also want more upgrades to be available. The current ones are all linear and boring. Money is only used to increase stadium capacity and improve your youth league. Fame is used increase experience gain. Using fame to upgrade the free agency is pointless and a complete waste of currency.
I think it would be interesting to add things like food, alcohol, security, maintenance, and other things. The game just feels "too basic" if you know what I mean. It's incredibly enjoyable when you're struggling in the bottom 2 divisions, but after enough time passes, you will have players with OP skills and you'll breeze through everything.
It's also odd that there is no stat decay. Your forward will perform better when he's 40 years old as opposed to 26 which doesn't make any sense.
I'd like for the game to have replays. Sometimes, when you're losing badly but manage to win at the end is extremely satisfying but there are no replays of even goals.
I'd also like to have the ability to change the age of my squad. It'd be really nice if I could make them as young as possible and then take them all the way to the top. I get attached to my players and loved keeping the same squad in the Master League mode of PES.
I look forward to the updates as this game was incredibly satisfying at the start and has an extreme amount of potential.

Good day good gaming folk.
I'm going to go for a lengthy review because I feel the game deserves it.
Firstly I like it. Sort of. And I dislike it. Sort of a little bit more than I like it.
This is not a fully negative review, it can change as the game is developed and progresses. At the moment it's fun to play but not for more than a handful of hours. I'm not inclined to start playing again from scratch unless something changes in the games development, so for me replayability isn't fantastic at the moment. I'm stressing the at the moment though!
There are positives to the game, it's a unique prospect with things that set it apart from other games that I've played (not an avid steam gamer). The fact that its turn based makes a big difference into making each game kind of special, however the fact that it relies on pure chance makes it fairly predictable and unpredictable at the same time. There are instances in the game when the ai and yourself just get into patterns of repetive moves. These moves are just the most efficient moves available to either side, then it literally just comes to rolling the dice. Hence the predictable (which move is made) and the unpredictable (the randomness of dice if the teams are fairly matched).
Surprisingly for someone who normally gets a game fairly quickly and figures things out I've come stuck in first division somewhere. I think that this is in part because I progressed too quickly through the lower divisions and am now in first division with little money, crummy players compared to the ai and no income. The fact that all the players on the transfer list are well above anything I can afford is a little disheartening as I have in theory played the game well (promoted 3 times in a row). Yet I'm now doing a season in second division then a season in first division where I still get destroyed becasue my team is only 2 stars. And as I said I can afford any decent players when I get to the first division.
The players look nice as does the general design of the game. However I'm not someone that really gives a damn about choosing what my players look like, its only important if you like gazing at your players profile lovingly for lengthy periods of time. Which I, as of yet, haven't done. The player design element is therefore a little lost on me and the same goes for the kit/badge design.
The development of youth players is a struggle as well. Especially when in the first division (not even premier division). When I had a 3 star youth academy and it cost 6.5 million to improve it. Which is out of the question when your only getting 100,000 a game. At that point the players that are produced by the youth academy are good, but not good enough for the first division. Its nigh on impossible to grow a youth team player in the first division without going down (I tried twice with two players each time). The way the game works means that every weak link is easily exposed, so if there's one useless defender then there's no way to avoid the ai going through him to the goal. And if there's a useless attacker then your other attacker(s) need to be very very good in order to compensate. It sort of all comes down to money again because I've never been able to afford a decent enough player that would offset the risk of playing youth team players.
The english could be improved in places.
Skill growth is kind of random. Expect attackers with +-50 defence even when training something else and keepers with +-50 attack. Maybe these could be ruled out unless the manager really wants to train those?
The extra skills are cool. They add another layer of tactical play to the game, however some are extremely overpowered. Rainbow flick/Cannon ball are way op. Long pass, layoff are good (ai doesn't really use layoff much?). Sliding tackle is overpowered in my opinion as well, there should be a trait to learn that counters a sliding tackle.
The thing when players 'get mad' after failing to do something is stupid. All of a sudden after managing to tactically defend the oppositions best attacker for all half he goes abosultely balistic and can pretty much score from anywhere on the pitch because his accuracy increases by about double. It doesn't really add anything to the game for me because it just punishes you for defending properly.
So my pointers to improve the game (we're all nice folk after all and just want the best for humanity):
-remove the scaling on the transfer list, it means you can't buy a player when you've just promoted because they're too expensive. There should be players of more price ranges available at all times.
-weaken the player going mad thing, it only ever punishes me for tactically blocking an attacker.
-think about tweaking the cannonball and rainbow flick, these are too powerful in my opinion.
-think about adding smaller traits, like players being 'sturdy' so they receive a boost to their chances when they get slide tackled. Or players 'touch' players who can immediately control a long ball and precision shoot.
-consider allowing youth players to grow whether they are playing or not. its more realistic and makes the youth academy more plausible.
- make the English more interesting to read
- The strange messages from the 'chairman' at the end of the season don't really add anything.
- penalties are completely random (maybe add a small trait like penalty boss or something?)
- free kicks are a problem as well, the ai has no clue how to defend them and for the player themselves its far too easy to defend them.
I think thats it. Although I'll add more if I think of it.
Thanks for the game and good luck improving it!

Batman: Arkham Origins review. It's no Arkham Asylum or Arkham City.
Set just two years after Bruce Wayne becomes Batman, the game has our caped crusader still as yet unknown, a myth amongst criminals and a wanted man by Gotham City PD. Bruce is on his own, and Origins explores how Batman becomes protector of Gotham.
Let's start off with the bad. There are a HUGE amount of horrific bugs and control issues that really hamper the game, including a few game breaking ones. Combat flows awkwardly and haphazardly, with serious AI issues abounding all throughout. Often the gadgets can stop working, and many times it's not always clear where to go next. However, YMMV in these areas, so take that with a grain of salt.
That being said, there are flashes of pure unadulterated brilliance in Origins. The story is AMAZING, and I would put it superior to both Asylum and City, even if they played it a bit safe with the ending. Fights with Deathstroke, Deadshot (♥♥♥♥ that fight) and even Firefly are great to see and pulled off nicely. Deathstroke's fight is absolutely brilliant, requiring strategy and constant awareness to do flawlessly.
The game looks very nice, even on my middle-range system. I can only imagine what a beastly rig would make this game look like. Environments however are a little bland. Would have liked to see more greenery, but the setting of the game at Christmas does explain away that omission.
Overall, while not as tight mechanically as Asylum, or City, Origins is worth your time. A great imagining of a Batman not yet a recognisable hero, but still a threat to the criminals of Gotham.
Rating: 3.5/5
Warner Brothers has no intention of patching bugs that don't break the game, so be aware that some issues can and most likely will arise while playing.

The mechanics are present--grand in scale, well implemented.
The visuals are there, a joy at 4k, another success for the series.
The dialogue element of the audio is where the game takes a turn toward the inexplicably sub-par.  There is 47, there is Diana and then there is  NPR host does video game dialogue.  I could appreciate english being the spoken language at a multi-cultural fashion show in Paris .  I could even reason that Sapienza had a high population of American expats who had taken residence and were now working the shops during the peak of the anglo-tourist season and that many were chosing to speak in there best mock-Euro accent while visiting.  Now we have Marrakesh, apparently a new American stronghold in Morocco, populated by Paris and Sapienza expats and to top it off the Swedish Embassy got in on the action as well. The coincidence of running into the same voice actor doing a sub-par impressions across a multitude of roles makes it feel like I am still in the training missions.  What's more, when I feel the need to quit playing a game because the language borders on cultural mockery, it makes me start to look at the whole package in a different light and in the case of Marrakesh--the level design starts to break down.  As a USA locale remains on the list, I expect to hear these same grating voices at least one more time--but if they show up in Thailand or Japan, I may be playing in total silence and for a game that chooses to release serially as opposed to a complete package--with a month or more between these levels, err...episodes--I consider such poor dialogue execution a genuine faux pas.
Additionally, the online vs. offline single-player argument is valid as well and smells of a yet unreleased micro-transaction market (elusives anyone?) that is as behind schedule as the Companion App.
There is fun to be had here but I'd wait until the full package is actually complete and discounted if I had it to do over again or choose the episodic thing and skip Marrakesh altogether--at least until they make a few things right.

It REALLY hurts to give this game a not recommend. It has so much going for it and does a good handful of it very well. It's more of a, "if you're interested then buy it on a sale" rather than a flat do not buy it, but Steam only allows me to say yay or nay so... here we are. Let's start with the good;
+ Amazing art, and this is coming from someone who has a hard time with western art in visual novels. I completely forgot I was even concerned with this once I started.
+ Great characters, with your daughter Amanda being a highlight for me. Some characters were better than others but everyone was pretty fun and compelling.
+ A well executed theme... I honestly expected "Dream Daddy" to be a joke game at first glance and it doesn't miss that opportunity to tell it's fair share of jokes. I think it did an excellent job going beyond that though and taking it's theming seriously, without coming off as disingenuous or ridiculous.
And then we'll touch on the bad;
- This game is pretty short for a visual novel. 8-9 hours is about all you'd need to beat this entire game which is about what it took me. (Extra length on my playtime was for capturing footage and listening to that sick opening theme song)
- There are a handful of minigames during your reading experience that are absolutely atrocious... they're like "floating unity assets that made it through Greenlight" bad. What's worse is these minigames that completely take you out of the experience occasionally have an effect on the story based off your performance.
- The length is all the more frustrating when you realize you only get to date a dad three times before thier ending but it's still trying to tell a deep story. It often gets close to completely selling me on the story and conflict it could be presenting but that's quickly snuffed out. 7 dads to explore? That's like... an hour a piece.
All in all I acknowledge that this games strong characters and unique theme will be enough for some but for me the length and a handful of poor design and story telling choices were deal breakers. It wants to be compelling at times but doesn't have the time to, and it wants to be funny but it doesn't fully commit to it with that limited time... I feel like all of this could've been fixed with just a little more play time or a cheaper price tag. If you'd like to check out a full video review I did on the game you can find it here,

While I was quite skeptical of this game at first due to the hype surrounding it, as quite often with such a hype games rarely live up to the standards set, I was pleasantly surprised to find it a thoroughly enjoyable game.
The graphics are very simple but work incredibly well, and the designs of the characters is brilliant. I also found I loved the storylines for each Dad, and how they often crossed over where other characters pop up. The controversy surrounding one of the character endings (whereby one cannot actually end up with this character) I believe is slightly unfounded - though the game does not boast to be 100% realistic, the ending is perfectly realistic for the scenario and storyline set up. The game developers even pointed out themselves that it was written that way for a reason, and though I would've loved to have been able to end up dating this specific Dad, I feel it was the correct ending for his character and his morals.
The main bonus of this game has to be all the dad jokes; as a lover of these jokes, I was in my element all the way through, and found myself really getting into character and the game. By far, Amanda is the best character in the game, and the dads are all written to be naturally different people, which works seamlessly.
Overall, I would recommend this game to just about anyone, be them a fan of dating simulators or simply curious - buy the game!
