Heavy Bullets has been haunting me rather successfully since 2015, but since I recently beat the new game that the creator had time to make in the interim, I decided to go back and smother this helpless baby once and for all.
It's a roguelite. Lite because it doesn't match some arbitrary criteria that some people, who are very mad that the Nethack wiki exists, came up with, but I'd be attempt to slot it under there anyway. All the roguelike elements, brimming on the surface like fecal matter at a water processing plant alongside Action-Adventure and RPG elements, just aren't very good. They're about as bad as that analogy.
So for the premise, the corporate hunting ground -  this time not solely referring to the process of hiring and firing - has been solidly buggered and you, a janitor, and about 10-20 other janitors depending on how good you are at the game, have been tasked with going down 8 levels to sort out this ruckus at the source. You're signing a liability waver first, they don't expect you to make it back.
Don't worry, they give you a gun. Save a bullet for yourself.
Yes, it's got a nice sense of humour about the whole thing, although most of it is simply confined to condemning this completely fictional practice that the developer made up, and isn't quite as fun as the short conversational logs where they take what's left of that water processing plant by the gallon. Complete with emoticons. Ingame it's just snide comments.
Something the developer realised, because High Hell has roughly the same slant with a much better emphasis on humour.
Whole lot of that trend here. Heavy Bullets, for all its flaws or depth or whatever close approximation of either it can muster, is just a bit of a step down compared to High Hell. Which is a good thing by all accounts, and not just because I'm heavily biased against procgen. Getting better with each game is a good thing, I'd say.
So the gameplay involves walking through a series of randomly generated rooms - "randomly generated" meaning pre-existing stitched-together tilesets - filled with the lamest items the developer could muster. It just has an absolute lust for giving you a series of scopes and pointy helmets like the Cursed Gem that makes all your bullets explode isn't blatantly the most fun item in the game.
Other than that you're just collecting cash to spend on the same pool of buffs and items, so not much to surprise you. It's threadbare and weaker for it, unless you really like the idea of continually running through the game until RNGesus blesses you with the items needed for that LOOK AT ALL THOSE HEARTS achievement. Not my thing. I mean I did it anyway, but I wouldn't recommend it.
So that's weak. But it's really the core gameplay that carries Heavy Bullets.
You start off weak. Panicky. Crawling around corners, abusing line of sight, and shooting at every potential snake-bush twice. After just one or two successful runs, you're a screaming Olympic-Athlete, feet drenched in the dregs of reused bullets and circle-strafing/firing blindly at every opportunity. It easily is a game that gets better the more you play it.
But that first few couple of runs are incredibly weak and this was easily set up to be a negative review before crawling over the line.
Honestly, I would say to go check out the Developer's newest game High Hell if you're in the market for this, apart from being sadly much slower movement-wise it's just got all the pieces this doesn't. But if you are in the market for this:
It's a bite-sized okay roguelike that's happy for you to play it. Not much to say other than that.
Not a bad game, actualy It's fun and not that easy FPS roguelite, but ultimately it lacks depth and gets boring quickly, After 2,5 hours, I'm not even interested in finishing it.

As of 2016-06-26, the game has been patched really well, as far as the single-player content is concerned; it looks great and plays great.
In short WRC 5 is a fast-paced sim-arcade game, as have all the previous WRC games been since Evolution's WRC games on the PS2. If you want sim rally I suggest Sebastien Loeb Rally, Dirt Rally or the rFactor rally mods.
WRC 5 has the toughest stages I've yet to play in rally game, and I've played most of them; from early Colin McRae and Richard Burns to the latest Sebastien Loeb and Dirt Rally. WRC 5 has some seriously demanding stage designs, which is a fantastic thing. They may not be realistic, but they are tough and I love that.
Visually the game looks fantastic; the colours are crisp and full of depth.The lighting effects are also noteworthy. Effects like the early morning fog and the blinding light on snow-covered tracks are executed really well in the game, it looks very realistic, which increases the visual immersion.
The various weather effects and day-night settings looked very nice as well. It's a highly immersive game in terms of visuals. Because of the night racing and rain/snow effects, WRC 5 is more representative of the real-life WRC event than Milestone's versions of WRC.
However the game does not look as good as Dirt Rally, but that's to be fully expected from a much smaller studio and publisher. It is completely unreasonable and irrational to expect the same visual quality when the developer budgets are significantly different.
As far as multiplayer goes there's very little of that in WRC 5, and what's there is not that good, so you are better off with Dirt Rally if you want multiplayer gaming, since far more people are playing that game.
The physics is on the sim-arcade side, on the same level as Dirt 2-3. It is slightly more sim-like than the previous WRC games, as it requires more technical skill to handle the car. However the game is not a "hardcore" sim in the same way Dirt Rally and Sebastien Loeb Rally are. Whether that's good or bad depends on what kind of game you are after. I like every type of rally game, whether arcade or sim, so I did not care that much about this matter.
You get three classes of cars to race with, and all countries are represented. There's both a Career mode as well as a Championship mode. So there's a great deal of content in this game. I've probably spent around 50 hours on my console version.
What adds to the replay value is the sheer difficulty of the game. Because of the technical difficulty of the rally stages it is very easy to make mistakes in this game, which can be very punishing. To me this is true to the real-life WRC, where a single mistake could make you loose an entire Round. The game is harsh but fair.
However I do recomend the harder difficulty levels if you are a racing game veteran, as 'medium' is far too easy in the game.
Part of the game's mantra is that you really need to use your intuition, and I think that's the perfect way to describe this game in a summary. Blaming the co-driver and stage designs is very easy, but if you play racing games for the challenge they are lame excuses. It's a tough game, with technical stages and great visual immersion.
Meh.....could have done with another year in development. And longer stages.

Normally games of this format lose my interest quickly, but man was this a fantastic game.
First, the replayability!! I've already played through this game 3 times and I will certainly play though it many more times. There's so many options/choices to make characters like you more, have successful dates, etc., and it keeps things interesting.
I really have to applaud the dialogue in this game. There are so many games I've come across that have subpar dialogue. I kind of just got used to cliche or cheesy (not the good kind) writing, so when a game comes around that has superb writing, I just get even more enjoyment out of it. The dialogue kept me fully engaged in a seemingly simple game. It was a pleasant surprise, because again, this game format is normally quick to lose my interest.
Honestly, I could go on and on about this game. I love it so much. The artwork in it is very charming, the dialogue is fantastic, the replay value is huge, and overall I certainly do not feel like I wasted my money purchasing this game. It's such a simple concept, and while this is technically a dating simulator on the surface, it's also so much more than that. This would definitely show up on a list of my favourite games, no doubt about it. The overall theme of the game, and maybe even the title of the game itself, could maybe lead people to not take this game seriously (if they went into it without any knowledge), but I would certainly recommend this game to anyone who might be on the fence about it, and just in general. This game was great, I honestly don't even have any complaints about it. I really, really would call this one of my favourite games that I've played, despite it being something I never would've considered playing. So glad I gave it a chance.
Not gonna lie I even got emotional on some of the endings because of how invested I was (teared up at Robert's ending because wow I relate to the guy, minus the dad part lmao). I know I'm praising this game to high heavens so it sounds like I'm just a huge Grumps fan or whatever but truth be told, I know next to nothing about the Game Grumps. I know there's mixed reviews about this game, and yes, at the end of the day this is just a visual novel. However, the reason I'm praising this game so much is because I HATE visual novels. They don't engage me and I just cannot (and have no interest in) get into them. But this game just really gripped me. While I will say it can be quite short, I personally think there's a lot of replay value so I really don't mind the length of it.
Of course this game will not be for everyone, and other people will have certain complaints that I won't, but that's what opinions are for! Overall, in my personal opinion though, this game was great. And I went into it with no knowledge and solely bought it because I was bored and saw part of a playthrough of it and thought why the heck not? I'm impressed, and I recommend people at least give this game a try.

The odd love child between association football, an RPG, and chess, Football Tactics combines 22 guys running after a ball with a whole hat full of trick plays and strategies. This is as much a strategy game as a sports game, with players possessing several attributes and skills that need to be mixed and managed well to succeed against the AI, whose players have their own set of abilities that need to be countered.
There are still issues with the game (but what is 100% perfect, ever?), like a rigid league structure that can't be edited, the lack of a way to buy and sell players directly with AI teams (only via the transfer market), and there is a point where winning becomes too easy currently, but not until after many seasons with a team. But the game is regularly updated, and a lot of features that have been requested in the last year or so have made it into the game by now.
Definitely recommended.

Well, I was about to give this game a bad review. I was at the second to last chapter and convinced that this game was nothing special, the story hype was wrong, and it was just another boring shooter that tried to be edgy.
I've never been so wrong about a game in my life.
That's the problem with this game, though. You have to play it through all the way to the VERY end, and then, you'll want to play it again. And that's something I never thought I'd say before I reached the final chapter.
Graphics: Technically, they're nothing special. The game runs pretty well and looks decent for being released in 2012. The design of the graphics is pretty good, though. The landscapes and the whole Dubai scene is gorgeous and has some wonderful views from tall buildings.
Gameplay: This is definitely the worst part of the game. The unfortunate part is that the gameplay is so generic, boring, frustrating, and clunky that I nearly stopped playing it. It's a typical third-person shooter where you're killing lots of people and using cover. The cover system is terrible, especially since the cover button and sprint button are the same. I'll be trying to take cover and instead sprint out in front of the cover, get shot, and die. Movement in general just feels clunky. Like I said, I nearly stopped playing because I got so frustrated. But trust me, you HAVE to push through.
Story: Believe the hype, and don't read spoilers. This game is on another level when it comes to twist endings. Leading up to the big reveal, I was just HOPING that there was gonna be some sort of crazy twist, but I had no idea that it would be what it was. 3079 was the first game developed by phr00t that i played, it was a few years ago on Desura.
To this day its still my favorite game in phr00t's lineup, its a real gem of a game, a mix between Borderlands and Terraria (some will say Minecraft instead of Terraria but i never played Minecraft so i cant argue either way).
Surprisingly the game is still as addictive today as it was several years ago.
Its an open world game.
Its a first person shooter/melee (you can use melee weapons and tools too).
It has decent rpg elements, you can level stealth, stealing, charisma, mining, engineering (crafting), strenth and energy.
The itemisation is really great, and the fact you can expand it with an interesting upgrade system (engineering/crafting), makes it even more satisfying than Borderlands or Diablo.
You can mine for resources (and a lot of the environment is destructible), you can build a decent amount of stuff (bases, storage, home teleports, elevators).
Can get plenty of quests and information from the npcs, can get followers who will help in combat, can get on friendly or hostile terms with factions.
The graphics are basic but even after several years i still like them, dont know if its because they grow on me or its just nostalgia, but regardless, this is a gem of a game that for me is just as addictive today as it was the first time i played it, and thats no small thing.

I really wish they didn't advertise the game as a simulator, because it definitely is not. What it is, however, is a casual game meant for rally and WRC fans.
If you're looking for realism, you won't find it here. The tracks are mostly fictional and the car physics are simcade level at best. The visuals are serviceable but dated and are reminiscent of racing games on last gen consoles.
The performance could be better, but the game should run fine on a modern low end system with some tinkering in the graphics options. With VSync off, I average around 70 fps on max settings with an r7 370 at 900p (45 fps at 1080p). Turning the shadows down a notch yielded a 10-15 fps boost.
There is plenty of content to play through in the solo campaign. You start out as a junior and have to work your way up every season to become a champion.  The rally school is a really nice addition for people who aren't familiar with rally techniques. There are random leaderboard challenges that appear from time to time that serve as a bit of side content. If you just want to drive and not worry about the career, there is a quick stage mode that has every track and car unlocked.
Overall, I would say the single player portion is very plain. You don't really need to do anything but drive. The car repairs, car setup, and team management have mostly been automated. While there are plenty of tracks, they are an example of quantity over quality. Most are short (<5 minutes) and have rather bland environments.
Also, don't get this for multiplayer unless you have friends to play it with since it's mostly dead.
tl;dr
If you just want to sit back with a controller (or whatever your preference) and have some casual rallying fun, then you should get this on a sale.

It should also be a little easier to sign good players. You start with most of a team which retires within a couple years, and all the decent replacements are like $200,000 each. That's far too much for a player in the first few seasons. Perhaps there should be more players from the get go in the transfer list.
The fan accumulation needs tweaking too I think. I am in 2nd division im at 400 fans and falling. In 3rd division I was killing it and came into Div 2 and had nearly 800 fans. I'm now playing my 3rd season in Div 2 and my fans are halved from where I started. Surely by being in a better league you should gain followers rather than haemorrhage them. It makes it very difficult to progress when your cash stagnates.
Other than that I love the game. Much more than I expected. However, maybe expand the youth system? Like you could have upgrades for more players per year coming in, and perhaps a pool of 3 or 5 etc players of which to choose one to promote. That could be fun and more control for the player. Maybe even the ability to do a training drill with them to boost stats???
Anyway, just my thoughts.

This is NOT a 'good game.'
It has various elements of a fun game, but if you're planning on playing it alone, just don't. It's best to grab a friend and laugh at how terrible it is.
The gun spread is nearly intolerable at times, the controls are difficult to figure out, the NPCs are quick to hate you because your spread hit one of them that one time and now they think you've changed sides, you lose 1 item on death and if you haven't gotten a few backups of everything, it will make your game unplayable (such as a weapon, battery, generator, and a jetpack).
Oh, and sometimes the red demons will spawn on the ground, killing entire swathes of NPCs and you if you don't get out soon enough. You can't kill them until you get a Demon Slayer, which is only given to you from certain quests (or when you complete 5 quests). So basically, you're going to lose your main quest givers and shops really early.
If you plan on sticking around, get a mining drill. You'll sometimes find gems to sell. After you get half-decent equipment, ditch the drill. It'll be too slow.
Your easiest quests will be to 'defend' an informant for 3 minutes, because they will never be attacked. It will give you a moment to just chill and take stock of your situation. Your hardest quests will be either covert assassination or getting a Holocube undetected.
The flying vehicles are fun enough. I like to hijack them. Nine points out of eleven, would fly again.
Your crosshair is very reliable... if you put it a bit to the LEFT of your target. Seriously, that's where your aim is centred.
Building is a joke. Just don't even try.
Overall, you can only enjoy this game ironically. Don't even try to enjoy it legitimately.
Final Score: -7/10
(Negative scores are indicative of ironic enjoyment, as sometimes a bad game is more fun than a boring game)

Torment is the long awaited "brother" to the original Torment that so many fans adore, yet it fails to deliver what most fans expected, which is a long and solid game with an captivating story and a world to experience and explore.
It is graphically ok ( It uses the unity game engine ), the player get's rather little options to customize his own character besides genre and 3 different classes , and a lot of the promised content from the early kickstarter campaign is absent in the early version of the game which allready shows when you create your character.
There's a lot of dialogue, but your own character is more on the listening side of the story and it seems your background and player type does little to change this ( which other older Interplay games did like Baldurs Gate , Fallout , Icewind dale and so on ) so the story is pretty straight forward and honestly seems to give little in the terms of replayability ( perhaps a couple of times at most).
Combat is ludicrious bad and almost absent in the aspects of strategy, once you find a tactic that works you will probably use that for the rest of the game. You do get certain "items" that helps you in combat, but most of the game is so easy you can have a large surpluss of these items without ever the need to use them.
The game did seem to have in the start certain "consecuences" of resting if you had a few quests active, as some of them had time limits ( to my knowledge only one ) , but strangely enough that part seems to dissapear completely from the game later on it seems. Again poor quest planning is probably behind that part of the game.
Other aspects of the game is that the story is decently written, but again nothing really special that will make you think about the game again when you hit the bed after having completed it. There's really none of those cuestion other great games gave you like "what if I had" and then go back and try that other option to see what would happen to the world...
Music and sounds where not bad, but to be honest I felt they could have been better , some areas certainly dont give you the feeling that the sound comes from there...
And the game is ludicrious short... My first playthrough (and I tend to try to get every little quest and content ) was around 41 hours and honestly speaking it felt like there's rather few "maps" and things to explore. The dialogue makes up for most of those hours and youre going to spend a lot of time reading.
It's not an outright bad game, but in terms of what it could have been since it's the spiritual successor to Planescape Torment it should have been so much more...
After having crowd funded Inxile a couple of times I have lost faith in them and are going to wait for their games to be released before bothering considering buying them ( like the upcoming bards tale )...

Another long time CRPG / PS:T player here.
If there wasn't so much hype about this being the spiritual predecessor to Planescape : Torment it could be an 8+/10 game. It is a high-quality title certainly worth the time to explore with some niggling design issues. Disclaimer, I intentionally started playing this at version 1.02 after a lot of early bugs were squashed that possibly plagued earlier users.
I'll start with the good. Big props to the immensely detailed environments and the intricately written stories / mini-stories you will encounter. The sheer whackyness and ambience did certainly (on occasion) rival/mirror the experiences that made PS : T great.
The bad: By far the biggest let down was the poor companion character development. Very little emotional depth and story development to your tag-alongs which was one of the best parts of PS : T! Huge omission. Also mid-to-late game it feels like there are no difficult challenges combat either combat or skill-check wise. So long as you've spread your skills out between party members, you almost never fail. Also the story intensity arc is ratherflat throughout the game, meaning the ending feels almost arbitrarily tacked on and somewhat anti-climatic.
In summary, this game's entertainment value comes in the sheer randomnessand quirkyness of the Ninth World and it's numenera coupled with very detailed artwork and writing. The main story, combat and emotional development does however feel like it gets lost in this detalied randomness at times.

First quick about me, I am a veteran RPG & CRPG player, the old Planescape Torment is still my favourite RPG game.
--- What I liked ---
I really liked the locations in the game. Both main locations are brimming with flavour, nicely presented through images, dialogues, quests, companions ... It sometimes feels over the top, but that's exactly what the world of Numenera should be like, and it makes it very interesting to interact with and explore. Especially Bloom rocks!
Overall experience of playing is also quite good, pacing is OK, there is always another interesting quest or location round the corner.
--- Issues ---
-- Main Soryline --
I found the main storyline very unbelievable, and also the main protagonists of it very wooden.
(Minor Spoiler) There is a war between the Changing God and the First Castoff, called the "Endless War" at least 100 years old. But ... although it is such a central point of the story, it is never explained what is it for? It doesn't seem to have any objective, it is never explained what they want to acomplish. And if you spend centuries slugging at each other, with vast armies of men and machines, in what seems to be a middle of nowhere, shouldn't there be some point to it? At least a city/laboratory/important huge artifact to attack or defend, that should feature in the story in some way? The leaders of both sides don't even take part in it, they hide somewhere entirely else.
I feel that a "Secret Cults" type of Endless War, 2 organizations slugging at each other wherever they can discover each other's laboratories, safe havens et, and then disappearing in the shadows would fit the theme much better.
I assume it was supposed to reflect the "Endless War" in Planescape, between Devils and Deamons. That one made much more sense, was firmly rooted in the cosmology.
Also the main 2 protagonists of this conflict. Bot hare so utterly uninteresting! The Changing God is a lying dork. First Castoff is an angry teenager. One of the facets of Planescape: Torment I really liked was the centrality of ideas, different characters embodying different views and ways of seeing life. This made that game very interesting, whereas here the main characters are just flat.
-- The Ending --
Very anticlimatic. No final showdown of any appreciable sort. I recently finished Shadowrun:Dragonfall, so much more interesting Ending there ...
-- Companion Stories --
If you're doing only 6, you could have made them better. I did like the story of Erritis, but all others felt bland, especially Tybir. Again, the issue here is that I couldn't really empathize with any of the characters.
-- Tides --
What's the point of them? It is nice to see and manage your "colour", but it doesn't seem to influence anything. For a feature that made to the Title of the game, pretty disappointing.
-- Smaller stuff --
Portraits! Why are there no portraits of people you talk to? CGiving a face to a person really helps.
Besides, the only existing portraits, of companions (and Last Castoff) are horrible.
Only 3 Foci, all of them bland ... wastes such a nice Numenera mechanic.
--- So So ---
Fighting system is OK, although unbalanced. That's OK tohugh, it is not a war game, and yo ucan always use some Cyphers to help you out.
--- Overall ---
It is a good game, strongly inspired by Planescape: Torment. Immortal protagonist, who did some bad things in previous lives and doesn't rememeber it, lots of interesting encounters and general interesting weirdness ...
But Planescape Torment it ain't. What I liked a lot in Planescape, was the exploration of ideas and attitudes. Here, you can see that from time to time, but it all feels flat. Only exception for me were the Memoralists faction, but even them, they were hard to empathize with.
So enjoy the atmosphere and all the side quests, and don't mind too much the main quest :-) .

As of this review, I've got 51 hours into this game. I've done the story, side missions and most of the other things, but there are still some collectibled to collect, and map to explore. But this was not done in a single sitting, I got it nearly a year ago for 10$ from a key seller website. That should tell you that this game may not come off as very appealing at first.
Well, first of all, the map is huge, which may be a bit scary at first, but in the end, it's a good thing.
And, at first when you start, without an upgraded car, it's just not that much fun. But, if you power throguh the first few hours, and upgrade your car a bit, it'll become really fun. Almost everything you do in this game is fun, and there are a lot of things to do.
Racing, capturing camps, vehicle combat, all really fun... well except clearing mines-which is just tedious and annoying-but there isn't much of that anyway. All in all, the comabt, gameplay and missions are mostly really fun, specially after you upgrade the car a bit.
On the story side... it's not that good... but not too bad either. Max's motives are not really clear, and his actions aren't that well explained. The ending is also a tragedy, which might put you off a bit.
The graphics and performance are great. The graphics, well, isn't as good as Witcher 3 or Rise of The Tomb Raider, but it's good. Face models for example need a bit of work. The landscape and cars look really good, however. The performance is also amazing. I can more that max out the game with a single R9 280X and a FX-8320 @ 4.5 GHz, and barely utilize 60% of the hardware, and I'm pegged at 75 FPS 99% of the time.
Concluding, I will recommend this game. But the initial price of 60$ was a bit high for what it is, but as of this review, it has dropped to 20$ and has gone on sale for as low as 6.67$, which is a steal. So yes, I do recommend this game, specially if on sale.

First off, I will get the praise out of the way.
This game looks great (on highest settings, 60 fps, 1080p). The physics are impressive and there is no shortage of moments where i realise that the sand is really moving like sand should and it influences car movements as it should. The character upgrade system does make the game much more managable compared to early game (even if you appear to become Judge Death by the end of it) which gives an excellent sense of progression. The combat system is fluid (considering Mad Max appears to have been trained by Batman) and there is a sense of impact to every blow/shot/car-related maiming that adds a sense of momentum to combat. The bugs are thankfully kept to a minimal, with the only ones i encountered being really funny, with no game breaking bugs being present at all.
Now onto my personal gripes:
The games main mission path is stupidly quick. I feel like most of the missions are there to introduce the area just so you can go on a side-quest-a-palooza. This one really got to me because, being a fan of the Mad Max universe in general, the movies tend to focus much more on the characters than anything else and here they feel like they are just kind of there, unique in every way yet lacking in any real relevance to the story.
The side quests, oh the side quests. These started off fun enough, but after liberating the second major area I started thinking 'I hope this isn't going to be every damn area.' Oh how naive my pre-side-quest self was. It has a bit of the air f the clone brush about it. The missions are not similar. Majority of them are the exact same thing.
The sounds, the sounds of the car in particular, are almost identical and thus do not give enough audio feedback to let me know of the monsterous engine i had roaring under my personal Max-mobile.This may seem like a little and petty point but when you have to hear that car engine go for 30+ hours and no matter how much you upgrade, that hunk of pixel-rendered metal still sounds like the relative sowing machine your car started off as, it adds up.
The 'Top-Dog' boss fights are a joke, i found one strategy, applied it to all of them and never got so much as a wrinkle in my armoured leather jacket. This is more a point of contention for me because i enjoy boss fights, I am not asking for a Dark Soulsian level of variety and design but just more than ONE design and attack type/pattern would have been nice.
If this game was sold for the usual AAA price (or around that price point) I would not recommend it at all. The game is far too repetitive and feels like Shadow of Mordor or any game in the Batman Arkham series (if another game feels similar to these i would start making use of the term 'Warner Bros Sandbox' as a generic label).
Although, this is a good game for its current lower price point and if you can get it on sale, i would say take a look. It may not be sparkling but it is worth your time, if only to pretend to be Mad Max for a few hours and work on your gravel-ly voice by growling lines at your family pet.

In an gaming era filled with first-person shooters Heavy Bullets does a great job of standing out above the crowd.  In most shooters you can unload clip after clip into to enemies with an array of weapons in your arsenal.  In this game thats not an option.  The revolver is the only weapon available and it comes with a mere six bullets.  You'll need to collect your bullets after firing them and individually reload them back into the cylinder.  If that wasn't daunting enough be aware this is a procedurally generated roguelike.  When you die you will lose everything on you and have to start from the very beginning.  Read on to find out if you're up to the challenge.
On each floor you'll find enemies, shops, banks, items, and locked rooms.  There are a variety of enemies from snakes hidden in the grass, spiders that can guard their bodies, to turrets that shoot out lasers and bombs.  You can use money dropped by dead enemies in the shops which can sell both items and upgrades.  Some upgrades can help you attract coins/bullets, some let you carry more of the same item, while others let you reload multiple bullets at the same time.  One time use items include weapons like bombs, mines, and rockets.  Other items offer passive effects much like the upgrades.  You can sacrifice a key card to open locked rooms and grab the random item within.
The mapping of the floors is different each time you play but they all basically feel likes narrow mazes with a couple openings here and there.  A series of doors break the floors into bite-size chunks to help give you a sense of progression.  Also, its important to know once a door has been open for a extended period of time lasers will stop you from going back for items or shops.  The maps aren't particularly pretty, their neon rainbow walls serve more of a practical purpose to help distinguish hazards than anything else.  The rest of the art is more cartoony with a lot of simple textures and polygons.  The art isn't awful but seems like its purely there to serve the gameplay rather than standout in its own right.
Caution and and steady aim is key to survival.  Audio ques are honestly just as important as visual ques as each threat will make a noise as its about to attack.  Some enemies even generate noise standing still, warning you that danger is right around the corner.  With such limited ammo its crucial to take your time, even just a second, to line up your shots right the first time.  You can quickly find yourself out of bullets and in the bigger rooms in can be especially dangerous to track them down.  Enemies move and shoot quickly so its best to take them on one at a time when possible.  Half the enemies will follow you allowing you to fall back and let them come to you.
This is just a wonderfully unique rogue-like that will keep you coming back for more.  It feels a lot like Spelunky with both the way the levels are laid out and in the sense of each death is a lesson.  Even with the procedural generation the game rarely feels unfair.  Its easy to get into a tight spot if you're not careful but if you take you time you shouldn't go through you're health too fast.  Just don't jump into Heavy Bullets expecting much visually as the gameplay was clearly the focus.  The bland looking levels get old pretty fast but thankfully the gameplay is fun enough to keep you hooked.  Fans of shooters and/or rogue-likes need to do themselves a favor and try out the uniquely crafted experience.

I have a couple of their older CD's but I'm not a what you'd call a "fan", so this review has nothing to do with the band.
There are a few problems as others have noted:
* Escape quits the game without warning.
* It's hard to aim magic.
* Some actions require the use of the mouse, like dialogs and using a potion (?).
* There's no map of the areas.
* It's mostly "hit and run" fighting with no dodging or blocking.
But all that doesn't matter because it's just plain fun. The areas are fun to explore, it's fun to scramble after coins showering out of chests, and fun to run through the spikey logs and acid spewing statues.
The repeatable bonus stages seem to be where you make most of the money so make sure to find the 3 bats in each area to open them up.
Edit: I finished it on normal in about 5.8 hours. Nightmare mode looks interesting enough to replay it and find the few collectibles I missed.

7.5/10 - Worth a visit, at the right price, for any rally fan.
First Impressions
+ 9 patches on pc, Kylotonn appears to be very committed and is listening to the community.
+ nice simple to navigate menus (though some may not be happy with no mouse control).
+ (since latest patches) able to detect all 3 components of my wheel setup.  including my Fanatec CSR Elite pedals and Thrustmater TH8A as separate USB conenctions.
- wish it would detect the Thrustmater TH8A in analog mode for handbrake (instead of needing to use sequential mode).
- overall sound needs improvement, engine sounds especially.  co-driver could also use work, has awkward pauses and sounds robotic.
Graphics and Visual Impression
+ runs just fine on triple screens (but no advanced rendering options).  appears to be well optimized (almost always 60 fps on triples with a single gtx 970).
- overall the visuals can't match visuals of DiRT Rally or other AAA racing games.
- no FOV or ability for full camera adjustments (but cockpit does give 5 view distance options).
- tracks could use more activity from crowd or wildlife.  feels lifeless.
Handling and Physics
+ decent damage modeling that effects handling (but have yet to see a full retirment).  few smart ideas with damage; stuck in a gear, loss of co-driver audio (electronics issues), etc.  fairly realistic repair format at service stops (can't fix tyres by 3%).
= sim-cade physics.  heavy cars and plenty of lateral grip when coasting makes it very easy to drive, but trail braking in to corners, and too heavy of accelreation in or out of corners can still be punished.  reminds me a lot of Colin McRae 2005 and similar... it's a very enjoyable drive, while not totally realistic.
= average at best force feedback.  advanced wheel options are lacking, but I've been able to get it to feel good at 900 degrees of rotation.
Track Selection
+ no deja vu, all 65 stages are unique.  353.7 KM of stages, 5 for each of the 13 coutries (one is repeated in a rally).  This is double that found in DiRT Rally, and still more a bit more than the 300 km quoted by Seb Loeb Rally Evo.
+ enjoyable stage designs, that feel authentic to the region.  reasonable track widths (not extremely wide and unrealistic).  good variation in terrain and turn types and corner combinations.
- stages are not real world recreations, as featured in DiRT Rally and Seb Loeb Rally Evo.
- some stages are very (2-3 km) short.  overall average is 5.4 km per stage (longest is 11 km).
Overall Experience
I'm really enjoying my time with WRC 5.  Those who only care about simulations can skip this title.  But if you're someone who is willing to play something a little more casual, you should be able to easily enjoy this experience.  Thing that makes rally awesome is learning new roads/routes... and this game will let you do that at a great volume.  Career mode is interesting enough as you make your climb from Junior, WRC 2, and finally to WRC.

Hitman (2016) Review
Having been stung by Hitman: Absolution I came to this game feeling a little cautious. However, any worries that I may have had were quickly resolved. This is not only the best Hitman game so far, it’s also one of the best games I have played in years.
Gone are the linear levels and focus on action of Absolution. Instead, we have a true successor to Blood Money. Each of the games levels offers sizable sandbox filled with rich interaction and myriad opportunities for cleaver and inventive play. Experimentation is encouraged and rewarded from the offset and it is perfectly possible to find novel ways of completing contracts outside of any set-pieces that the game designers have baked into each of the areas.
The introduction pack includes three maps. The first two, which are presented as training maps, are around the same size as those found in Blood Money. Despite being called training levels they offer plenty of opportunity for some interesting plays albeit in a more confined place than the games sprawling main levels. The third map in the first pack is set amid a Paris fashion show. The building is enormous, there is loads of stuff going on and getting through it properly took me several hours.
But what really makes this game stand out is just how repayable the levels are. There are challenges to complete the hit using various different methods, dozens of hidden areas and many different achievements you can aim for as you perfect your skills. I found my first hits were always somewhat messy as I improvised while learning the layout of the level. However, I have found there is a great deal of motivation to come back and retry hits as you are able to exploit the knowledge you have gained to better navigate the levels.
Furthermore, in addition to the main hits there are timed escalation missions which offer a series of five mini-hits with specific objectives that you complete against the clock, with your final score going up on global score-boards. This ‘time attack’ mode is a really nice addition and offers a fun challenge and new way to see each of the levels.
And then there is also the addition of custom contracts which players can make for one another adding further fun and replayability to the game. These are created by the player having to complete them so they are always possible if tough. They come with a fun selection of bonus objectives and offer a nice reason to return to levels that you have already player without having to retrace the same objective that you have already completed before.
The second episode is perhaps even more fun than Paris, being set in a beautiful seaside town during the middle of summer. It offers a nice change of feeling and pace to the Paris level, and serves to underline just how versatile and well thought out each of these stages is. I’ll avoid going into any real detail as discovering things for yourself is half the fun. I’d just say that for the asking price of £6.99 it is more than worth the money. Everything feels like it has been very carefully crafted. All the assets are custom for the level, the voice acting is top notch and the AI is sold.
On a technical level the game seems great too. I am running it on a modest PC (GTX770-2GB/i5-4700k/8GB RAM) and I find I can get a mostly locked 60fps on medium settings. It is worth noting that I did suffer bad framerates until I updated my graphics card drivers, so if you do find problems with the game and you’re using an Nvidia card then make sure you have the latest drivers on offer.
In conclusion, Hitman is a fantastic game. It will be one that I will go back to play for many months to come. I’m very excited to see each of the new levels as they come out, yet at the same time I feel I have hardly scratched all of the content on offer with the few that I already have. If you like stealth games at all then getting this is a no-brainer.

After an ingame week you decide to take in 150 more maximum security prisoners to make a challenge for yourself. You would think all that time spent playing simcity 4 would prepare you for what happened next, but no. Here comes your first legendary prisoner, you look at your prisoners stats to see only some of the max security prisoners have a skill or two, but this legendary prisoner...he has abilities you have never heard of. After two days go by, your legendary prisoner decides to start a fight, easy enough since your guards all have tazers...but wait!  The legendary took the tazer like nothing, no worries here come your armed guard to...HOLY CRAP! THAT GUY JUST STOLE MY SHOTGUN! The legendary prisoner quickly kills off your guards. You set the whole prison on lockdown while rito police arive. It's a very dramatic scene as the air siren you installed sounds as riot police, parametics and firemen come to fix the situation. The CEO arrives on the scene and gives you one last job. Send the army in to KILL THAT LEGENDARY S.O.B. You quickly send the experienced soldiers in with their machine guns. It is a gory sight but the riot is over. You start to relax, you beat the legendary, you ended the riot, YOU EVEN STO wait what's this...A NOTICE OF TERMINATION! I'M FIRED AFTER ALL THAT! In short, this is way harder than all the simcity games, the violence is fun, and the power will go to your head 10/10

After spending many hours building a prison, I decided to take a test run as a prisoner and see what damage I could do. This was the result:
Have you ever been trapped in an insane asylum, surronded by brutal savages waiting to rip your throat out at any given moment? The only thing protecting you is a small green door that could easily be broken down in a matter of seconds?
This is the case of Officer BlackLady (BL for short).
The prison was running smoothly on a fine sunday afternoon, all was calm. The prisoners had just gotten off of their three hour work period and were going on a break for lunch. BL and the other staff members chit chat in the cafeteria, but BL steps out to use the ladies room. In the cafeteria, all the prisoners line up to get their daily slop. The newest inmate (lets call him Brick), sits down to eat his meal. He goes to reach for the salt, but as he goes to pour, the lid pops off and all the salt pours onto his meal, ruining it.
"Who the ♥♥♥♥ did this..."
Brick's salt levels reached an all time high, never before had anyone seem this form of salt. He leaned over to a snickering inmate, and ripped him in half. His blood spilled onto the ground as the other inmates look on in terror. One of the guards attempts to subdue him, only to be pummeled to the ground.
This display started the unforgettable riot.
The entire cafeteria exploded into a hellish war zone of flying fists and meat chunks. The guards were all blitzed and had all their weapons taken. Some were brutally beaten into an unconcious state, while others had their heads dipped into the boiling pots of water. They prisoners exploded out of the cafeteria in a hellish manner, inciting others to join the riot. Within minutes the entire prison was being overrun by prisoners with tons of illegal contraband either stolen in the raid or hidden from earlier points.
On her way back to the cafeteria, BL saw the riot, and quickly took shelter in the infirmary. There, she saw all the patients assaulting the doctors who were working, some being stabbed in the neck with syringes and others being gutted by scalpals and knives. One young doctor (lets call her Cherry), was being cornered by one especially unruly inmate. BL jostled him down, grabbing Cherry and rushing her into the morgue for safety. They locked the doors behind them, turned off the lights, and hid in a corner, hoping nobody would see them.
The riot went on for what seemed like hours, hundereds of guards were murdered, multiple prisoners escaped, even the cooks and janitors were gutted and hung out to dry in the yard. BL and Cherry were the only two survivors in the onslaught. After the noise calmed down, BL looked out of the window to see the horrid landscape. Bodies laid in the yard. Prisoners and Guards alike. Other prisoners simply walked over their bodies, carrying weapons and looking for any survivors.
BL knew that some of the more insane prisoners would stay behind, waiting for backup to arrive, just to claim more lives and shed more blood. These were the sick and the deranged, the ones locked up in the basement always forgotten about.
She gave Cherry her gun, told her to use the emergency phone to call for help if she didn't return, grabbed her baton and stun gun, and exited the morgue, locking the door behind her. She carefully snuck around the prison looking for anyway for her to safely get Cherry out of the prison. As she turned the corner to the cafeteria, she was ambushed from behind. As she fell to the floor, she whipped out her tazer and electrocuted the man on top of her. Pushing him off she made a dash for the exit, hoping to find someway to save Cherry afterwards. As she turned each corner, she could hear the roars increasing behind her of prisoners out for blood. She bolted out the front doors and headed for the hole in the fence to freedom. With each step she heard them closing in. 20 meters. 10. 5. "Almost there" - she said to herself. Only three yards from the hole, she was tackled to the ground. She tried to fight off the inmate, but was quickly surronded. It was no use, she was dead. The prisoners began their assault, kicking and punching her. The life was about to leave her body when she heard the gun fire. A prioner dropped dead at her side. The back up SWAT team finally arrived, and swiftly shot down all the prisoners. They grabbed BL and brought her into the back of their van. She told them about Cherry, before finally falling unconcious.
When she awoke, she was in the hospital, Cherry sitting at her side. On the TV she saw that the prison had finally been secured once more, but the body count was in the thousands. BL looked over to Cherry and smiled. That was when the knife had entered her gut. She looked down to see the blood, and looked back up at Cherry. That was when she remembred, the hospital had a psych ward attatched to the infirmary. Cherry was no doctor, she was an insane inmate looking for a way out. And now that BL was dead, there would be no loose ends.
Cherry walked out of the hospital, bloody knife in hand, and walked off into the sunset.

Ok, so I'm another one of these guys that hasen't written many reviews so bare with me.
Short and sweet:
PROS:
Awesome story with amazing backdrops and characters.
The diolog between them is funny and the voice acting is pretty solid.
The quests are enjoyable and well written for the most part with some pretty amazing surprises along the way.
Finding out what "random" stuff does in your inventory is a nice treat and some of the items have some pretty amazing stories associated with them.
CONS:  (and sad to say, the motivation for me coming here)
The combat.  Holy jesus the combat is pure infuriating at times.  It's not because it's overly difficult and you can't manage to figure out how to deal with the enemy.  It's because in some cases you just can't layout a strategy because you can't select different characters and set them up.   You MUST lead in with your main character who cannot die or it's GG and in many of the cases I've found so far your enemy has a much higher initiation level than you.  So they go first.  So, you lead in with a character that can't die or it's GG (while your allies don't die but get "knocked out" instead) against enemies who in large part can move first.
Pure rage inducing.
Why this company, who made Wasteland 2 (among others) with it's amazing combat, would choose to make such horrid combat decisions is just adding to the anger.
I'm a pretty big InXile fan and LOVE wasteland 2.  It is a huge letdown in this game that you can't select seperate characters and move them individually.  As far as i can tell you can't even decide who stands next to who in the "lineup".
I love the overall aspects of the game.  The story is really pretty amazing.  The combat though...my god, i just don't understand.   Those 2 things make such an impact on the pure frustration levels of the game that I just can't figure out why they went with it.
Would i recommend the game, yes.  Overall, yes, i would.  But it's a strained yes.

PS:T remains one of my top 5 all time favorite games. I reviewied it many years ago on GamesDomain. So of course I backed this game. I've been playing RPGs since the original Wizardry. I watched a couple of videos but avoided playing the demo because I wanted the entire experience at once. I was truly excited to play this one.
And...meh.
If there was a "meh" button on Steam, this game would be the poster child for it. The first problem the game encounters are the expectations. When you name your game the same as one of the most beloved RPG of all time you're setting the bar quite high. There's no way for an experienced PS:T player to play this and not think of the original. It doesn't deserve the name Torment so I'll refer to it as Tides.
Normally I'd talk about the graphics, the sounds, the quests, the bugs, the pros and cons of the game. That's my normal MO. But I can't do it in this case. So let me tell you why it finally got a thumbs down from me.
Sure it's linear - but so was Torment.
Sure there are bugs (like the combat freeze bug - inexcusable) but those will get patched out.
Sure the graphics can get muddled. But those are acceptable.
Sure there are exceptionally annoying sequences (not really combat) in the game that if you don't have the correct build you will struggle to get through.
Nope, those aren't the problem.
The game commits the cardinal sin of being unmemorable. How? Let me provide a few examples.
The NPCs are all fairly dull. People still remember Morte, Annah, Fall-From-Grace, Dak'kon and Ingus. I haven't played that game in 10 years and can rattle off the characters. I finished Tides a week ago and can't remember one character name. I guess you could chalk that up as a Senior Moment but the characters aren't even worth the time to talk to. Plus there are some very weak NPCs that you simply should avoid. There was no attachment to any of them by the end of the game and that's a darn shame. I HAD to pull Morte out of that pile of skulls 15 years ago. There was no such urgency or attachment in Tides.
Remember the Morgue? Farods? The Upper Ward? Curst? Torment had some great set areas each with a different feel. In fact, if you go look at the screenshots of the upcoming remastered version the areas look awesome. Tides? There's one - the Bloom - and that's about it. The main town just seems like a collection of different ideas with no coherency at all. Other areas aren't memorable at all. Like the NPCs, the world isn't very interesting. Go to the Tides website - or better yet, just Google - the Tides wallpapers. Those captured the imagination. The actual set designs were so flat and dull as compared to those it's mind boggling how poorly executed the art design is.
But the worst, most cardinal sin is the writing. It's writing for writing's sake. It's like a student trying to pad their essay to get to the magical 1,000 word count. Much like this review, it just goes on and on and says nothing new. You started off in Torment with some fairly extensive dialog but it wasn't overwhelming. Only later - as you got more engrossed into the world - did it explain more and more to you. Torment built up the world, word by word, until you were fully engrossed. Tides just spews dialog at the player without ever really taking the time to set everything up. Thus it has little meaning and no emotional impact.
Now next week a remastered version of Torment will be released. You can get the existing game for half the price of this one and it's a far, far superior product. Tyranny, another RPG recently released, is a superior product. Now maybe they'll create an enhanced edition with new NPCs, areas and dialog that makes Tides into something more. But until that happens, I'd say you have better options for your money.

I'm a huge fan of the Mad Max movies, so I knew I'd eventually play this game. Unfortunately, having played The Witcher 3 and MGS V: TPP, I automatically compared this game to those two. Sure they're not entirely the same, but being open world games and how they offer entertainment is what I mostly had in mind.
Mad Max was fun, but most of what was offered in its vast wasteland was repetitive, and at times I didn't bother to pay attention to these sidequests. Despite ignoring these sidequests, there were moments where they were necessary to advance in the main storyline. Honestly, that bothered me a little. I'm the type of player that's playing for the main storyline, not to collect special items or discover all the locations on a map. Most of the times, these types of additions to a game are included to beef up the amount of gameplay time, but that's a weak way of doing so. I'd rather play a medium/long game that involves a well written storyline or gameplay, much like The Witcher 3.
Despite this complaint, I enjoyed Mad Max. The game's setting was well created and the storyline was decent, along with being an interesting way to expand the Mad Max lore.
One thing I've heard others complain about is the combat system. The combat system in this game is similar to the latest Batman games. Honestly, it didn't bother me because it can be upgraded and this allows some variety and I genuinely enjoy that combat system.
Overall, I enjoyed the game and I recommend that you play it, even if you haven't seen the movies. I give this game a 3.5/5.

Mad Max is an outstanding open world action/adventure masterpiece which takes some of the best parts of it's genre siblings and mixes them with a fantastic theme to create an unprecedented stand alone experience.
Step into Max's boots, a man who just wants to get his car back, driven solely by survival instincts. You take to the road in a freshly built and decently customisable new set of wheels to topple a fiendish bloodlusty raider boss named Scrotus and reclaim the Interceptor, the black on black.
With fantastic driving combat built from the ground up coupled with the acclaimed hand to hand combat/counter system made popular by the Batman: Arkham series (as well as Shadow of Mordor), there is a lot to see and find out in the wastes as long as you don't mind a little bit of repetition. Mad Max is also a beautifully example of how good Photo mode in these games can be (I've a couple of nice shots on my profile, bit of a photographer in games) and you can get some truly stunning shots.
For a game no one saw coming and didn't have much expectation on, Mad Max rallies with the release of Fury Road to bring this post-apo universe back from the dust with fire and nitro and madness for all

As someone who read a bunch of reviews for this game and decided to risk it, I thought it was worth saying: I was skeptical, I had a lot of fun, but I have to say I agree with the reviewers saying this game is too expensive as is.
This game is ridiculous at a glance, but there's a shocking amount of worthwhile story to sift through. I loved that each dad had a unique romance. I loved the comedy. I loved how invested I got sometimes, especially when it came to Amanda. I loved the art and scenic variety. I loved the dads! Craig and Damien, best boys. There was so much this game unexpectedly did right. Buuuuut...
There was a lot to nitpick, too. For being able to customize your character, I actually felt it was somewhat sparse. I made a new dad for each playthrough, but by the end, I found I was using the same few features over and over because nothing else really looked right. (Fair Warning: customize options are not suited for bishonen dads, lol). Your character has a set personality throughout, so I felt he was better suited with some dads more than others based on his dialogue and choice options which really killed it for a few of the plots. He just didn't work with some guys, making it awkward and forced. By far, the worst offender of this game is that: "everything's made up, and the points don't matter." You have to go out of your way to try and lose this game. It wins for you. It's either going to be an obvious right or wrong answer, a mini-game that's childishly easy (minus the infamous putt-putt, of course; that's Satan's playground), or worse - there is no wrong answer with some of the options making your choice mean nothing. And that's downright unforgiveable to me for a dating sim. The challenge is gone, and that's the game. It becomes a point and click chore list, and that was a major bummer for me.
You can't save a sinking ship. This game is grossly short, and it's barely a game at all. The lack of content is its fatal flaw. What it has is done well, but it's just not enough to justify the pricetag. I will still recommend this because it was funny and cute and exactly as promised, but I'd only really recommend it to buy if the price goes down after the hype, or they give it more updates, but currently... it's only worth it for the time sink and to sate your curiosity. I'm with the others who said wait for a sale or watch a let's play.

TL;DR consider getting this game if you want an arcady and more easy rally game.
Full story:
Many reviews seem to be comparing this game to Dirt Rally (I own both of these games), and the way this game is marketed suggests it is a rally simulator. However, people, who search for rally simulator will not find it here, because this game has quite arcady driving and damage models. That certainly will not appeal to Dirt Rally crowd, but I think people who are not into hardcore racing simulators would enjoy this game: this game has rally school, much less steep learning curve and it can be enjoyed without having a racing wheel. The tradeoff is not that realistic driving.
Is it better than WRC 4? Yes. It runs smoothly at 60 FPS (older game was locked to 30), the graphics seem to be a big improvement over WRC 4. The amount of cars is decent, but less than Dirt Rally offers and classes are limited to WRC, WRC-2 and J-WRC. The price compared to amount of content on offer (comparing to Dirt Rally) is quite high, but if you can get it on sale, it is worth the money.
Cons: it suffers from problem WRC 4 had as well: many special stages are on same pieces of road, so amount of unique roads is much smaller than number of stages. The rewind feature seems to be missing from WRC 4, now you just can restart from last checkpoint. Some signs of poor port from consoles to PC: key prompts seems to be bugged out, a lot of times Xbox controller prompts are shonwn for me when I only own a Logitech Driving Force GT, which has PS3 buttons on it.
As a conclusion I can say if you are into hardcore racing simulators, you own a decent raging wheel, then get Dirt Rally, it is much better game for you. If you are into more arcady and more casual fun, this might be worth it for you.

This game is definitely NOT the "sell-out" to gamers that many people accuse it of being. Avenged Sevenfold, a fantastic Heavy Metal band composed of longtime gamers, decided that they wanted to write a love letter to the classic dungeon crawler RPG games they grew up playing. This is what
is.
The game was made to play and feel like the classic dungeon crawlers, like
etc. The graphics resemble those of the original Playstation, so some people may be disenchanted by the lack of graphical fidelity that today's gamers are used to. It's important to keep in mind that this look was done on purpose, and that it helps cement that fantastic retro feel. If you keep the right mindset, you might just be overwhelmed with nostalgia.
Every enemy requires a slightly different approach to defeat, the bosses especially. Beating this game is
easy and will require the player to get a good grasp of the game mechanics and enemy patterns. This is one of the reasons that this game is such a great homage to the golden age of RPGs; no hand-holding. This game will kick your butt unless you really commit to playing it well.
The controls are simple: wasd to move, left click for melee, and right click for your ranged magic attack, which can be charged for a large special attack that varies with the weapon one uses. The controls may seem button-mashy at first- and they kinda are- but this is not as unpleasant as one might think, because it gives all the more reason to really work at mastering the gameplay.
The soundtrack is superb, and you'll have to play the game to appreciate it; not much I can say to do justice to an awesome band writing a video game soundtrack that melds 8-bit music with modern instruments perfectly. With every boss battle, a hit from the band's catalog will play in an instrumental version, accenting the change in dynamic and upping the energy for the intense showdowns.
All said, you don't have to be an Avenged Sevenfold fan to love this game. Try it. It's made for hardcore gamers and was created with the utmost love for the classics. Try it yourself, don't diss it because cynics like to say that a band can't make games too.

Disclaimer: yes i am an Avenged Sevenfold fan so this might be a little bit bias toward the game due to that. other than that.
Hail to the king deathbat is a simple hack and slash zelda/diablo dungeon run. It features as guessed A7X's songs in and some of their own 8-bit songs that can be hit and miss (my favorite is the level Wicked End song. Just damn) That being said you would think they would use the full library of their songs to its potentional and since this is the main selling point I will focus on it first.
It misses out using many of the bands tracks and during mini bosses you will keep hearing the same song (Unholy Confessions). I really wish they would have used their songs to the max. The songs are in no particular order: Nightmare, Wicked End, Beast and the Harlot, Little Piece of Heaven, Unholy Confessions, Bat Country, and Fiction. No Hail to the King, MIA, Sidewinder, Shepard of Fire, Carry on, Welcome to the family. Now while the song choices match the levels (each level is named after the song used in the boss fight, excludeing afterlife) they are just instrumental version of the song with vocals removed. Now don't get me wrong I LOVE nightmare, but I would have been blown away if they did all their songs in 8-bit format. seems like a missed opportunity to me. Regardless the soundtrack is a blast if your a fan and the actual level songs can be darn good (Bat Country and Wicked End are pretty good). Now onto the meat of the game, the gameplay.
The gameplay in all honestly is lack luster.  W A S D to move, P to pause, and mouse 1 to hit and 2 for magic. The big burden that seems to hold this game down is it being a mobile port. Due to this it is rather simplistic. While simplistic might work on mobile easily, here it just feels boring. theres no real stratigy or tactics to the combat other than hit and weave away repeat till it dies. Theres no sprint, Stamina meter, dodge move, run, nothing. It just feels barebones and at times boring as you hack and weave an enemy to death. They do try to mix it up with giving your magic a secondary attack that changes with your weapon, but that just makes it easy to find the best weapon and never switch tactics.
The level design is standard with some varity of hidden goodies to find. The issue with some of the levels is most look very similar and ocassionaly on Unholy Confession i found myself lost for a little bit. If they added map of some kind as in the pause menu or an item pick up that would be helpful.
The secrets to find can range from easy to find to nearly impossible (how do i get to that damned chest in Afterlife?). The "secrets" themselves are some of the bands artwork such as City of evil cover and the bands logo.
The bosses range from interesting to frustrating. Certain bosses you just have to tank until either you or they die. *cough* Harlot *cough* other bosses can't be beat by the standard stab, stab, stab way and require some cunning moves to defeat which spiced up gameplay and made each boss fun on it's own merits. The final boss is not too tough unless you ran out of health items like me and tried to kill him on 25 HP.
the Graphics are not half bad for a mobile port. the art style works with the style the band has set up and stays consistant (one of my favorite map visually is Little Piece of Heaven)
Overall for a band that decided hey we play games a whole ton lets make a sweet game and make it have some of our music they did damn good. They didn't stick to any of the bad mobile games trend and made a fairly difficult but fun hack n slash gothic 3rd person game. Good job A7X, but please next time you make a game have it be on PC and for the love of god add the full track list and maybe some 8-bit versions of the songs.

"I'll right a better review later, but this game is awesome." Alright, now that I'm done with the game, I can talk about it. This game was a masterpiece. I've only used that word for one other game- The Last of Us, and this game is absolutly on the same level. The story is so amazing and complicated but without over-duing it and making you too confused to play it. The gameplay is fun, compeling, and very gritty, and by the end, you feel like you've been on the journey with Delta (the name of the squad in the game). SPOILERS FROM HERE DOWN!
This part of my comment is for people who just finished the game, and have no idea what the ♥♥♥♥ just happened. Allow me to explain:
The 33rd were in Dubai to oversee the evacuation.♥♥♥♥♥♥goes sideways, everyone is trapped in Dubai. No one can leave. Since the 33rd are the only form of authority in the city, they take over. This doesn't go well. They enforce martial law. People die.
The CIA goes to Dubai to basically kill the 33rd. They go about doing this by inciting a rebellion against the 33rd. In the same way the MACV-SOG were used in 'Nam to train insurgent forces to fight the north Vietnamese. The CIA has to kill the 33rd because if word ever gets out that America came in and took over Dubai it could start a serious war between the Middle-East and the US. So the CIA's goal is basically kill everyone and erase all the evidence.
The Civilians are under the protection of the 33rd whether they like it or not. The 33rd are still trying to save everyone from an admittingly hopeless situation.
It's unclear whether or not the insurgents existed before the CIA arrived and stoke the flames. But in any case, the Insurgents want the Americans out. They see this as another case of classic American interventionism in a country they don't belong in. Vietnam, Afghanistan, Iraq, you name it. They want them out. This is their home and they will fight them to do it. The 33rd's violence against civilians during riots and martial law only fan the flames.
Ok so that is all before Delta shows up. This is where things get complicated.
Delta arrives and runs into rebel forces. They attempt to have a conversation. Interestingly enough in Dubai, the local population speaks Arabic, Lugo talks to them in Farsi. In any case, they try to talk, Walkers and Adams discuss how to kill the rebels in case things go bad. The rebels notice them talking and say "they're plotting to kill us". And they're right, technically. The rebels shoot at you because they think you're the 33rd coming to take them back to the Nest. So you start killing them because you think they're bad guys.
Then you get to the plane and shoot at more rebels who're fighting the 33rd. The 33rd, at this point, are actually fighting against the CIA trying to prevent the cover-up/destruction of Dubai.
You run off to rescue the soldier taken by the rebels, and find out it's the CIA running the rebels. You now think well if the CIA is fighting the 33rd, the 33rd must be the bad guys, right? Why would the US Government fight the 33rd unless they went off the reservation and turned traitor? So now you side with the CIA against the traitorous 33rd. The first sequence where you shoot Americans is more or less started by you. If you let the soldier go, he warns his friends some CIA goons are coming. You're met with resistance and you shoot. You kill because you think you know what you're doing. Similarly, in the market where the 33rd are shooting at civilians? They're not shooting at them. They're trying to evacuate the civilians and take them back to the Nest.
By the time you figure out that the CIA is just trying to kill everyone, it's too late. You've already massacred freedom fighters, civilians, and American troops. You've already doomed everyone.
The 33rd keep fighting you because they have to. You're killing them! Walker and Delta are like a god damn meat grinder, everything they run into is reduced to quivering slabs of meat. The 33rd also think you're part of the CIA, at least initially. But the most telling scene is near the end when you make your run at the tower. Even after everything you've done, after all the soldiers you've slaughtered, even after the white phosphorus attack... the 33rd have you surrounded and they ask you to surrender. The 33rd are willing to let you give up! They weren't trying to kill you, they were defending themselves!
Delta constantly thinks they're the good guys, but they're not. They make decisions when they think they have all the facts, but they only ever know a fraction of the story. They have good intentions, but it leads to death, destruction, and despair at every turn.
The story is unclear because it has to be. Walker has to make his decisions with partial facts and half-truths. If you know more than Walker, the effect is lost. You have to be just as blind as Walker for the story to have any impact.
There are also four different endings to this game:
The first is that Walker commits suicide after not being able to cope with the crushing reality of his actions in Dubai. (Medium ending, not too sad and horrible but not to happy)
The second is that he is killed by Falcon One, the army squad sent to rescue him, when he chooses to retaliate against them. (A little sadder then the previous one because it shows how bat♥♥♥♥♥♥crazy Walker really is)
The third is that he kills all of Falcon One, and continues to live in the ruined city of Dubai. (By far the saddest and most horrible ending. Shows that you're an insane killer that doesn't care about anything anymore.)
The last is that he surrenders to Falcon One and is safely returned home, albeit mentally scarred. (Probably the best ending, if that makes any sense)
Walker just wanted to be a hero.

I really enjoyed this game. Or rather, I should say, I really enjoyed the story. The gameplay I didn´t really like.
From the outset the game wears its love of Hear of Darkness on its sleve just stopping short of calling the antagonist Kurtz (Called him Conrad though, which is the next closest thing really). As one of my favourite books I was quite looking forward to how this game did it and I was not dissapointed. The story is the selling point of the game and from the prespective of the game as an adaptation of Heart of Darkness it suceeds. Moreso, I would argue, than Apocalypse Now.
The differeces are big: moving from the jungle river setting of HoD and Apocalypse to what is pretty much the polar opposite - hyper developed Dubai enveloped in sandstorms. But the setting and plot do nothing but relay the same core story. Its easy to identy various characters that are encountered along the way with counterparts in the novel but what for me made it really stand out in this regard was the handling of the Kurtz character.
[not really a spoiler but I'll warn you anyway]
Conrad is built up with all this hype just as Kurtz is and then at the end of it all we see a man - not a god or a hero, just a man.
Just as this causes Marlow to examine himself so the game asks the player to examine themselves showing them not to be a god or hero either. In this aspect the story really captures some of the essence of Conrad's novella.
And then there's all the moral choice stuff that people like which is fun and exciting and disturbing and harrowing. Its a wonderful game for making you feel things.
However one thing it did make me feel was bored. I'm not much of a player of shooters so I was expecting this to be an interesting break from the normal strategy nonsense I get up to. However by the final chapters of the game I was so bored of being in cover and firing out of it that the only thing driving me on was wanting to finish the story. I can't imagine what it must be like to people who are used to this genre. The combat is grindy and boring and really takes away from the experience in the later game.
All in all I really enjoyed this game though. Its a wonderfully refeshing twish on a classic story that makes you feel and think.

Kk, I deleted my old review, since I felt it might have been harsh, so here I go again. The verdict is still the same (not recommended, at least at the moment), but I feel I now understand the game well enough to explain my reasons better.
All in all, this game shows a lot of potential, and is fun to play, even now. The graphics and music are pretty much "meh!", as in pretty bad, but don't matter anyway, and don't really influence my opinion of the game. What does influence it, is the gameplay mechanics.
Basically, this is a stripped-down / casual football manager. It really tries to be and look simple, but here is where I was starting to have problems.
The first problem, and perhaps the major one, is that it doesn't really succeed in being simple, at least when it comes being intuitive and understandable. I've clocked countless hours of gameplay on plenty of versions of both football manager games and action soccer games, such as FIFA and Pro Evolution Soccer in the past, so I dare claim to be able to learn such games quick and easy. Not with Football Tactics, though. For a game that presumes to be simple, there sure are quite a lot of reading materials. While some of the skills and moves are easy enough to figure out while playing, others aren't, so don't plan on just jumping in and figuring out as you go.
The second problem regarding the game's presumed simple design, is that in some aspects, it is too simple. Soon enough, many things become tedious and tiresome, as the game becomes repetetive and dull. Some would choose the word 'boring'.
My last issue with the game is its core gameplay component - how it deals with every action within the soccer games. While I can't provide any proof of any of this, as I don't have access to the game code, I feel very strongly that sometimes, in specific situations, the results don't make sense.
