Summary: joyless, gratuitous frustration.
This is coming from someone who appreciates bullet hell shooters and twitch-based games.
Success in this game is more heavily dictated by luck than by the player's actions, and rarely will you die feeling like you were to blame instead of one of the various ill-designed or broken mechanics that plague Heavy Bullets.
You will suffer from:
- Getting hit by explosions and turret fire that hit the opposite side of a wall (broken hit detection)
- Exploding enemies that spawned around a corner in a tight corridor and trigger immediately (no-win situation)
- Turrets that seem to fire with a set interval, but glitch and fire in quick succession out of nowhere
- Seemingly no player damage rate limiter (full life to death in no time if unlucky)
- Terrible enemy AI that's overcompensated with dumb attribute buffs in speed/damage.
- Grating sounds emitted frequently by every unpicked bullet and coin
- Uninformative and confusing menus
- Assorted glitches, such as the reticle jittering (on Windows) or even jumping around (on Linux) with mouse movement.
And I see no sign that any of it is going to be improved.

Why should I buy this game?
-Its a procedurally-generated level system, meaning, everytime you play, the levels change! You never know what to expect
-It's really exciting - theres enemies around every corner so you gotta be super careful and peek around. Survival gaming at its greatest.
-It's super hard - but fair! Every enemy gives fair warning, so if you die, its either because you got careless, went too fast or wasn't prepared. So it makes you want to try again and again! Great replayability!
-You can grind to victory! In a sense. You can deposit the cash you collect in the bank for future runs, allowing you rack up a ton of cash for use right from the start!
-Design is super-unique! Apart from (and I'm stretching it here) Hotline Miami and Far Cry Blood Dragon, you won't find this neon retro style. The stark color contrast also makes things pop out, which is good for gameplay, such as the bright weak spots of enemies.
-Music and sound are all top-notch! The music picks up whenever theres enemies around - a nice jungle battle theme - than dies down when everything's dead. The sound effects are all delightfully (in my opinion) retro and the enemy popping (yes they pop in pieces, like Lego) sounds in particular are very satisfying.
What's not so good?
-Its nail-bitingly difficult. You can only take a few hits, and enemies hit FAST and UNEXPECTEDLY. Within a minute of your first playthrough you'll be left with 1/2 of a heart left, gasping and cringing at the low-health sound. Then, you'll reach the first boss and possibly destroy your controller as he destroys you in a split-second. Which is a good point for some, a bad point for others. I personally find it a tad bit TOO DIFFICULT.
-There's not that many enemies in the game really, but there's enough and their placement always changes.
-Can be confusing for new players. It was complicated to configure the xbox controller - it isn't automatic. There's no tutorial. You'll suicide by accidentally throwing a bomb. Enemies look like the rocks and bushes. In stores, it doesn't say what things do. You just gotta try it out and figure it out on your own.
-The game isn't terribly balanced. Some items are awesome, but most are terrible to useless. Most players will have to resort to stocking one particular item in the bank and ALWAYS USING THE SAME THING. That's kinda sad.
Can't really think of any real faults in the game other than that. Its just perfect at what it does, so it doesn't need to be overly ambitious like GTA V.

Tides of Numenera is a great game if you play it for writing and atmosphere and mediocre at best if you play it for combat and mechanics.
Its plot, while a bit short, is quiet interesting and unusual, side quests are fabulous and a vast majority of NPCs are wonderfully written. World of Numenera is intriguing enough and a multitude of useless but colourful artifacts that you gather in course of action adds a lot of flair. It's really a pleasure to delve into unknown aspects of this world, visit its wondrous places and get to know its inhabitants.
At the same time, combat is awful. Luckily, you can evade it for most part, but when you can't,,, turn-based style works poorly here, where you often meet a lot of enemies and have to wait through their endless turns time and again. Especially now, when game sometimes freezes or bugs out and you have to restart from the beginning. Much-advertised tides mechanic is sadly almost non-existent too.
But despite all these faults Tides of Numenera is one-of-a-kind game, well, two-of-a-kind, together with original Torment. You're not gonna find another RPG with these awesome and picturesque walls of text where you can resolve most of the conflicts with words. It's well worth to try out if you're a fan of this kind of RPGs.

Welcome to Dubai. Sitrep, you say? FUBAR. While this game isn't perfect, it's certainly a step in the right direction for the storylines of shooters. Every character exists in a morally gray area in which their actions are both justifiable and revolting.  The game is works because we try to categorize people and actions into simple, clear groups. To use a dated example, the good cowboys shoot the bad Indians. Spec Ops:  The Line reminds us that there is no simple answer to everything and that right and wrong may not exist. It begs the player to ask, "Am I the good guy?" More significantly, it also makes us question, "Is there a good guy?" and leaves the player to answer that question.
Also, I'd be doing you a disservice to not mention that the gameplay is dull, but the writing and atmosphere make the game worthwhile, not its enjoyability.

Review:
To say this was one of the best CoDs is an understatement. It had a great single player campaign and really expanded from the original with multiple endings and memorable characters. Small choices were short term, however some were longlasting and affected the ending slightly to extremely different from the other; however after all this CoD put a good amount of attention on choice. On to the multiplayer side: One word: Extraordinary. For the PC, the game is extremely well optimized coming from a console port! It easily surpasses 60FPS on a descent gaming rig because it is not a demanding game by any means (even on a low rig these days your PC should easily handle the game over 40 FPS). Multiplayer is a blast and the pick 10 system laid the groundwork for last year's Advanced Warfare (which has a great experience too!) and optimized great too (unlike Call of Duty Ghosts but that's for another time). And last but not least, Zombies. Zombies in this iteration has been extended like never before from Treyarch's past games. Although the main characters were replaced by 4 new ones, they are still quite charming as the original 4; the originals even are playable in DLC 4's zombie map, origins. With new ways to fend off the undead hord, crafting tools, and various ways to survive, zombies is still as fun as it was in World at War and Black Ops. As it stands in June 2015, multiplayer is still extremely active, even with Call of Duty Advanced Warfare released, and is safe to say that population will return for a bit in the upcoming months leading to Black Ops III. Now on to final thoughts: While the game has an extreme amount of bang for your buck, for nearly a three year old game, It definitely felt like a breath of fresh air when it was released and stands out to this day from the yearly drag that Call of Duty has become in recent years, however at the end of the day, it is still Call of Duty and whether that is a good or bad thing is up to you. Iit is best to pick up this game on sale  for those hoping to jump in either to replay in preperation for Black Ops III, or if you are hoping to get warmed up come this November! Call of Duty Black Ops II remains as a great game to date and is fun across the single player campaign, multiplayer, and zombies. 4/5 stars
-PS: Be sure to get the season pass too!

The Call of Duty hate game is strong. Every year, thousands of gamers rush to the forums to vent their hatred for the infamous series. While many of the complaitns are fair complaints, they aren't complaints with the game more so with the popularity of the game.
Pros: the game controls almost perfectly. One of the upsides of making the same game over and over is you learn how to do it well. Your character responds precisely and quickly. Also, the zombies mode is awesome. I hate calling it perfect, but really it's extremely good. I found myself buying the game AGAIN on the xBox 360 JUST so I could do split screen zombies with my friends. Standard mode is good, and grief is entertaining, but really tranzit is the real gem here. Basically you travel map to map in a bus and can get different guns and do different things at each map. However if the bus leaves and you aren't on it, you can get stuck at one map for 4-5 turns with nothing but the wall weapons (usually). It's tense when the bus leaves and you're stuck surviving round 15 with almost no amunition for your good gun, knowing that if you don't get full ammo you'll be stuck with a pea shooter.
Cons: well, here's what most of you wanted to read. Firstly the multiplayer shows little to no energy. I'm not talking about reused ideas, more that what's there is done slopply at best. The maps are bland and ofter have spots that can be exploited to wreck havok. While it's fun when you're the one doing it, nothing sucks more than to die to an unkillable sniper. The single player isn't so much a con as it just is not great. It is short and for the most part forgetable. It's really just a feature rather than the main point of the game. Something to show in the trailers. Sure it has cool moments, but the futuristic tech is almost always (unfortunatly) just used in quicktime events and what you're left with is your average Call of Duty.
In short, if you're a fan of the series, go ahead and buy it. It's a faithful entery in the series with enough new features to keep you entertained. If you're not a fan, don't get it, there's nothing really new to change your mind. To be honest, it doesn't matter what I say because 99% already have made up your minds. If you're a fanboy you'll get it and if you just want the series to burn you won't buy it. The quality of the game wouldn't change very many of your minds...

EDIT: With the impending end of the first season of HITMAN upon us, I wanted to revisit this review and say where Hitman stands with me.
I f*cking love it. Although the annoying "online requirement" is still present, the game at least gives you a chance to reconnect if you are suddenly disconnected from the servers, unlike before where it would just kick you out of your current game. It's genuinely fun trying to achieve full mastery in each location; the game lets you unlock cool gadgets, weapons, and different starting spots as you achieve a higher "mastery" in each location.
Furthermore, the frequent crashing and framerate drops are pretty much nonexistent, and the game feels much more polished and refined. They continue to add content such as elusive targets and escalation contracts somewhat often, and new locations come in roughly once every two months(?)
Early on, the story really did not feel prevalent to the game, but I'm happy to say that I'm actually interested in how the story will shape up.
The game has class, style, and humor. Go out and buy it, I feel that personally it's worth the money I've put into it. Some things to note though: if you're going into the game wanting a third person shooter, this isn't the game for you. Hitman requires patience, strategy, stealth and accuracy. Can you just take a rifle and shoot everyone in your way? Sure, you can, but more often than not it is infinitely more rewarding to plan out and meticoulously set up your assassinations. IMO, this game is the second best game in the franchise, barely behind Blood Money. Only thing I miss dearly is the sniper briefcase, but I'm hopeful it comes in all its glory in the last episode coming out October 31st.

I really do like this game, how much freedom it gives you, all the awesome weapons, disguises, and scenarios that you find yourself in as Agent 47.
Before getting into the my big issue with the game I'd like to point out the smaller but still annoying issues of the game: random frame drops and freezes seem to be pretty common.
The only really BIG issue I have with this game though is their dependency on the "Hitman server's" being online. In all honesty, this really wouldn't be all THAT bad if all it did was just simply not put your "score" on the database. I could live with not having my ♥♥♥♥♥♥ score of -100,000 because I killed every guard in Paris. But no. Unfortunately, if your internet fails or for some other reason you are disconnected from the Hitman servers, it will kick you out of your current game (without giving time to save) and you are left with the bare bones of the game, no "perks" that you've unlocked through completing missions with better scores.
I really don't like the way many games and systems now a days rely so heavily on being connected, and Hitman seems to have 80% of its game online.
I wish I had more options for recommending from steam besides "Yes" and "No" because the game is AWESOME when it's at its best. However, like I lightly mentioned before, random frame drops and freezes seem to be pretty common, along with the whole connectivity issue.
For anyone looking to play this game, I wouldn't purchase it until the full game comes out and all the other kinks are straightened out. Right now it can be frustrating.

Euro Truck Simulator 2 is one of, if not the best, truck simulator game out there right now. It focuses on the very core of Europe; allowing you to create and grow your own trucking business to your own liking across the motorways and roads that spread across the land, with your own customised vehicle with many upgrades and additions that make the game dynamic and gripping.
- Huge map to a decent scale of Europe, including many of its key cities and locations that allow you to discover new places, stores, recruitment centres etc. encouraging you to explore - giving you an aim.
- Levelling system of unlocking new parts of the game, upgrades for your truck, and a business is brilliant - you are constantly striving to grow bigger and better.
- Ability to create, manage & expand your own business which operates all around Europe with your own staff, trucks, and money.
- Weather is although decent and realistic, only offers minimal options - features like snow would be a brilliant addition.
- Roads are repetitive and plain; however updates are routinely being brought out to help tackle this (as well as DLCs available to open more diverse locations).
- For the average gamer it may be seen that to set up a business and to customise your truck to a satisfactory level may take more time than would be preferred.
The game is a must if you are a truck fanatic or generally wanting the simulated experience, it offers a realistic approach to trucking in the modern day world. You even have the option of playing multiplayer with thousands of other truckers (an unofficial mod, but trusted by all) which makes the game more diverse and interesting than it already is. Buy it, and you definitely won't regret it.

I've got a Thrustmaster T300RS and I play a lot of Assetto Corsa. I love racing. I bought Euro Truck Simulator 2 for my girlfriend to practice driving in a "real-world" environment. ETS2 does this very well, it's very immersive and "real" driving conditions are well simulated. My girlfriend doesn't play ETS2 very much; I'm always playing it. Fun, immersive, awesome.

Euro Truck Simulator 2 is good as a simulator genre game. I'm not really into driving/racing games but this is fantastic. The feeling of driving around Europe just feels great. Most people aspire to go travelling, I know this is far from reality but you still get a feeling like that. It's awesome.
GAMEPLAY
Gameplay overall is good, travelling across Europe and delivering cargos is fun, but that's not the heart source for the fun. The fun comes in when you're driving normally. Remember the times when you would try to drive in GTA, normally? Like you would do in real life? Well, that's what this game is about. There is even a section in-game where you can add your own music (on the radio) and play it whilst driving. That's not a big part of the game though, I don't use it.  The trucks feel like trucks - you can definitley feel the weight being dragged on your back whilst driving past the 30 St Mary Axe also known as the Gherkin in London. There is a wide range of trucks to drive and after saving money by completing quick jobs you can eventually buy your own and drive freely. There is one bug which is constant throughout the game, unfortunately the only way to fix it is by going directly into the game files and changing a couple settings. The bug is when there are no jobs to do. Of course there are but they are not showing up therefore you can't do anything. Like I said, the gameplay is great, but that bug is annoying and we should not be fixing it ourselves.
7/10
GRAPHICS
The graphics are poor. No matter what setting you have them on, they are poor, it does not mean this is a bad game and you shouldn't get it. Look at Club Penguin. That's not even 3D yet but Club Penguin is fantastic! There is nothing more to say really, The textures for grass isn't 2D, that says enough.
4/10
MULTIPLAYER
The multiplayer function is a mod which you have to download from a certain website. With roughly 2000 players on each server, this is the best part about the game. I only play multiplayer because you can have a convoy with your friends and deliver your cargos together while passing the odd driver on his side in the middle of the road pleading for help. The admins run each server well and help keep it clean. There are rules though which you have to abide and if you break them you will get banned temporarily. In multiplayer, everything is the same, just without AI drivers around you. There are real people beside you and to be frankly honest, some of them are ♥♥♥♥♥♥s, not to worry though, press tab, click on the person that is bothering you and report them, they will soon be off your tail.
9/10
OPTIMIZATION
The game runs perfectly fine. I have a GTX970 and everything runs fine, with no mind-blowing graphics, nothing should make you drop frames. The only time I drop frames is when there is around 30 to 40 people in one city on Multiplayer, which might be a problem if you are in the same town and the same server with well known streamers such as Squirrel, famously known for playing Simulator games.
9/10
OVERALL
Overall, game is brilliant, it is worth the buy but not the 97% reviews. The only reason why I don't think it is worth the 97% is because of that bug that we have to fix ourselves. SCS should've fixed that a long time ago. I'm excited to play American Truck Simulator but I'm waiting for the Multiplayer Mod. The graphics are poor but if you judge the entirety of a games fun down to graphics then you are deluded (ง ͠° ͟ل͜ ͡°)ง and the optimization is fine. If you are looking to buy this game, just keep an open mind as even I, the reviewer was not into driving games, but this takes it to another level for me.
Thank you for reading

I've played a lot of visual novels, and a good half of them or so have been dating sims of some kind. My experience with dating sims in North America has been rather disappointing, compared to some of the treasured stories I've read that come from Japan or South Korea, so when I saw Dream Daddy release with fanfare, I had very low expectations.
And I was pleasantly surprised!
Dream Daddy went forth and crafted a scenario with an inclusive heart. You build your dadsona in a character creator, which can feature a binder, implying your dadsona is transgender. Your daughter's late parent can be male or female. The only thing you can't be is completely heterosexual, since this is a dating sim where you are a man dating other dads. Other characters in the story are gay, lesbian, bisexual and transgender as well. Not only that, but there are plenty of people of colour.
Also his game is very funny. It executes pro writing and great comedy while also letting every character have depth. I laughed. A lot.
All of the best dating sims revolve around a character's flaws. A route revolves around these, and the main character helps them to grow in spite of them. This is also the case in how the romances are written in Dream Daddy.
Each of the dads is working through his own problem. Some of them are huge character flaws that have left them rotting in misery, while other ones are lighter, less inconvenient things. Either way, your influence changes them, which is good romance writing. This means that the characters with the more terrible flaws have become more popular, because they're more interesting. I hope the writers learn from this part.
I played through each route (and Robert's twice, because his plays very differently if you put out on the first date) and I've logged 13.3 hours, according to Steam. Compare this to Dandelion ~Wishes Brought to You~ which earned us 39 hours. Dandelion is $33 Canadian, so the price-to-time value for Dream Daddy ($17 Canadian) is less than half of a game like Dandelion. This might not be a thing that matters to you, but that time could have given us more about the Dads that we love. I would have happily paid more for a longer game, but I know that might not be the case for everyone. (I'm just thinking that I should have waited for the game to go on sale. I don't make enough in ad revenue for this!)
Dream Daddy also doesn't follow all of the usual trappings of an eastern-made dating sim, and is most notably missing a "true ending". Dating Sims often have a mystery interwoven into the text that is only discovered once you've seen each character's route. Dream Daddy does not yet have this.
If you're looking for a game that will warm your heart and make you happy, this is the one to do it. I can't promise that the endings will all give you what you want, but in the end they're an expression of the Dad's development and autonomy, which is my favorite part about the whole thing. The characters are wonderful, each in their own way. They're flawed. They make mistakes. Sometimes you can help them, and sometimes you can't. Sometimes you don't know what the right answer is, but that's okay. Love isn't always easy.
I recommend the game if you enjoy character depth, and also laughing.

A good Star Wars 3D Arcade platform game that lets you create your own Jedi character. There are 5 races divided as 2 for male, 2 for female and the shared one being human. Looks are just for aesthetic purposes and you get a voice depending on gender and a Unisex name for your character. Female played characters may or may not recognize Jenifer Hale's voice here.
In its retro style, various Star Wars iconic planets are visited here such as Tatooine and Hoth and a couple of characters make an appearance too. Not Including main story missions after each tier such as Hoth there are 3 tiers of main missions and each tier has about 5 or 6 missions and there is usually one mission that is a little different to the others in each tier. There is an option to skip one mission before moving on with the story which I think is a great idea if you don't like that different style or maybe a mission you just don't want to do for whatever reason. Whatever you do just be ready for some cheesy acting and story telling.
Fighting through the levels with lightsabres feels fun and most levels you get to level up your light or dark force powers between tiers 1-3 of power rating. Neutral powers upgrade normally as the story progresses and later you get to choose duel or a double sabre. Personally I like to blast enemies with Force Lightning and use Force Grip or Push/Pull to knock enemies off high ledges which does have a sort of comedy element to it. Fighting dark force users will involve more lightsabre duels with powers thrown in.  I think some things should be tuned a bit such as when using your force to jump slows down the action and sometimes you need to wait while it recharges before making another jump or task.
This is an old game now and it shows with its 3D style arcade platforming and controls can sometimes feel clunky. The visuals are old too but not bad and don't have so much of those modern day evil effects like Depth of field. The game can also be challenging and even on easy you can be one shot sometimes if you are caught offguard or unlucky but mostly feels fair and you can save mostly anywhere.
I would love to see a modern take of this kind of game now with all the choices this game gives you and without any modern take of ransoming options as DLC.
Lastly there is a free for all dueling multiplayer mode which can be fun and includes Bots and many character skins from the game. Many games sadly don't have such features anymore.  Also there is mod Support for the game but you will have to look online for them. This game would really benefit from a Steam Workshop :)

Splice is a very unique puzzle game. It's basically the concept of creating a specific binary tree with special nodes and moving smaller trees (splicing) to make a goal pattern/layout.  This gameplay is very logic dependent and an intriguing concept, but the game doesn't provide much context to your input or any form of hints system.  They do offer a sort of time reversal system and a simple undo, but some of the design decisions are questionable to me and this game could have benefited from a clearer input tutorial.
Things I really liked about Splice: the atmosphere of the game is pretty calm and soothing with a beautiful soundtrack and very ambient aesthetics; some of the angelic solutions (optimal moves to save as many splices as possible) are brilliantly designed; the concepts don't overstay their welcome too much with only 7 levels per sequence and the levels can be solved fairly quickly unless you get stumped.
Aspects that didn't click with me: minimal tutorial/context to input (a tool tip or two wouldn't hurt when a player gets stuck; just have a setting in the menu to enable/disable hints if they are purists); unfortunately a lot of the levels feel very similar to others and portions of the main sequence levels don't distinguish themselves particularly well; clearer menu system from the select screen to help identify potential angelic levels would be appreciated.
I got stuck for about 10-15 minutes on around 2 or 3 levels for the main sequences, but I didn't really care to plan my moves as I started to lose interest by that time [I was on the last series of levels].  The epilogue levels have some really neat puzzles and patterns they want you to understand, but it started to feel a lot like Computer Science work to me near the end and it might become too much pre planning with all the combinations for some folks.
Overall, Splice gets a Below Average Recommendation unless you're a Puzzle aficionado and for those people it would be an Above Average Recommendation.  Splice is a neat experiment that can provide a cerebral evening or short bursts of puzzle solving split up into smaller segments over a few days.  I'd just suggest keeping your Google-fu handy to get hints or some tools nearby to draw out the various combinations.

Another great game by Cipher Prime.
It is obvious by now that Cipher Prime (makers of auditorium, intake and fractal) really know how to make puzzle games with amazing visuals, and I was pleasantly surprised with Splice. This was a game I got in a bundle and was pretty much 100% that I would never even play, let alone finish.
There’s many great things about this game and I guess I’ll start with the visuals.
Splice is lovely‘n’bright and full of colour. It’s just great to look at, plus there’s a really nice feeling to this game which the music also contributes a lot to. It’s calm and casual to play but not short of a challenge, that’s for sure. The mechanics are great, and the whole concept works well with them. You use different little cells with different ability’s to solve the puzzles, and it really makes you think about what you are doing. Towards the end of the play through my head really did start to hurt, but the game is so pretty and interesting I would always be coming back to it. I was motivated enough to want to complete this game, and that is a LOT coming from someone that usually hates puzzle games and gives up after the first few levels.
It is a fairly lengthy game for an indie, seven levels in each sequence (I think) and seven sequences for the main game, plus an extra 4 sequences in the epilogue series. It may take a little bit, depending on how good you are with the puzzles of course, it personally took me just under 6 hours play time over the course of a few weeks or so, so it isn’t a game you can whizz through in an hour or two (unless you are insanely good at the puzzles), but in all fairness I think it’s worth the time and experience. It’s a great game and I would recommend it to anyone that wanted to try something a bit different.
I would also recommend Cipher Primes other games to.
All in all, awesome game. Try it out.

Typical Warner Bros button mash em up...but wait! They're onto something here!
Mad Max has a great deal of repetition, there is no doubt. Combat is repetitive and extremely easy - to the point where towards the end of the game I just started mashing my controller buttons like I did for Batman: AA. Bosses are equally all the same, with the only difference being one of colour and more health. The same attack formula ALWAYS works.
The world is beautifully created and exhibits atmosphere and mystery. Sadly this is let down the moment you realise that the huge map is split into 5 zones. Each zone has a large base structure, in which Max will be based once he can impress it's owner. In order to do that you need to improve said base by collecting 4-5 'Projects' that are scattered around the wasteland. Repeat this for all the other remaining bases and things quickly get repetitious.
In order to maintain and improve your car, you require SCRAP. This is dotted about the landscape and luckily in large amounts, so upgrading your car is nice and eas...no it's not. For some silly reason (See WB) all the upgrades are locked until you lower the threat rating in a respective zone by carrying out missions. In doing so induces a grind, in which you eventually max (hurrrr) out your car right at the end - when most of the zones are completely cleared! "Ah but you can simply select New Game+ and..." No you can't - there's nothing of the sort here.
So after 51hours I have finished the main mission, and have one minor side mission remaining, that needs to be performed at night. Only problem is, the sense of time progression ingame is very odd and you cannot fast forward time apart from via the main story missions that are now finished. So I'm out of luck there and no time fast forward mechanic seems to exist looking at various forums/reddit.
After all that has been said, one would think I wouldn't recommend Max Payne er Mad Max even. However there are a lot of positives
- Gorgeously created world
- The ingame engine runs superbly with great sound/storm effects too!
- Excellent story (takes place post Mad Max: Fury Road)
- Driving/Combat is excellent. Convoy battles are sadly very limited in quantity but great fun.
- Great characters
- You get a DOG
- Engine upgrades are meaty sounding!
Whilst I initially struggled with the game early on in, things do level out towards the end (a bit late if you ask me) and the story kicks into gear too. It is a shame we will never see any updates to the game as a New Game+ mode would be most welcome. If you enjoyed watching Mad Max: Fury Road, you will positively LOVE this.

"Batman Arkham Origins" is the third part of the adventures of Batman in the Arkham universe. This time , however, Rocksteady studio is not in charge of development. This episode was made vy Warner Brothers Montreal , and the multiplayer mode was created by studio Splash Damage. Acquisition of rights for Batman by other studios made me a little concerned. Batman games have become one of the best games of all time for me. That's why I was not able to understand why the development was given to another team.
When we start, the game greets us with about 40 seconds of videos presenting companies that was involved in making this product. You can not skip them of course , but you can disable it by adding the command in the steam launch options. This does not change the fact that for the average player videos will be very annoying. Game options are quite extensive and certainly I can not complain about the lack of customization , the only thing I lacked in this section is the lack of key mapping for quick use of gadget. I personally liked to set it to use under the separate button , but somehow I can get over the double keystrokes gadgets.
Graphically the game looks solid, although really little has changed on this issue since Batman Arkham City . But when we play longer we can notice a lot of glitchy graphics. Cloak often decides to ignore the laws of physics and perform odd stunts. Batman apparently got used to this state of affairs, because it absolutely does not impress him. However, the most drastic visual mistake for which I came across is gliding. Quite often when we fly Batman can't decide whether he is gliding or landing and begins to hop up and down on the screen.
Combat mechanics are solid as usual , however, almost nothing new was added. The only variety that have been changed ( not even added) is gadgets. Background music is as always spectacular and well fits the atmosphere of Arkham.
But how the game's storyline, look? In contrast to the previous titles , this title wanted to show us an inexperienced Batman , who just starts on his way to fight crime. So how Batman shows his inexperience? Here lies a problem. Batman is the same as always, we cannot see that he just started his career. There's not many inserts that tell us about it . At the beginning the villains do not believe in the existence of Batman, but after playing 30 minutes of gameplay they all definitely know the Human Bat is real. Amazingly Batman made earlier his Batwing than the Batmobile, which still lies in scraps in his bat cave. Once we're about two hours into the game, Batman shows his lack of experience when one of the criminals escapes after being knocked down and not tied by Batman. In my opinion, developers didn't use all the opportunities of Batman being in the beginning of his career.
Well everything , though perhaps less polished, was in the previous parts. In this game , however, there is added multiplayer mode. In multiplayer we have a chance to play one of the subordinates of Joker or Bane, as well as Batman or Robin. Both criminals factions are fighting each other by taking control of places that allow them to earn domination points. The team that accumulates more points wins the match. All the time during this struggle they must also think about Batman and Robin who have the task to stop the criminals. Team Batman wins when bar of terror is filed, and they earn it by doing more and more interesting knockouts, and eliminating team captains. For a long time there was no asymmetrical multiplayer game and I must admit that it is made very well in this one. But the problem arises when someone has a poor internet connection. During my battles in multiplayer very often I've seen players teleporting all around the screen, and some looked like their game just freezed.
Overall, the game is very nice but does not seem as solidly polished as the previous parts of Batman. After all, the announcement of the new DLC before the solution of technical problems with the game, left me a big disgust . Multiplayer is very nice as far as opponents do not teleport on the the screen. If you are not tired of the previous parts of Batman you can go ahead and reach for the title, although I would wait until all the problems that the game has are fixed. Which apparently will never be fixed. On official forums WB montreal's community manager wrote that they are not planing to fix any more bugs that aren't blocking player from finishing the game, cause they are busy working on new DLC for batman. Just for that reason I would say that you shouldn't buy this product. It's really sad how impudent this developer is.

Max Payne is the perfect combination of an over-the-top third person action game mixed with a great noir atmosphere and cheesy 80s style one-liners and dialogue.
The gameplay is spectacular. It is simple, raw and challenging. Even on the easiest difficulty one shotgun wound at close range is enough to kill you. It is always a blast to enter bullet time and clear out a whole room full of baddies with your dual pistols or your assault rifle. It's mind-blowing how even after all these years the gunplay still holds up to this day and manages to deliver a very fun and enjoyable experience. The sound effects are also great, as is the soundtrack - even if for most of the game there is no music and the track list isn't very long.
The story is a typical tale of revenge. What makes it stand out is the excellent Noir vibe that Max Payne's New York gives out and the dialogue which are can be so cheesy and oldschool, it's amazing. Max's one-liners in particular are too good to miss out on.
I should point out that when playing the game on Windows 7 or 10, you may experience sound issues, Thankfully there is a fix which you can find in the guides for the game that will sort out the issue. The game isn't very long either and I could live without the dream sequences. And yes, the graphics haven't aged terribly well. Even so, the game does have replay value with its several difficulties as well as the New York Minute mode and the gunplay more than makes up for the game's shortcomings.
Overall, Max Payne is a blast from the past. It is a phenomenal third person shooter with a solid story and great atmosphere. I can not recoomend this game enough. It was one of my favorite games ever as a kid and playing it once more after so many years only made me appreciate the game more.

Absolutely amazing game. I was early backer and yes game had it's highs and lows through developement and yes there was some content that was cut. Game developement isn't just so straight forward process, it could be handled better but in the end I think we got a great game. I've played a lot of PnP Numenera and they just nailed the 9th World atmosphere. Story and characters are great, every NPC has nice background and you'll have walls and walls of text to read and immerse yourself in fantastic world of Numenera. Other thing is exploration, explore everything, tinker with stuff you find, try to find out how it works and what you can do with it if it works (or if it doesn't!). This game is AWESOME. If you want a good story and reactivity, I can't recommend it enough. It has great writing, an interesting setting, the locations look amazing, soundtrack is good and I had no problems or bugs at release. It has a lot of text and very little combat - the focus here is on story and exploration, not tactics. Combat is not only rare but always avoidable - every problem has multiple possible solutions, and combat is just one of those. The game if somewhat short, but very involved: every dialogue is full of options, and even straight up failure often opens new and interesting paths (sometimes failure gets the most interesting outcome). There is a lot of interconnected options, with subtle consequences for most of your choices (even the seemingly unimportant ones). There is also a lot of explore, items to discover, things to meddle with and find out what they do... even if it sometimes kills you. Especially if sometimes it kills you - finding ways to die is actually kind of important for some quests.
The setting is very weird, but in a good way. Places and people and items are unique and fun to learn about, instead of another old story about the lost dwarven kingdom or the millistaristic alien society. Instead you have veterans of a psychic war, a whole city inside a huge blobby creature and ancient... candy dispensers. It is sometimes grandious, sometimes creepy, sometimes philosophical, sometimes gruesome, sometimes silly.
Now, this game was crowdfunded, and in this aspect the game was a huge disappointment. The developers made super ambitious promises that they weren't able to fulfill, made some big changes and didn't communicate well. But if you are planning to buy this after release, this doesn't really matter for you... it's just us backers being bitter.

This game is surely not for everybody, which might explain the many negative reviews in steam, but it also offers a depth in storytelling and world building that most games do not.

The drawn backgrounds look at least good and sometimes awesome and some even made me stop and admire them in awe. Also the locations are packed with details and always look promising. The character models are not that detailed and their animations are rather rudimentary.
The music and sound effects are rather reserved but do their job well.

A big plus are the various solutions the game offers to solve a problem, mostly considering various positions and make choices that are both reflecting the attitude of the character and have understandable consequences for the game world. In other words: It really makes sense to role-play and get involved into the world. A minus point is the rather thin combat system as it does not allow much strategic thinking and is more a means to an end than a complex system.

As already mentioned, it is often possible to solve problems in multiple ways and even failures can lead to new paths. There is also a good mixture of dialogues, exploration and riddles. Some combats seemed a bit unfair, also due to the limited range of actions available.
Here it is where the game shines the most. From what I have seen so far, the texts (there are a lot of them) are excellent and do not only make up for the missing voice overs or lack of visualization, but enabled me to create an even more dense world inside my head. This is both true for the dialogues, the descriptions of the environment and the interactions with the objects in the world. I really care for the fate of my character and want to know more about him and his origins and how he will develop.
I have not backed  this game and only played very little of Planescape Torment but so far it has been a really unique experience and it makes me sad to see that the game receives rather mixed reviews on steam.
I hope this review sheds some better light on the game which it definitely deserves.

A genuine masterpiece that subverts and deconstructs its genre, Spec Ops takes you on a journey through a beautifully crafted and increasingly hellish world in which you are forced to face the consequences of your actions - 10/10

Spec Ops: The Line, is not really a fun and enjoyable game at its core, which is why it's so interesting, especially as just one (pretty short campaign with not very much multiplayer) shooter in a world where shooters are released en masse. Mechanically speaking, Spec Ops is a pretty standard third person shooter - two weapons at any one time , three throwables, and a selection of alternate weapon options with a comparatively smooth cover system. I did not really like the inability to aim and fire while sprinting, but that's a bit of a minor issue that I feel can be overlooked.
The graphics are reasonably good, especially for a game released in 2012. The background and setting is particularly well done, well able to convey a sense of a city tearing itself apart, and also the issues that have arisen from a city cut off from the rest of the world. It is a pretty brutal Dubai that you find yourself in, and the game conveys the sense of horror that has descended on the city very well.
The soundtrack is fantastic. Both it, and the storyline, short it may be, are probably the standout features of the game for me. Evoking imagery of Apocalypse Now, Spec Ops: The Line shows just how nightmarish and hellish war really is, apart from the glorified imagery that certain media has portrayed it as. Offering a look at the damage that can be done to a soldier's psyche from tours of duty, it also offers a look at the chain of command, something that is explored comparatively rarely. Offering questions regarding morality and cause and effect, while short, Spec Ops: The Line is well worth playing through.

English(ishish) version:
First of all, I'd like to adress two main concerns regarding HITMAN - always online feature and the fact that it's being release as an episodic game. Not one of these two thins are a real problem, as far as I can see. The whole problem around always online feature is absolutely unnecessary and pointless. Without any intention of spending my time on explaining why it doesn't matter, I have to admit that being always online is never going to be a dealbreaker for me. It's pointless since we're online anyways. The only drawback that I can see is that Squeenix and IO have decided to store our saves online, rather than doing so on our precious SSDs. In case of a disaster, disconnecting from the servers means that all unsaved process is lost. Bad, but not *that* bad.
Another thing, as I've mentioned previously, that many people see as troublesom is the fact that Squeenix and IO are releasing HITMAN as an episodic game. This isn't something new, just think of all TellTale games that have come out. Also, I'd like to remind you of all the DLCs that many modern shooter get (Battlefield and Call of Duty). This isn't something new and never before seen. It's something we've gotten used to and, frankly saying - HITMAN is just the right game for this sort of thing. With episodic content, HITMAN is able to deliver its content in its full glory. Instead of rushing through campaign (which has around 7 or eight maps) and complaining how short the game is - players will play it for months on end. We'll get to enjoy elusive contracts, contracts our friends and other players have made, special content and all sorts of things that devs can come up. Not to mention that maps themselves offer countless challenges and achievements. I can understand that some people might feel a bit underwhelmed and bored by replaying same map over and over again but... Hitman has always been about exactly that - find your target and utilize countless ways of disposing of them. Play, succeed and repeat.
As far as gameplay goes, HITMAN is rather good, even if it still isn't on-par with its predecessors (not Absolution! everything trumps Absolution). The biggest problem in the game is that it often feels rushed. There's no real opportunity to let player see things and plan his own way. Rather, we're forced to rush to certain events while AI mindlessly follows the same routine, over and over again. It can get irrititating sometimes, but given how gameplay options allow us to tweak the game - it can also be much more fun! I'd say that, when gameplay of any Hitman game is questioned, it is all up to the player and how they play. Some might argue that Hitman games are all about being slow, metodical and surgically precise (me me me!) while others might like to speed up things and "just do it". I'd say that the latter shouldn't really even be bothering with Hitman.
All things said and done, Paris is a solid outing into the world of Hitman. It's really big. Much bigger than anything we've seen in Absolution. If my memory serves me right, I've seen bigger maps in Hitman II: Silent Assassin, but I can't say that for sure. The important thing is that there's a lot of room for improvement that's needed. HITMAN must be polished and advanced if IO and Squeenix want to keep gamers interested for another six months.
Non-English version:
Prije svega mislim da je potrebno da se" skinu dvije stvari sa dnevnog reda" - "uvijek online" i epizodni karakter igre. Niti jedna od dvije spomenute stvari meni ne predstavlja problem. Cijela hajka koja se digla oko "uvijek online" zahtjeva od strane Squeenixa i IO Interactive je apsolutno bespotrebna i predstavlja tipično i besmisleno kukanje. Nemam namjeru da trošim riječi (dalje) i da objašnjavam zašto to nije loše no, barem kada se ja pitam, zahtjev da gamer bude uvijek online nije i nikada neće biti "dealbreaker". Istina, ima tu jedna velika mana - autosave funkcija je vezana za Squeenixove servere - no i to se da zaobići redovnim snimanjem igre.
Druga stvar za koju se veže najveća kontraverza kada je Hitman u pitanju je epizodno izdavanje igre. Iako ovakva praksa nije nešto novo u gamingu, jeste ipak nešto novija kada su u pitanju shooteri (treba izignorisati činjenicu da smo ovo vidjeli prije kod raznih Battlefield i Call of Duty naslova). Zasigurno da ovakva metoda ima kako mane tako i prednosti. Jedna od najvećih prednosti je činjenica da je Hitman jednostavno jeftin! Na mjesečnoj bazi, nakon tzv. "uvodnog paket", igra košta svega osam eura! Mogućnost da se /legalno/ nabavi 3A naslov po toj cijeni je apsolutno smiješna. Naravno, nedostatci se ogledaju najviše u samom igraču. Postoje oni koji će igru prije svega gledati kroz single-player kampanju i čiji će cilj biti da istu pređu u što kraćem roku. Takvim igračima će i cijela igra sa svega sedam (ili osam, nisam siguran) mapa biti prekratka. Tu su, također, i oni drugi koji će gledati da progiraju što više mogu. Upravo je takvim igračima Hitman i namjenjen. Uz dosta dodatnog sadržaja koji obuhvata razne izazove, achievemente te niz "ugovora", čak i jedna mapa iz Hitmana može da potraje barem desetak sati igre i to bi trebalo biti i više no dovoljno za cijenu koja se plaća. Mislim da na kraju vrijedi spomenuti kako mojoj malenkosti epizodno izdavanje igara, barem kada je Hitman u pitanju, itekako ima smisla i ne gledam na to kao na neki veliki minus. Znam da neće svi dijeliti isto mišljenje ali barem treba pokušati sagledati stvari iz drugog ugla pa tek onda pljuvati i kukati.
Kada je u pitanju gameplay, Hitman je poprilično dobar iako i dalje odudara od starijih naslova (poredim sa drugim dijelom u serijalu koji je i dan-danas jedna od najboljih igara koje sam ikada odigrao). Najveći problem cijele igre je što se često ima osjećaj kao da je igra zbrzana jer više ne postoji ideja planiranja i skautiranja prije "napada". Umjesto toga, posebno kada se uključe sve stavke u opcijama, igra postaje poprilično lagana. Čak i sa isključenim instinktom te smanjenim informacijama za izazove i objektive, igra je i dalje poprilično lagana i odudara od starijih naslova. U želji da stvore dinamičan i brz gameplay, Squeenix je odbacio ideju planiranja (tu u igru ulaze tzv. izazovi) te polaganog nastupa. Pariz, koji slovi kao jedna od većih mapa (mada to i nije, realno govoreći bilo je mnogo većih mapa u Silent Assassinu) je moguće završiti za nekoliko minuta. Opet, naravno, ovo sve zavisi od pristupa. No onaj ko je volio Hitmana zbog same ideje da je igru potrebno igrati prije svega pametno i strpljivo sada i neće baš biti oduševljen no neće biti ni potpuno razočaran.
No, sve ovo na stranu, Pariz ipak ima i svojih prednosti. Mapa je zaista velika, mnogo veća nego ono što smo gledali u Absolutionu. A ukoliko igrač isključi par opcija u gameplay sekciji, igra može biti interesantnija. I dalje postoji mogućnost izbora a opcije koje igra nudi igraču su ogromne (negdje sam pročitao da se glavni likovi u Parizu mogu ubiti na više od pedeset! načina).
Na kraju vrijedi spomenuti performanse igre. Obzirom da se radi o prvom DX12 naslovu koji sam imao prilike igrat, nisam nešto pretjerano sretan. DX12 ne funkcioniše kako treba i sama igra ima problema koje Squeenix još uvijek nije uspio riješiti. DX11 radi poprilično dobro, sve dok ne pretjerujete sa stavkama. Treba držati na umu da je jednostavni broj NPC-eva koji se pojavljuju u igri ogroman i da to zahtjeva ogromne resurse. Šesnaest giga rama, i5-2500k, r9 270 dc oc, mogu igru pokretati (na 1080p rezoluciji) na srednjim postavkama.
TL;DR: Šta je tu je, nekima će se svidjeti a nekima neće.

Heavy Bullets is a rogue-lite (not roguelike, which I'll get to later) FPS that ISN'T a terrible game, but not something that I would recommend.
Let's start with some pros and cons:
Pros:
-Level generation is very good and provides a high level of area variety with the occasional secret.
-The ammo system of retrieving your scarce bullets flows very well.
-In my experience, the game performed very, very well. No performance issues.
-Gameplay is fast with little downtime.
Cons:
-The game has VERY LITTLE content, and a pretty good amount of that content isn't very exciting. Within 3 hours of play, I had reached the final boss and experienced most of what the game has to offer.
-The graphics and sound, while part of the game's specific art style, are abysmal.
-Gameplay is VERY unbalanced. You will encounter large numbers of trivial creatures, while occasionally facing off against turrets that are much, much more powerful. While there are plenty of effective strategies I used against these turrets, I found that they are very inconsistent; with buggy mobile varieties that can glitch and shoot through walls, and stationary varieties that can turn their gun a full 180 degrees in the blink of an eye. This makes gameplay against these foes extremely frustrating.
-The game offers the ability to save your money and items for later runs, but this is very slow, boring, and grind-y. This is also the reason why this game should be considered a rogue-lite rather than a true roguelike.
Some other points to consider:
-There is no real story present except for a few lines of start-up text, but this isn't really a bad point in my eyes; I'd rather have no story than an awful story.
Overall, I'd say that Heavy Bullets isn't a bad title to play if you get it on sale (AT LEAST 50% off) or in a Humble Bundle (I got it in the Humble Roguelike Bundle), but you are overpaying if you pay the full $9.99 for it.
Thanks for reading (assuming you did).

I have a bit of a weak spot for Roguelikes, so when I saw this on sale, I had to check it out. Overall, I'm quite content with my decision to buy this game, although there's still a few things that really prevent me from fully enjoying it.
The pros:
1. One thing I really like about this game is that each enemy is unique and challenging in their own way. No one enemy feels too easy or hard too fight by themselves.
2. A problem that you sometimes see with games that have randomly generated levels is that they occassionally throw something nigh-unbeatable at you if you're unlucky. This game never does that. It gets harder as you go, but every death you have feels like its because of a mistake on your part, not on the game's part.
3. There is a small way that you can make future playthroughs easier. By storing money in the bank, you can have a large stockpile of cash to use in different playthroughs to make things easier. If you have a lot of trouble with this game, or if you run across some items that you want to buy but don't have enough money for, the bank has you covered. This really helps to take the edge off of this game's difficulty.
The cons:
Now that I've gotten the praise out of the way, let me address the one thing that "prevents me from fully enjoying this" as I said. During the beginning of the game, I noticed that it had the occasional stutter. By this, I mean that the game had a rare lag spike, in which everything would freeze for a second, before it would unfreeze, with me in a different spot. Splice is a puzzle game that has an extremely high production value.  The music and aesthetic of the game provide an almost ethereal feel to the player as they play it, kind of a trippy, mind-effecting theme going on.  Playing it reminded me of the Cylon Basestar section of the Battlestar Galactaga series.  For that alone Splice is worth playing, but the gameplay is so polished, the graphics are so sharp, and the music is so excellently packaged together with everything else I'd say it would be a shame if you didn't at least give Splice a try.  I was extremely impressed with this puzzler and, while not the most head-scratchingly difficult puzzler I've ever played (it has a rewind feature a-la Braid so you can work on puzzles for as long as you want without penalty) the puzzles aren't easy and there are a lot of variables that can make you pause for a moment to think about your next action.
The gameplay of Splice is quite simple, easy to pick up, hard to master, as I always say of good puzzlers.  You have a bacterial strain and move the pieces around to try and fill the silouettes provided on each level.  There are "special" sections of the strain that do various things, like extend, or split the strain, duplicating the amount of cells you have.  You have a lmited amount of moves to complete the puzzle; however, using "special" sections of a strain don't cost a move to use, so that adds an additional layer of strategy to Splice.
Even if the puzzles were bad (which they're not), just playing this game is a nice, chill, experience.  The feeling I got while playing it reminded me a lot of playing Flow, the ambiance this game exudes is just otherworldly and really the biggest selling point of this game for me.
Come for the puzzles, stay for the experience. B+

I kickstarted this game as soon as I found out about it after having kickstarted Wasteland 2 from the same developer. Numenera was a big name at the time and I was excited to play in that world.
I just finished my first playthrough of this game, having completed every quest I found (except one, which I completed and which did not, for some reason, complete in my journal). While I do have some complaints about the title, I give this game two thumbs up. Pillars of Eternity did not set my character in the game world. Tyranny tried, but soon became boring. This game, on the other hand, drew me into the story right away.
Before I go on, please note: This game is not Planescape: Torment. The developers touted that name in order to get people excited, and blowhards never figured out what "spiritual successor" really means, so there are a lot of people disappointed that this game is not Planescape. If you are expecting Planescape.. well, move on. This game will never be Planescape.
Pros:
+ Fantastic story with good pacing. At over 50 hours, I read everything, explored every item description, journeyed through every mere, and absorbed all the lore I could find. It was never a slog to read like Witcher 3 or Mass Effect 1.
+ Weird setting. Numenera is all about the Weird. The tabletop RPG has a ho-hum system with some serious flaws, but most people enjoy the setting enough to put up with the system. Tides of Numenera rips the setting free and spares us the flaws of critical failures being as common as critical successes or average success. I don't want to spoil anything - if you're familiar with the Numenera setting, I think you will be happy with this game's use of it.
+ Choice. Many conflicts can be solved in multiple interesting ways. A lot of games give you a 'choice' but it tends to revolve around cardboard morality, black hat/white hat tripe. Here is a game where you can speed through using the standard Bioware-type actions, or put some thought into your actions and discover really cool solutions that add to the story and setting.
+ No meaningless combat encounters. Remember Baldur's Gate and having to fight wolf after wolf forever, regardless of your power level? The endless slog of going through dungeons without challenge, knowing you're going to annihilate everything in your path? All of the fights in this game make logical sense and none feel they were placed just to prop up playtime.
+ Inventory that's part of the world. This intersects with setting a bit, but I can't stress how much I wish other games would take a lesson. Don't just give me a shiny new sword and leave the story up to my imagination. Tons of oddities and artifacts can be used and will present anything from puzzles, filler stories, meaningful narrative, to useful rewards. Quest items in most games are used once and forgotten, but many quest items can be used multiple times and often in interesting ways. Again, this makes sense if you know the Numenera setting. If you're only familiar with the old Infinity Engine games, make sure you're reading your item descriptions and checking what can be used.
Cons:
- Awful character customization. You are given no choice over how your character looks despite your gender. Devs tried to say it was because you are learning to live in a copy, but let's be honest here - if you pick a female, you're still interacting with a Changing God who is a male. There's no compelling reason I see that they would not allow you to customize your appearance except that they didn't want to take the time/resources to allow it. There is literally no part of your character's appearance that could not be customized and still remain plot-relevant.
- Awful use of Descriptors. Descriptors are probably the coolest part of character creation in the Numenera tabletop RPG and this game does the absolute worst job it possibly could at picking fun ones for you to try. They could explain this away by giving you a flat Descriptor like the one Rhin uses, to explain the various powers you have from your progenitor. But they don't. They shoehorn in 3 boring descriptors that give you no awesome powers whatsoever. It's a travesty.
- Sparse combat. If you love these games because you love tactical RPGs, I would stay far away. If you love min-maxing, I don't think this will scratch your itch, either. Combat is fleeting and you can play for hours without coming into a battle unless you push to instigate the few you find, especially early on in the game. What this means, really, is that you gain levels and are forced to choose several powers *before you ever really understand how combat works in the game.* Don't get me wrong, I appreciate not having random encounters with 15 wolves around every corner I turn - at the same time, exploring "dangerous" areas of the cities you explore feels exactly the same as exploring the safe areas. Also, combat in the tabletop RPG is fun, for the most part, especially because of Descriptors (see above). They could have done SO MUCH MORE.
- Frustrating camera controls. While not a dealbreaker, because this game's combat becomes extremely easy later on... the isometric view combined with the way they use triggers means that sometimes you have the ability to walk further on a map, but you can't, because your pathing ends too close to a door or something else and you can't prioritize your walk action over interacting with whatever object is in the way. Related: some rooms that *look* symmetrical are not, as you cannot properly walk behind all walls equally, and sometimes one or two characters can block a hallway that looks wide enough for three or four.
- Grammar errors. I can't remember seeing any typographical errors, but at times it felt like the entire script was run through a spellchecker and autocorrected rather than having humans read and correct sentences that don't make sense. It wasn't a huge deal, but when 98% of your game is reading, the reading should probably be polished, yeah?
- Disappointing ending. I remember the first time I beat Rygar on the NES. The ending screen was just a short blurb of text. Fine for an NES game. When I beat this, I got to make a choice, but I was treated to the same - a short blurb of text. It was super vague and I learned nothing of anyone I had grown to care about while playing. I wanted to know if Zebb and Nym's father turned his life around and made their family happy again, for example. I wanted to see what happened to.. well, ANY of the playable NPCs. Granted, I only beat the game once as of writing this; maybe there are better endings if you choose a different option. I hope so, for your sake. But this game's ending made Mass Effect 3 seem like War and Peace by comparison, while this would be Cliff Notes for Green Eggs and Ham.
- Lackluster companions. Okay, they weren't bad, and I loved Rhin to death. But they weren't anything close to, say, Baldur's Gate 2's chatty, loveable NPCs. And there aren't even enough to play a few times using different rosters (I think there should be at least 2-3 more companion choices). Meanwhile, they almost never interact with each other the way we've come to love (and expect) in our RPGs. They also very rarely comment on choices you make compared to other games. They are definitely a part of the scenery compared to the numenera and non-playable NPCs you'll meet, at least 90% of the time.
I could probably come up with more pros and cons, but at this point you might ask, with such heavy cons, why would you still recommend this? Well, because I had fun. A lot of fun. And if you can live with the cons, and the pros sound good to you, I think you'll like it too. Happy playing!

It's surprisingly good.
In terms of Steam games that I began playing in Early Access, this is one of three (Terraria and Kerbal Space Program being the others) that I would readily rank ahead of numerous triple-AAA titles.
So, let's get the main question out of the way immediately: I strongly recommend this game if you're really into the Tycoon/Sim style of game. I'd probably give this about a 7.8/10, to be honest, which is solid for $29.99, but is a steal if you can get it cheaper.
Now to the rationale for my decision:
---------------------------------------------
GOOD :
You can play it on a simple level, or on a complex one, and it remains just as fun. If you enjoy sitting and connecting up elaborate electronic doors, CCTV cameras, and making the most efficient-yet-safe use of space as possible while trying to never have an escape or death, you can do so and find it a genuine challenge. Or, alternatively, you can turn failure conditions and events off, use old-school patrol-planning and little else, and even give  yourself unlimited funds.
And the prisoners behave in ways where you can act simply, or really think things through. At first blush, it seems so simple as to why a prisoner kills someone. But if you get informants and look at info, you'll notice that murders occur more often for pretty logical reasons: victim is an ex-cop or snitch... murderer has a violent reputation... murderer was dissatisfied with several of their needs (hygiene, nutrition, etc.). You can ignore all this and just beef up security in general and take 30 seconds just to re-route a patrol and add a guard, or you can form a protective-custody cell block that is more isolated and start putting snitches and other prime-targets in there away from the Max-security cons.
And you have the logistical tools to actually do all this... you can set individual schedules for each security-level, lay down specific patrol routes, assign certain blocks to be used only by certain groups of prisoners, and hire staff that conduct reform programs.
It's a lot of fun, and you can pick how you want to play. And in the mean time, you can go around clicking on prisoners to see what ridiculous things they did to end up in prison. Great fun.
-----------------------------------------------
BAD :
There *are* issues, however.
My main gripe is that too many toys are locked behind tech unlocks. Which at first sounds like SimCity, another game where the neat special buildings have to be unlocked and even then you have to wait a painful amount of time to build them (here, too, money comes in pretty slowly). But here the issue is worse, because I feel like really, *really* basic things are too expensive simply to unlock:
Why do I need to unlock being able to assign patrol routes?
Why do I need to unlock being able to take out a loan? (though grants do exist for building specific things)
Why do I need to unlock janitors and gardeners?
And as far as I know, even if I play with unlimited funds, I *still* have to manually unlock these things, which don't just unlock with the push of a button but take time. And, similarly, there's no option for insta-build... if I play with no failure conditions and unlimited funds, why not also allow me to build things instantly rather than having to hire 50 workers and wait for my mega-prison to be built over the course of real-life hours, hours that are added on to whatever time it took to actually lay out everything for them to build?
These are fairly minor issues in my opinion, and the Steam Workshop is a great place to go for some pre-built prisons, but doing that takes some of the fun out of building it yourself. Yet when building huge prisons, building it yourself takes you a while to give all the build orders, and then even longer to actually see the place be built. Which is fine when going for realism, but when I want a sandbox mode experience, it slows things up.
Really, this game needs a full-out sandbox mode where I can build instantly, rather than just a couple of options that sort of approximate a sand-box mode.
Again, not nearly a big enough issue to really hamper the fun for long, but does make it hard to experiment with designs numerous times unless you stay a bit smaller in scale.
---------------------------------
AND THE UGLY:
Tooltips and info are really, really sparse for this game. The info is all there, really, but sometimes it's in a place where you might not think to look, or is so briefly covered that a bit of clarification would have been helpful.
Right away, you assign reform programs, but it says no time is scheduled for them. But it doesn't say *why*. So you have to go to the scheduler (under Regieme) and hover over 'Work' to find out that reform programs don't have their own slot but occur during 'Work' time for anyone who isn't working. Which is already obscure, but what's worse is that you don't have an intuitive need for 'Work' time until you unlock 'Prison Labor'... so you might have already removed the default 'Work' time slot prior to deciding your unruly cons need some reform programs. It's a mess, and one that could easily be avoided if it said on the 'Programs' screen that your reform programs aren't scheduled because there is no 'Work' time slot (rather than just saying there's no time scheduled for them).
And similar issues, though not always to this scale, exist elsewhere. When a room needs furniture to function, the game tells you exactly what you need... but when the room fails to function because an escape tunnel entrance is in it (mostly in cells), it doesn't tell you this. Which is an issue because the tunnels can sometimes be partially underneath some other sprite in the game, usually a bit of debris a work left in the cell after not throwing out the dummy left in the bed,
It's an issue that goes away once you play a bit and learn the ropes, but it's an unnecessary learning curve that could be removed by including just a little more info here and there.
The other 'ugly' issue is that a few sprites are unclear as to what is forward and what is backward. TVs, Radios, and garbage bins look surprisingly the same whether looking at back or front. This isn't a graphics issue so much as it is a design issue... the TV screen looks like the TV's back CRT area. Just make the screen blue and white and keep the back part black. It's not an issue for too many objects,  but there are a few where just a slight change of color would distinguish the back from the front.
---------------------------------------
OVERALL:
It's part SimCity, part 'Tycoon', and part 'The Sims Go To Prison'. If you want your convict-sims to be able to kill each other daily, you can make it happen, and if you want a genuine challenge to keep them healthy and alive, you can make that happen, too.
If you're into any of the three games mentioned above, I'd recommend this.

Mad Max has a great deal of repetition, there is no doubt. Combat is repetitive and extremely easy - to the point where towards the end of the game I just started mashing my controller buttons like I did for Batman: AA. Bosses are equally all the same, with the only difference being one of colour and more health. The same attack formula ALWAYS works.
The world is beautifully created and exhibits atmosphere and mystery. Sadly this is let down the moment you realise that the huge map is split into 5 zones. Each zone has a large base structure, in which Max will be based once he can impress it's owner. In order to do that you need to improve said base by collecting 4-5 'Projects' that are scattered around the wasteland. Repeat this for all the other remaining bases and things quickly get repetitious.
In order to maintain and improve your car, you require SCRAP. This is dotted about the landscape and luckily in large amounts, so upgrading your car is nice and eas...no it's not. For some silly reason (See WB) all the upgrades are locked until you lower the threat rating in a respective zone by carrying out missions. In doing so induces a grind, in which you eventually max (hurrrr) out your car right at the end - when most of the zones are completely cleared! "Ah but you can simply select New Game+ and..." No you can't - there's nothing of the sort here.
So after 51hours I have finished the main mission, and have one minor side mission remaining, that needs to be performed at night. Only problem is, the sense of time progression ingame is very odd and you cannot fast forward time apart from via the main story missions that are now finished. So I'm out of luck there and no time fast forward mechanic seems to exist looking at various forums/reddit.
After all that has been said, one would think I wouldn't recommend Max Payne er Mad Max even. However there are a lot of positives
- Gorgeously created world
- The ingame engine runs superbly with great sound/storm effects too!
- Excellent story (takes place post Mad Max: Fury Road)
- Driving/Combat is excellent. Convoy battles are sadly very limited in quantity but great fun.
- Great characters
- You get a DOG
- Engine upgrades are meaty sounding!
Whilst I initially struggled with the game early on in, things do level out towards the end (a bit late if you ask me) and the story kicks into gear too. It is a shame we will never see any updates to the game as a New Game+ mode would be most welcome. If you enjoyed watching Mad Max: Fury Road, you will positively LOVE this.

While this game might seem like a normal military fps, it isn't. This is another game made by 2K
. It's interesting to note how many of the games are made by 2k when we asked the various gaming groups to nominate games with the best story. This particular one entitled 'Spec Ops: The line' is actually the 8th one in this particular series though it shares nothing in common with its former installments of the games with the same namesake.
(Spoiler Alert)
The story basically follows a soldiers personal journey through limbo. You take control of a captain Walker who is in charge of a 2 man delta squad. The three of them are on a rescue mission to find the 33rd battalion and their captain Konrad who is someone considered to be of noble rank since he saved your life in a previous battle.
Dubai has become somewhat apocalyptic thanks to huge never ending sandstorms requiring that the whole city to be evacuated. The politicians and the elite downplayed the situation while at the same time evacuating it themselves in secret leaving countless thousands of refugees behind. The 33rd battalion coming home from a war in Afghanistan volunteered their services to help with the relief efforts.
The United States government however ordered the 33rd to abandon the city and its refugees, but the 33rd led by Captain Konrad ignored the command and insisted upon their wishes of leading a caravan of 1,000 people out of the city. However the sandstorms grew worse and the caravan promised never arrived at the proposed time given. Future communication and travelling was severed and the 33rd was publicly disavowed for treason.
After significant time a looped radio signal could be heard coming from the city again. It was a brief one from Captain Konrad. It basically stated that the attempted evacuation was a complete failure and the death toll was too many. The US military then decide to send a covert 3 man delta team in to locate any survivors and then radio for extraction.
Problem is as you guide this 3 man crew into Dubai, things begin to seriously not add up. The refugees are trying to kill you, the 33rd battalion wants to kill you and so does the CIA operatives. As you begin to hallucinate voices and visions, you also begin to witness some atrocities that each splintering faction of the city has done to each other. The game unfortunately forces you to make some of those atrocities yourself in order to push on and find answers and hopefully in the vain attempt to nobly save someone. Somewhere at the end of the game you will be haunted by the dead faces of those that you have killed asking you why you committed such acts and for what purpose? Eventually you will realize that your character is suffering with severe effects of PTSD.
There are 18 campaign chapters to play through with a somewhat highly decorated abstract version of Dubai buried in the sand. These chapters are spasmodically broken up with several morale choices placed throughout the game. The importance of these morale choices and the effects they will have on the game are purely there for illusion. None of your choices will really matter. No matter what you choose or how you go about things your character will be haunted by the people he has killed. There is no pleasant way out of this. The game literally forces you to make a decision which unknowingly at the time will kill thousands. It will then show you the consequence of that decision regardless of the fact that you had no choice about it and it will ask you why did you do it?
Here's where the nobility of the story fails immensely and does not have the same power or punch to a story where your choice really does matter. Any morale judgments are quickly dismissed under a rigged gaming framework. While it does get you to think about things and it has moved and inspired countless people to think about the consequence of actions, I personally think it could have been delivered better to make more of an impact on gamer's than what it already has.
Definitely worth a look...
